documents.title: Company overview
documents.summary: Conduit builds AI agents and a shared workspace for hospitality guest operations: answering messages and calls, coordinating handoffs, and connecting the stay journey to property systems. This overview explains its product system, commercial model, customer situations and market position, with source disagreements kept visible where they affect a claim.
documents.markdown:
# Company overview

## Business at a glance

Conduit presents itself as an AI-agent platform for hospitality: on-brand agents that answer guest messages and calls, take action in connected systems, and coordinate work with human teams. The live product lineup on the marketing site is Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows, with Operations labeled coming soon. Industries called out on the same pages are short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups. Copyright on the site is “© 2026 Conduit AI.” The site prominently uses “Book demo” and “Get Started” calls to action; these captures do not establish an unattended self-serve checkout. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/)

The company page states the same positioning in one sentence: a fleet of agents that handles the guest journey across channels, converts inquiries, drives upsells, runs internal operations, and surfaces insights, connected to systems operators already use. That is a company promise, not independently audited performance. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/company)

Public identity facts do not line up. Treat the table as a source map, not a reconciled corporate record.

| Attribute | What a source says | Tension |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brand and operating entity | Conduit / Conduit AI; the privacy notice identifies HostAI Labs, Inc. dba Conduit | [Privacy notice](https://www.conduit.ai/privacy), updated 2 December 2025; this is a company disclosure, not a registry check |
| Prior name | HostAI (PitchBook; PhocusWire, 11 Apr 2025) | HostAI still appears in older YC launch copy |
| Founded | PitchBook 2023; YC and LinkedIn 2024 | Unresolved |
| HQ | San Francisco; PitchBook 230 California St, Suite 303 | Third-party location listing; confirm current business address if needed |
| Scale claim | Homepage and manifesto: 300+ brands, 120+ countries | YC and LinkedIn: “over 1000+” brands, 120+ countries |
| Headcount | YC team size 15; PitchBook 30 employees; LinkedIn 51–200 and “26 employees” | Unresolved |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai) [Source](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/548975-44) [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/company/useconduitai/)

Security language on the homepage is company-reported: SOC 2 Type II, encryption, RBAC, PII protection, audit logs, SSO, and “Supports HIPAA workflows.” Do not treat those as third-party attestations from this corpus. G2 is cited as 4.7 / 5 on the site. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/)

## Origin and evolution

Active founders listed by Y Combinator are Cole Rubin (Founder/CEO, real estate & tech) and Punn Kam (Founder/CTO, ex-Google). YC batch is Winter 2024, location San Francisco, status Active, primary partner Pete Koomen. A prior Launch YC post under HostAI described an all-in-one vacation-rental “operating system” (guest communication, payroll, maintenance, loyalty, IoT). That earlier surface area is not the current homepage catalog; whether payroll or loyalty still ship is unknown from these passages. [Source](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai) [Source](https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/KTc-hostai-the-operating-system-for-vacation-rentals)

PhocusWire (11 April 2025) reports the rename and a $3.1M seed: HostAI became Conduit after starting as automated STR guest messaging and once calling itself “Shopify for Travel.” Rubin is quoted that chaotic STR stacks and missing integrations pushed the company to build workarounds, then a broader AI operations layer for conversation-driven real estate (leasing, retention, maintenance, scheduling). Pi Labs led the round, with YC (Pete Koomen), a16z Scout, Jawed Karim, and Aaron King named as participants in investor commentary. PitchBook’s preview lists a 14 Dec 2023 accelerator at $500K, a May 2024 seed, the 10 Apr 2025 $3.1M seed, ~$3.6M raised to date, and “Formerly Known As HostAI.” Company pages also name YCombinator, PILABS, Unpopular Ventures, Transpose Platform, and yventures. [Source](https://www.phocuswire.com/hostai-conduit-strs-artificial-intelligence-investment) [Source](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/548975-44) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/company)

A LinkedIn post attributed to Punn Kam says the Conduit name came from exposed conduit on the ceiling of the founders’ first San Francisco apartment. That is founder storytelling, not a filing. [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/company/useconduitai/)

## What Conduit sells

Observed product architecture on the homepage, not a complete technical spec:

| Layer | Stated job | Complements / replaces in customer stories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agents | Chat across email, WhatsApp, OTAs, social; voice for calls; internal agents on existing tools | Failed AI vendors, night shifts, copy-paste support |
| Inbox | Messages, calls, and team handoffs in one place | Split OTA/WhatsApp/Intercom/Hostaway inboxes |
| Portals | Upsell offers, guidebook, AI concierge; LinkedIn launch: check-in, ID, payments | Static upsell pages guests never open |
| Workflows | Check-in to follow-ups and routine tasks | Manual SOPs living in people’s heads |
| Operations | “Coming soon”: AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance, inspections | Not a current homepage SKU |

Supporting claims on the same page: multilingual replies, native integrations or custom connectors, inspectable agent activity, scheduled workflows, performance reporting (automation rate, response time, resolution, satisfaction), API & MCP. Procedures, escalation handling, and “access internal systems” are marketed as how agents are tailored. LinkedIn also announces Portals, an iOS app, device control (locks/thermostats/sensors), Expedia messaging, a Mews connection, a Claude connector, and internal agents for upsell/review analysis. Those posts are product marketing, not proof of every action in every PMS. See [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities), [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), and [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/company/useconduitai/)

The manifesto goes further: a coordination layer that answers guests, dispatches contractors, and can close a booking or push a refund. Company-reported manifesto metrics (50M+ conversations, $3B+ reservation value influenced, 87% autonomous resolution, 95% CSAT, sub-minute first reply, 140 languages) are not replicated on the homepage’s 300+ brand line and should stay attributed. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto)

## Who it serves

Conduit’s own industry nav is three buckets: short-term rentals, independent hotels, hotel groups. FAQ copy on customer pages says it is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers. YC and PhocusWire still frame a wider housing/real-estate conversation layer (leasing, renewals). LinkedIn specialties include apartments. Do not collapse those into one ICP without a discovery call. Segment detail lives in [ICP strategy & segment priorities](#knowledge/ideal-customers), [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels), and [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

Named customer stories in this corpus are mostly professional STR/villa/aparthotel operators plus at least one boutique hotel. Examples: Haven (~270 Smokies STRs), HomeHop (Cleveland/Akron, 40→108 listings), Cascadia Getaways (Oregon, acquisition integration), Canbnb (Canberra, 7→170 properties), Bocobay (Aruba/Curaçao luxury PM), Cosmica (Italy and Dubai), Wynwood House (seven countries), The Flex / Flex Living (London, SF, Dubai), Bali Luxury Stays / Easy BnB exit narrative, The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel. That is observed published proof, not a census of the book. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

## Business model

Conduit sells recurring software packages with monthly credits. The public pricing page lists starting rates of $18 per unit per month for Messaging, $30 for Guest, $36 for Guest + Devices and $48 for Full Suite. Included credits rise from 40 to 100 per unit per month across those tiers. A separate Startup offer is explicitly labeled for 0–25 units at $899 per month with 2,000 credits and no implementation fee. Package eligibility, the definition of a billable unit, credit consumption and any additional usage charges must be established for a real quote; a seller should not apply a per-unit headline rate to a small portfolio without checking the Startup rules. [Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

These packages combine capabilities: Messaging includes Inbox, Voice AI, PMS/OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, escalation and reporting; higher packages add portals, payments, devices and operational functions. They are not separately published licenses for each product guide. The site lists operational functions in Full Suite while its navigation marks Operations as coming soon. Confirm the exact feature and release availability in a proposal, rather than claiming the entire category is either fully shipped or unavailable. See [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) and [Operator & internal AI availability](#knowledge/product-operator). [Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

The company uses demo and Get Started calls to action and a separate affiliate channel. Customer stories can explain economic motivation, but a customer's support-cost saving is not Conduit's subscription revenue or list price. Public evidence does not establish realized ACV, retention, total revenue or payback for a new customer. [Commercial model & market context](#knowledge/commercial-model) separates those questions from the published rate card.

## Market position

The site maintains a “Conduit vs.” list spanning hospitality messaging (Canary, Akia, Revinate, Duve, Volara, Enso Connect, Besty AI, HiJiffy, Quicktext) and general desks (Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, Intercom). That is positioning, not a win/loss study. Observed displacement in stories: Bocobay left Intercom for a hospitality-shaped inbox; Lauderdale replaced Jurny PMS/call center and other call services; HomeHop replaced a failed AI vendor and Google Voice; Flex Living kept building its own PMS but refused to rebuild conversational AI and compared Conduit favorably to Front, Zendesk, and Trengo. Competitive framing for sellers is in [Alternatives & differentiation](#knowledge/alternatives) and [Positioning & brand promise](#knowledge/brand-messaging). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex)

## Customer evidence

Company-wide “300+” / “1000+” claims are marketing. Usable proof is named and attributed. Outcomes below are what Conduit’s customer pages say those operators reported—not a benchmark every account will hit. More cases: [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

| Account | Fit snapshot | Attributed result (company story) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Haven Vacation Rentals | ~270 STRs; customer since Feb 2024 | 40%→90% automation; support need from ~25 people to two per shift; quality scores held | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) |
| The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel | Boutique hotel; since Dec 2024 | Support $4,000→$600/mo; response 57 min→2 min; story claims ≥$3,400/mo NOI and >$500k modeled asset value at an 8% cap; it also describes staffed support, so the software-only contribution is unresolved | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel) |
| HomeHop | 40→108 listings; since Jun 2025 on the page | ~70% automation; no added guest-support hires; overnight voice 1–7 AM | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) |
| Cascadia Getaways | ~100 properties, then acquisition | 60% automation; 4.9 communication score; 150 properties per support rep on shift | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) |
| Wynwood House | Seven countries; since Oct 2025 | Resolution 14–15 min→3 min; unified inbox vs Guesty + ChatGPT + sheets | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house) |
| Easy BnB (story published as Bali Luxury Stays) | Exit-oriented PM; Bali is the founder’s subsequent venture | ~$22k/mo labor savings; 75 units added; ~80–85% messaging automation | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays) |
| Canbnb | 170+ STRs; since Mar 2024 | ~1,500 messages/week, 60% AI; the historical customer setup quote uses “HostAI”; this does not describe today’s onboarding UI | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) |
| Cosmica | Italy + Dubai; late 2025 | No outsourced VAs for guest support; Dubai upsells “up to 5%” of revenue | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cosmica) |
| The Flex | Multi-city rentals; since Dec 2023 | CEO assessment: 70% CS automation is “very realistic,” not an independently measured result; 17 tools in the prior stack. The story’s 90% hero and 70%+ results copy differ | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) |

Internal contradictions to preserve: HomeHop’s page says “USING CONDUIT SINCE: June 2025” and also “approximately two years”; Bali Luxury Stays is “FOUNDED: 2025” and “USING CONDUIT SINCE: December 2024.” Use quotes with dates, not blended timelines.

## Commercial implications

Lead with a hospitality operations problem (after-hours volume, split OTA/WhatsApp/voice inboxes, VA/call-center cost, growth without linear headcount), not a generic “AI platform” pitch. Proof that lands is named STR and boutique-hotel work: automation rates, response time, night coverage, and in a few cases NOI or exit math. Do not promise 90% automation, $500k valuation lift, or 1000+ logos; those are specific stories or conflicting claims.

Qualify the actual hospitality operating model and guest-communication workload, including the marketed hotel/rental segments and FAQ serviced apartments; resorts, villas and aparthotels are not excluded merely because the navigation groups them differently. Establish willingness to maintain property knowledge and procedures (Haven, Cascadia, HomeHop, Flex all describe documentation as the real implementation). Ask what system Conduit would sit beside (PMS, channel manager, Intercom/Zendesk, call center). Resolve availability at the specific feature level: devices and operational functions appear in the public packages, Operations is marked coming soon in navigation, and broader leasing/housing language comes from historical sources. Do not treat those as one uniform availability claim. [Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Pricing must be pulled from [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) or a live quote. For messaging and voice, stay inside [Brand voice & language](#knowledge/brand-voice) and [Audience-to-message map](#knowledge/message-map); do not invent a relationship with a prospect.

documents.title: Commercial model & market context
documents.summary: Conduit publishes per-unit monthly packages with included credits, a small-portfolio Startup bundle, and sales-assisted mapping for larger use cases; list rates are starting prices, not reported revenue. Value is framed as hospitality AI agents that convert guest conversations into bookings, upsells, and coordinated work, presented through Book demo, Get Started and Talk to Sales calls to action; self-serve checkout is not established, with affiliate referral as a partner route rather than a product.
documents.markdown:
Conduit sells a hospitality AI platform, not a standalone chat model. Public pages describe on-brand agents that handle guest journeys across channels, convert inquiries into bookings, drive upsells, and connect to systems operators already use ([Company](https://www.conduit.ai/company)). [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) is the detailed rate card; this note covers how that packaging sits in the market and what is still unpublished.

## How value is created

The published commercial idea is simple: guest communication is the operation, and an agent that already holds reservation and property context can answer, act, and hand off instead of adding another inbox. Industry pages position the same core for short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups—after-hours coverage, omnichannel inbox, extras and upgrades, and PMS-connected work ([Independent hotels](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels); [Short-term rentals](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals); [Hotel groups](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)). Product surfaces that carry that value include [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), and [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). Operations (AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance, inspections) is labeled coming soon on the company site, while the pricing page lists tasks, workforce and operational workflows in Full Suite; the exact release and quoted feature availability need reconciliation ([Company](https://www.conduit.ai/company)).

Company-authored proof on the manifesto and build-vs-buy pages should be treated as Conduit’s own scoreboard, not third-party audit: more than 50M conversations handled, over $3B reservation value influenced, 87% of guest messages resolved autonomously, 95% guest CSAT, median first response under a minute, and a customer base described as past 300 hospitality brands in 120+ countries and 140 languages ([Manifesto](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto); [Build vs. Buy](https://www.conduit.ai/build-vs-buy)). Those figures are not the same as billed revenue or average contract value.

Credits sit next to the subscription. Each published package includes a monthly credit allotment per unit (or a flat 2,000 credits on Startup). The rate card gives included credits; the documentation explains consumption for voice, Operator, internal agents and paid workflow actions, while inbox AI replies use no credits. Included credits reset monthly. Dollar overage rates and contractual treatment of unused credits still need confirmation. [Credit guide](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits) [Detailed pricing guide](#knowledge/pricing)

## How the offer is sold

The site sells from independent teams to enterprise and asks buyers to talk to an AI expert to map plans to a use case. Starting rates are shown; pricing is said to scale beyond 50 listings ([Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)).

| Package | Starting list rate | Included credits | Buy motion on page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Messaging | $18 / unit / mo | 40 / unit / mo | Get Started |
| Guest | $30 / unit / mo | 60 / unit / mo | Get Started |
| Guest + Devices | $36 / unit / mo | 80 / unit / mo | Get Started |
| Full Suite | $48 / unit / mo | 100 / unit / mo | Talk to Sales |
| Startup (0–25 units) | $899 / mo | 2,000 / mo | Get Started; no implementation fee claimed |

Messaging is the unified-inbox and voice layer; Guest adds portals, waivers, and one-click upsell payments; Guest + Devices adds locks, thermostats, and sensors; Full Suite adds tasks, workforce, scheduling, dispatch, and inventory ([Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)). FAQ copy says Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers—not a free product ([Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)).

Y Combinator lists Account Executive and Sales Development Representative roles in San Francisco, which is consistent with a demo-led motion alongside “Get Started” ([Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai)). Contract length, discounting, seat vs. unit definitions for hotels, and whether “unit” equals listing, room, or door are not published.

## Routes to market

Primary demand capture is the public site: Book demo / Get Started, industry landing pages, comparison pages, and a [Build vs Buy](#knowledge/alternatives) argument aimed at operators considering in-house agents. The [Affiliate Program](https://www.conduit.ai/affiliate) is a partner channel, not a SKU. Anyone can submit a referral; Conduit’s team runs outreach, demo, and go-live. Referral partners earn a flat $500, paid 30 days after the referred business becomes a customer. An invite-only Ambassador tier is described as 5% of ARR for 12 months, $10,000 max per deal, monthly while the account is active, with a $25,000 quarterly cap that the page calls negotiable ([Affiliate Program](https://www.conduit.ai/affiliate)).

Investor and accelerator presence (Y Combinator Winter 2024; company page also lists Pi Labs, Unpopular Ventures, Transpose Platform, yventures) is backing, not a GTM product ([Company](https://www.conduit.ai/company); [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai)).

## Market and alternatives

Conduit’s own footer frames two competitor sets: hospitality messaging/guest-experience vendors (Canary, Akia, Revinate, Duve, Volara, Enso Connect, Besty AI, HiJiffy, Quicktext) and general service desks (Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, Intercom) ([Company](https://www.conduit.ai/company)). Build-vs-buy copy contrasts Conduit with in-house engineering (claimed days vs. 6+ months and 3–5 engineers), VA teams or spreadsheets, and ChatGPT or Claude plus Zapier. Those are Conduit’s positioning claims; they are not independent win/loss data. See [Alternatives & differentiation](#knowledge/alternatives) for a fuller map.

Identity notes that affect how the company is researched: PitchBook lists the business as formerly HostAI, founded 2023, private, seed, San Francisco; Y Combinator lists Conduit, founded 2024, Winter 2024, team size 15 ([PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/548975-44); [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai)). An earlier HostAI launch described an all-in-one vacation-rental OS; current commercial packaging is the Conduit hospitality agent platform ([HostAI launch](https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/KTc-hostai-the-operating-system-for-vacation-rentals)).

## Buying economics

List prices scale with units and package depth. The page provides a separate Startup package for 0–25 units at $899/month with 2,000 credits and no implementation fee. Do not present a small-portfolio quote by multiplying the lower headline per-unit rate: eligibility and Startup package rules must be confirmed. Beyond 50 listings, the page only says pricing scales—no published curve.

Do not treat those starting rates as realized ACV, net revenue, or a customer’s all-in bill. PitchBook’s public preview redacts current revenue while stating $3.6M raised to date, including a $500K accelerator (14 Dec 2023) and a $3.1M seed (10 Apr 2025) ([PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/548975-44)). Credit overages, telephony/SMS pass-through, implementation for non-Startup deals, and multi-year terms are unknown from these sources.

Customer-count language also diverges: Y Combinator and LinkedIn say trusted by over 1000+ global hospitality brands across 120+ countries; industry pages and the manifesto say 300+ brands ([Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai); [Independent hotels](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels); [Manifesto](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto)). Use both as company statements until reconciled. Named operator quotes on pricing (Cascadia Getaways, Cosmica, Haven, Renjoy) illustrate why some teams buy—workload, automation, custom workflows—but are not financial outcomes ([Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)). Named case metrics live in [Customer evidence](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

Headcount signals are similarly inconsistent (YC team size 15; PitchBook 30 employees; LinkedIn company size 51–200 and “Discover all 26 employees”). Treat them as snapshots from different directories, not a staffing model ([Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conduit-ai); [PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/548975-44); [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/useconduitai/)).

## Questions for the company

Ask sales or finance to map unit definition, credit burn, overage, implementation, and which package actually matches the stack (messaging-only vs. portals vs. devices vs. Full Suite). Confirm whether Operations “coming soon” is in the quote. For partner-sourced deals, confirm Referral vs. Ambassador economics before promising payouts. Reconcile 300+ vs. 1000+ brand counts if the figure will be used externally. None of the public pages publish realized revenue, logo-level ACV, or a guaranteed payback period—do not invent one for [ICP strategy](#knowledge/ideal-customers) or campaigns.
open_questions: What is a billed ‘unit’ for hotels versus STR listings, and how does the unpublished scale curve work past 50 listings?
What does one credit buy, do unused credits roll, and what is the overage or telephony/SMS pass-through rate?
What contract term, implementation fees (outside Startup), and discounting apply to Full Suite / enterprise quotes?
Which customer-count figure (300+ vs 1000+) and founding year (2023 vs 2024) should be used as the current company statement?
What share of bookings is self-serve Get Started versus demo-led sales, and what is realized revenue versus list price?

documents.title: Product catalog & capability map
documents.summary: Conduit’s public site currently names four primary products—Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows—with Operations marked coming soon, while commercial packages bundle those surfaces rather than selling them as one-to-one SKUs. Operator, REST/MCP access, integrations, and the affiliate listing are supporting capabilities, not additional catalog products, and several packaging and availability details remain unresolved against the v3 docs.
documents.markdown:
## Product system

Conduit’s current website catalog is a four-product hospitality stack, not a long list of SKUs. The global product nav and footer name **Conduit Agents**, **Conduit Inbox**, **Conduit Portals**, and **Conduit Workflows**. A fifth nav item, **Operations**, is labeled coming soon for AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance, and inspections. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Those four names are the primary products. Other surfaces should not be treated as extra catalog products unless a source says they are sold that way:

- **Operator** is a workspace assistant for inspecting and editing agent configuration, and it also appears as a line inside the Messaging package, not as its own product page. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)
- **REST API and MCP** are a developer platform for workspace data and tools. Docs state both are available only on the **v3 plan** and may need support enablement. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/developers) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)
- **Integrations** are connections (the public directory lists 43 entries, including some marked coming soon). A logo is not proof of a specific write-back or messaging action. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)
- **Affiliate Program** appears in the site footer; the integrations page also carries reseller-style copy. Neither source defines a standalone product. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Docs describe a different internal model: Inbox as the conversation surface; Build surfaces (Agents, Knowledge, Skills, Tools, Operator, Sandbox) as the brain; Workflows as automations; Dashboards as metrics. That is how the system is assembled, not a second product list. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

Plan packaging is a third layer. Public rates are **Messaging** ($18 / unit / mo starting, 40 credits), **Guest** ($30, 60 credits), **Guest + Devices** ($36, 80 credits), **Full Suite** ($48, 100 credits), plus a **Startup** bundle for 0–25 units at $899 / mo with 2,000 credits. Starting rates are shown and pricing scales beyond 50 listings. A bundle price is not a standalone Agents or Portals price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

## Product and capability map

Buyer problems below are the problems each product page claims to address, not an inferred ICP.

| Product | Buyer problem (site language) | Workflow the page describes | Dependency | Linked guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Agents | Answer guest messages and calls, retrieve context, and take action; escalate when needed | Handle voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA threads; update bookings, collect payments, create tasks; review and backtest replies | Property information, reservation data, and supported connected tools | [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) |
| Inbox | Messages, calls, and team handoffs in one workspace | Organize by property or team; take over with conversation history; keep stay/booking context beside the thread | Connected channels; PMS/OTA context for booking details | [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) |
| Portals | One branded stay link for guidebook, upsells, payments, and AI concierge | Pre-arrival details and checks; extras with payment; in-portal questions using stay and property info | Stay/reservation context; Guest packaging on the public price page; optional smart-lock/device connections | [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) |
| Workflows | Automate the guest journey from check-in to follow-ups and routine tasks | Visual builder: PMS-dated messages, post-stay campaigns, conditional upgrades; webhooks or MCP to supported tools | Connected email/WhatsApp/OTA channels and booking signals | [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) |

Agents are described as answering with property information and reservation data, acting through connected tools (for example creating a task or updating a booking), and passing requests to the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Inbox is the operating surface: SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social, and connected OTA threads in one workspace, with handoffs that keep history. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)

Portals give guests one branded link (no app) to review stay details, complete pre-arrival and identity checks, sign agreements or waivers, pay fees or deposits, buy upgrades, access the property when requirements are complete, and ask the AI concierge. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals)

Workflows send guest messages, run follow-up campaigns, and offer add-ons such as early check-in, gap nights, and room upgrades; the operator chooses trigger, conditions, and actions. Docs also classify workflows as proactive, routing, and triage automations. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/types-of-workflows)

Industry and use-case URLs (Airbnb automation, after-hours receptionist, room upgrades, and similar) are marketing entry pages, not extra products. Comparison URLs (Canary, Zendesk, and others) are positioning pages, not capabilities. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

## How the products work together

The intended loop is: connect channels and PMS data → teach agents with knowledge, skills, tools, and rules → run conversations in Inbox → use Workflows for scheduled or conditional journeys → use Portals as the guest-facing stay surface → inspect configuration with Operator and measure in dashboards. Docs frame this as a Connect / Teach / Test / Deploy path from copilot toward autopilot. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

Inbox routing assigns new contacts to an inbox before workflow triggers fire, so automations should target the routed inbox, not Unmapped. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing)

PMS connections feed listing and reservation context. Docs say Conduit integrates with over 15 PMS systems, classify some as messaging PMS connections and others as reservation-data-only, and warn that mixing incompatible types can duplicate conversations. Opera Cloud, for example, is described as syncing property, reservation, and profile data without routing guest messaging through that integration. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera)

Developer access sits beside the four products: typed REST endpoints for workspaces, contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, knowledge, agents, skills, workflows, and devices; MCP exposes overlapping tools to clients such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and VS Code. Device tools in MCP require the Devices add-on. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/developers) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

## Availability and boundaries

**Generally marketed as available:** Agents, Inbox, Portals, Workflows; Messaging-package features listed as unified inbox, voice AI (inbound and outbound), PMS and OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, escalation, analytics. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

**Packaged, not separately priced on the public page:** Portals sit in **Guest** and above (“Everything in Messaging” plus in-portal AI concierge, guidebooks, damage waivers, upsells). Smart-home/device capabilities sit in **Guest + Devices**. Tasks, workforce, agentic operations workflows, scheduling/dispatch, and inventory sit in **Full Suite**. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

**Gated or enablement-required in docs:** API and MCP on the v3 plan, contact support to enable; MCP default 120 requests per minute per workspace, shared with REST. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

**Availability conflicts:** Operations is marked coming soon in navigation while Full Suite lists operational features. The integration directory labels Booking.com and VRBO coming soon, but industry pages and release notes describe OTA messaging paths. Confirm direct versus PMS-mediated connections and the exact enabled actions; do not promise or deny the complete workflow from one directory badge. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)

**Contradiction to preserve:** changelog entries already describe Operations tasks, schedules, workforce call reporting, and portal/device controls (for example 3.13–3.15 in September 2026), while the marketing nav still says Operations is coming soon. Treat nav copy as the catalog status and changelog as evidence that some operations surfaces already exist in-product. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/changelog)

**Do not infer:** that every listed integration supports the same agent actions; that HostAI-labeled Email/WhatsApp blurbs redefine the product name; that “most teams go live within a week” is a verified implementation SLA (docs claim, not customer-proofed here). [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

Commercial mapping, credit burn, and contract packaging belong in [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing). Connection depth belongs in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).

PMS visibility also depends on workspace industry configuration. The setup documentation uses STR/LTR in general instructions and STR/Hotel in a provider-specific passage. Confirm the selected PMS and workspace setting; this is implementation readiness, not a negative ICP rule. [PMS setup](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)

## Choosing the entry point

Lead with the **named product** that matches the job, then confirm **package** coverage:

- Omnichannel guest comms and human takeover → Inbox, usually with Agents; Messaging is the public starting package. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)
- 24/7 answers plus actions in connected tools → Agents (voice and messaging). VoiceAI numbers, schedules, and warm transfer are documented separately. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-voiceai-ai-number)
- Pre-arrival, waivers, deposits, upgrades, guidebook → Portals; public pricing places this at Guest and above. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals)
- Confirmations, check-in, win-back, rule-based upsells → Workflows; they also appear inside Messaging packaging. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)
- Custom systems, MCP clients, or code tools → [Developer platform & custom workflows](#knowledge/product-developers), after confirming v3/API entitlement.
- Internal configuration help → [Operator & internal AI availability](#knowledge/product-operator), not a fifth website product.

documents.html:
Product system

Conduit’s current website catalog is a four-product hospitality stack, not a long list of SKUs. The global product nav and footer name Conduit Agents, Conduit Inbox, Conduit Portals, and Conduit Workflows. A fifth nav item, Operations, is labeled coming soon for AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance, and inspections. Source

Those four names are the primary products. Other surfaces should not be treated as extra catalog products unless a source says they are sold that way:

  • Operator is a workspace assistant for inspecting and editing agent configuration, and it also appears as a line inside the Messaging package, not as its own product page. Source Source
  • REST API and MCP are a developer platform for workspace data and tools. Docs state both are available only on the v3 plan and may need support enablement. Source Source
  • Integrations are connections (the public directory lists 43 entries, including some marked coming soon). A logo is not proof of a specific write-back or messaging action. Source
  • Affiliate Program appears in the site footer; the integrations page also carries reseller-style copy. Neither source defines a standalone product. Source

Docs describe a different internal model: Inbox as the conversation surface; Build surfaces (Agents, Knowledge, Skills, Tools, Operator, Sandbox) as the brain; Workflows as automations; Dashboards as metrics. That is how the system is assembled, not a second product list. Source

Plan packaging is a third layer. Public rates are Messaging ($18 / unit / mo starting, 40 credits), Guest ($30, 60 credits), Guest + Devices ($36, 80 credits), Full Suite ($48, 100 credits), plus a Startup bundle for 0–25 units at $899 / mo with 2,000 credits. Starting rates are shown and pricing scales beyond 50 listings. A bundle price is not a standalone Agents or Portals price. Source

Product and capability map

Buyer problems below are the problems each product page claims to address, not an inferred ICP.

Product Buyer problem (site language) Workflow the page describes Dependency Linked guide
Agents Answer guest messages and calls, retrieve context, and take action; escalate when needed Handle voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA threads; update bookings, collect payments, create tasks; review and backtest replies Property information, reservation data, and supported connected tools AI Agents
Inbox Messages, calls, and team handoffs in one workspace Organize by property or team; take over with conversation history; keep stay/booking context beside the thread Connected channels; PMS/OTA context for booking details Inbox
Portals One branded stay link for guidebook, upsells, payments, and AI concierge Pre-arrival details and checks; extras with payment; in-portal questions using stay and property info Stay/reservation context; Guest packaging on the public price page; optional smart-lock/device connections Guest Portals
Workflows Automate the guest journey from check-in to follow-ups and routine tasks Visual builder: PMS-dated messages, post-stay campaigns, conditional upgrades; webhooks or MCP to supported tools Connected email/WhatsApp/OTA channels and booking signals Workflows

Agents are described as answering with property information and reservation data, acting through connected tools (for example creating a task or updating a booking), and passing requests to the team. Source

Inbox is the operating surface: SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social, and connected OTA threads in one workspace, with handoffs that keep history. Source

Portals give guests one branded link (no app) to review stay details, complete pre-arrival and identity checks, sign agreements or waivers, pay fees or deposits, buy upgrades, access the property when requirements are complete, and ask the AI concierge. Source

Workflows send guest messages, run follow-up campaigns, and offer add-ons such as early check-in, gap nights, and room upgrades; the operator chooses trigger, conditions, and actions. Docs also classify workflows as proactive, routing, and triage automations. Source Source

Industry and use-case URLs (Airbnb automation, after-hours receptionist, room upgrades, and similar) are marketing entry pages, not extra products. Comparison URLs (Canary, Zendesk, and others) are positioning pages, not capabilities. Source

How the products work together

The intended loop is: connect channels and PMS data → teach agents with knowledge, skills, tools, and rules → run conversations in Inbox → use Workflows for scheduled or conditional journeys → use Portals as the guest-facing stay surface → inspect configuration with Operator and measure in dashboards. Docs frame this as a Connect / Teach / Test / Deploy path from copilot toward autopilot. Source Source

Inbox routing assigns new contacts to an inbox before workflow triggers fire, so automations should target the routed inbox, not Unmapped. Source

PMS connections feed listing and reservation context. Docs say Conduit integrates with over 15 PMS systems, classify some as messaging PMS connections and others as reservation-data-only, and warn that mixing incompatible types can duplicate conversations. Opera Cloud, for example, is described as syncing property, reservation, and profile data without routing guest messaging through that integration. Source Source

Developer access sits beside the four products: typed REST endpoints for workspaces, contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, knowledge, agents, skills, workflows, and devices; MCP exposes overlapping tools to clients such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and VS Code. Device tools in MCP require the Devices add-on. Source Source

Availability and boundaries

Generally marketed as available: Agents, Inbox, Portals, Workflows; Messaging-package features listed as unified inbox, voice AI (inbound and outbound), PMS and OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, escalation, analytics. Source

Packaged, not separately priced on the public page: Portals sit in Guest and above (“Everything in Messaging” plus in-portal AI concierge, guidebooks, damage waivers, upsells). Smart-home/device capabilities sit in Guest + Devices. Tasks, workforce, agentic operations workflows, scheduling/dispatch, and inventory sit in Full Suite. Source

Gated or enablement-required in docs: API and MCP on the v3 plan, contact support to enable; MCP default 120 requests per minute per workspace, shared with REST. Source Source

Availability conflicts: Operations is marked coming soon in navigation while Full Suite lists operational features. The integration directory labels Booking.com and VRBO coming soon, but industry pages and release notes describe OTA messaging paths. Confirm direct versus PMS-mediated connections and the exact enabled actions; do not promise or deny the complete workflow from one directory badge. Source Source

Contradiction to preserve: changelog entries already describe Operations tasks, schedules, workforce call reporting, and portal/device controls (for example 3.13–3.15 in September 2026), while the marketing nav still says Operations is coming soon. Treat nav copy as the catalog status and changelog as evidence that some operations surfaces already exist in-product. Source

Do not infer: that every listed integration supports the same agent actions; that HostAI-labeled Email/WhatsApp blurbs redefine the product name; that “most teams go live within a week” is a verified implementation SLA (docs claim, not customer-proofed here). Source

Commercial mapping, credit burn, and contract packaging belong in Pricing & packaging. Connection depth belongs in Integrations & implementation readiness.

PMS visibility also depends on workspace industry configuration. The setup documentation uses STR/LTR in general instructions and STR/Hotel in a provider-specific passage. Confirm the selected PMS and workspace setting; this is implementation readiness, not a negative ICP rule. PMS setup

Choosing the entry point

Lead with the named product that matches the job, then confirm package coverage:

  • Omnichannel guest comms and human takeover → Inbox, usually with Agents; Messaging is the public starting package. Source
  • 24/7 answers plus actions in connected tools → Agents (voice and messaging). VoiceAI numbers, schedules, and warm transfer are documented separately. Source Source
  • Pre-arrival, waivers, deposits, upgrades, guidebook → Portals; public pricing places this at Guest and above. Source
  • Confirmations, check-in, win-back, rule-based upsells → Workflows; they also appear inside Messaging packaging. Source Source
  • Custom systems, MCP clients, or code tools → Developer platform & custom workflows, after confirming v3/API entitlement.
  • Internal configuration help → Operator & internal AI availability, not a fifth website product.

Startup is a published $899/month path for 0–25 units. Messaging, Guest and Guest + Devices show per-unit starting rates with Get Started; Full Suite has Talk to Sales. The site says pricing scales beyond 50 listings without publishing the curve. Confirm package eligibility rather than making 25 or 50 a universal sales-process gate. Source

documents.title: AI Agents
documents.summary: Conduit AI Agents answer guest messages and calls with property and reservation context, then take supported actions in connected tools and escalate when rules require a human. They are packaged inside hospitality plans rather than as a published standalone SKU, and reported automation outcomes depend on knowledge work, channel/PMS setup, and operator review.
documents.markdown:
## Overview

Conduit positions **Agents** as the product that answers guest messages and calls, retrieves property and reservation context, takes action in connected tools, and escalates to people when needed. The public product line treats Agents as distinct from [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), and [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows): Agents “answer guest messages and calls, and take action,” while Inbox is the handoff surface and Workflows automate journey and routine-task sequences. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

The company-defined agent is not a draft-only chatbot. Conduit’s FAQ states that an AI agent “answers guest messages and calls using your property information and reservation data,” can create a task or update a booking through connected tools, and can pass requests to the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Docs describe the same product as configurable workers: external (guest-facing), internal, and voice agents with persona, tool access, skills, behavior, triggers, and publish state, plus Knowledge, Skills, Tools, sandbox testing, and Operator for inspecting configuration. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

## Who it is for

Conduit says the company is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, and that its AI agents answer messages and calls, handle routine requests, and coordinate work with the team. Industry pages on the same site group short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

**Buyers** in published stories are operators and founders who need 24/7 coverage without linear headcount (portfolio growth, after-hours phones, acquisition integration). **Users** are guest-services staff who teach the agent, standardize answers, review gaps, and take escalations—Haven describes team members becoming “conversational engineers.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

This is a fit conversation when guest volume already hits phones, OTA inboxes, WhatsApp, and email, and when property policies and live reservation data exist (or can be documented). It is a weaker first product if the account only wants a shared inbox with no agent autonomy; start from [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) instead.

## Capabilities and limits

| Capability | What Conduit publishes | Bound to watch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omnichannel answer | Voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA messages with conversation history | Only connected channels; Booking.com and VRBO listed as coming soon on the integrations directory | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) |
| Property-specific answers | Uses property information and policies | Quality tracks what is in Knowledge / PMS-synced listings | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) |
| Actions | Check bookings, change reservations, collect payments, create tasks via supported integrations | Not every PMS connection is two-way messaging or write-back | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) |
| Rules and escalation | Procedures the agent follows; requests the team should handle | Humans remain in the loop by design | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) |
| Improve loop | Find gaps, review proposed fixes, test before guests see them | Changes are not live until reviewed/tested | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) |
| Voice | Voice agents for calls; VoiceAI numbers can run 24/7 or on a schedule, with static/dynamic/warm-transfer escalation | Bring-your-own Twilio SMS needs webhook, A2P 10DLC, and SMS enabled | [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-voiceai-ai-number) |

The complete product FAQ says resolution depends on the guest requests, knowledge base, integrations and escalation rules; track resolved conversations and human handoffs. It does not prescribe a universal automation percentage. Do not treat marketing “end to end” as a guaranteed resolution rate. Operations (“AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance and inspections”) is listed as coming soon and is not this product. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

## Workflows and use cases

**Before.** A night or weekend guest texts for a door code, then calls about parking. Staff hunt Drive/PMS tabs, copy-paste the same policy, and miss the phone. Volume rises with each listing. Haven described ~25 support people at peak across shifts before the automation push. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

**After (Agents).** The same thread lands with history. The agent retrieves listing policy and reservation context, answers the code/parking question, and—if the integration supports it—updates a booking, collects a payment, or opens a task. If the request is out of policy, it escalates. Operators inspect reasoning/sources in the conversation, teach the miss, and sandbox a fix before guests see it. HomeHop used voice AI for overnight coverage 1 AM–7 AM rather than staffing that window. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop)

**Limits of that loop.** The Flex’s CEO said that if the information was not there, the AI would not reply—and that misunderstanding delayed turning it on. Haven’s jump from ~40% to 90% automation required knowledge standardization, Slack “AI Avengers” review, and months of teaching, not a switch-flip. Workflows that notify cleaners or inject follow-ups are a related but separate product; see [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex)

Docs map a crawl: Level 0 copilot drafts, Level 1 the team teaches simple end-to-end conversations, Level 2 the agent takes actions. “Road to Autopilot” is Connect → Teach → Test → Deploy, not an implied day-one autopilot. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/the-5-levels-of-ai-automation)

## Integrations and setup

Agents do not magically “have Guesty.” Setup is: workspace → connect channels → connect PMS/data → configure the V3 agent (knowledge, skills, tools, triggers) → sandbox → publish. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)

**PMS route.** `Settings > Connections > PMS` → pick provider → authenticate → import listings; PMS-backed content appears under `Build > Knowledge`; auto-sync is scheduled from the Knowledge source menu. Conduit says it integrates with over 15 PMS systems to populate listing information. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)

Messaging path is the critical split: some PMS connections (e.g. Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, Beds24) send guest messages into Conduit; others (e.g. Opera Cloud, Mews, Cloudbeds, Apaleo) supply property/reservation data only—OTA messaging must be connected as auxiliary channels. Connecting the same OTA both through a messaging PMS and directly can duplicate conversations. If Airbnb is the primary PMS, another PMS cannot be added in that workspace. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)

Opera Cloud example: OHIP credentials sync property, reservation, and profile data so agents can ground answers; Conduit states Opera “does not route guest messaging through this integration.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera)

Airbnb is documented as two-way send/receive in Conduit plus reservation modifications—verify write actions per account, not from the logo wall. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/airbnb)

Voice: `Settings > Channels > Phone` → claim or route a VoiceAI number → configure agent voice, greeting, and escalation. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-voiceai-ai-number)

Full catalog and implementation caveats live in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).

## Pricing and packaging

There is **no published standalone Agents price**. Voice AI (inbound and outbound) is listed inside the **Messaging** package, starting at **$18 / unit / month** with **40 credits / unit / month**, alongside unified inbox, PMS/OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, and escalation. Starting rates are shown; pricing “scales beyond 50 listings.” Guest ($30/unit/month) adds the stay/portal layer; Guest + Devices ($36) adds devices; Full Suite ($48) lists workforce and operational features. Operations remains marked coming soon in navigation, so confirm the specific operational feature before promising availability. These are package rates, not a separate Agents license. A 0–25 unit Startup plan is **$899 / month** with **2,000 credits / month** and “no implementation fee.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

The credit guide says inbox AI replies use no credits, regular voice costs 1 credit/minute and AI voice costs 8 credits/minute. The workflow action guide separately lists Voice Agent Call at 6 credits/minute. Confirm the applicable call path and how these meters relate before quoting; do not silently substitute or add the rates. Dollar overage pricing remains unestablished. [Credit guide](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits) [Workflow usage](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage) Map the account on [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing).

## Differentiation

Attributed product claims, not guarantees:

- **Answer plus act**, not draft-only: property context, reservation data, and tool actions, with team escalation. Renjoy’s CTO, quoted on the pricing page: “We don’t want to just draft messages—we want real automation.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)
- **Inspectable worker model** (docs): reasoning and sources in-thread; users approve, edit, or teach inline; sandbox before deploy. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)
- **Hospitality channel + PMS split** rather than a generic helpdesk bot, including scheduled or 24/7 voice. The Flex’s CEO contrasted Conduit with Front, Zendesk, and Trengo as “flow bots” on AI—his opinion, not a bake-off. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex)

See [Alternatives & differentiation](#knowledge/alternatives) before using competitor names in outbound copy.

## Customer evidence

Company-published stories; not independently verified. Do not copy a portal, inbox, or whole-platform metric onto Agents unless the story is about AI answering/acting.

| Account | Agent-relevant report | Scope / date notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Haven Vacation Rentals | 90% automation across ~270 properties, from ~40%; support staffing need described as 25 people to two per shift; quality scores held ~4.8–4.9 | Using Conduit since February 2024; required teaching, workflows, and knowledge work—not Agents in isolation. Header “59%” Guest Favorite vs body “55%” | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) |
| Cascadia Getaways | 60% automation and 4.9 communication score across ~100 properties; AI on lockbox, parking, local recs; humans on empathy/escalation | Start date unresolved: header says December 2024; body describes a March deployment | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) |
| HomeHop | 70% automation; voice AI 1 AM–7 AM; portfolio 40→108 listings without added guest-support hires (company claim) | Using since June 2025 in the story header; body also says “approximately two years”—leave unresolved | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) |
| Canbnb | ~1,500 messages/week, 60% handled by AI | Mix of inbox structure and AI; since March 2024 | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) |
| The Flex | CEO describes 70% automation as “very realistic”; the hero also claims 90% | The hero and body differ, and 80–90% also appears as a future ambition. Do not use 90% as a verified outcome; using-since header says December 2023 | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) |

Lauderdale Boutique Hotel reports faster replies and lower support cost after replacing a call center with “Conduit’s AI-powered support platform **and** 24/7 staffed support team”—do not cite $500k asset value as an Agents-only outcome. Wynwood House’s “cannot tell the difference between an AI agent and a human agent” is a CX quote on reply quality inside a unified-inbox rollout. More proof: [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Sales discovery

1. Which channels must the agent own on week one (Airbnb/Hostaway messaging vs Opera/Mews data-only plus direct OTA/voice)?
2. Which requests may the agent execute (booking change, payment, task) versus escalate—named policies, not “most FAQs”?
3. Who will teach Knowledge/Skills weekly, and what is today’s after-hours phone path?
4. What automation rate and quality floor would you accept in the first 60 days (Haven held scores while climbing; Cascadia locked 4.9)?
5. Unit count and whether Messaging ($18/unit starting) vs Startup ($899/month) is the commercial path—credits included vs unknown overage?

**Next step:** book a demo that uses one live listing, one PMS connection type (messaging vs data-only), and a VoiceAI schedule, then sandbox the top three intents before any autopilot discussion.

HomeHop’s story header says using Conduit since June 2025 while the footer says approximately two years.
The Flex page reports both ~70% customer-service automation and 90% of guest communication automated.

Omnichannel answer Voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA messages with conversation history Only connected channels; Booking.com and VRBO listed as coming soon on the integrations directory Source
Property-specific answers Uses property information and policies Quality tracks what is in Knowledge / PMS-synced listings Source
Actions Check bookings, change reservations, collect payments, create tasks via supported integrations Not every PMS connection is two-way messaging or write-back Source
Rules and escalation Procedures the agent follows; requests the team should handle Humans remain in the loop by design Source
Improve loop Find gaps, review proposed fixes, test before guests see them Changes are not live until reviewed/tested Source
Voice Voice agents for calls; VoiceAI numbers can run 24/7 or on a schedule, with static/dynamic/warm-transfer escalation Bring-your-own Twilio SMS needs webhook, A2P 10DLC, and SMS enabled Source

The complete product FAQ says resolution depends on the guest requests, knowledge base, integrations and escalation rules; track resolved conversations and human handoffs. It does not prescribe a universal automation percentage. Do not treat marketing “end to end” as a guaranteed resolution rate. Operations (“AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance and inspections”) is listed as coming soon and is not this product. Source

Workflows and use cases

Before. A night or weekend guest texts for a door code, then calls about parking. Staff hunt Drive/PMS tabs, copy-paste the same policy, and miss the phone. Volume rises with each listing. Haven described ~25 support people at peak across shifts before the automation push. Source

After (Agents). The same thread lands with history. The agent retrieves listing policy and reservation context, answers the code/parking question, and—if the integration supports it—updates a booking, collects a payment, or opens a task. If the request is out of policy, it escalates. Operators inspect reasoning/sources in the conversation, teach the miss, and sandbox a fix before guests see it. HomeHop used voice AI for overnight coverage 1 AM–7 AM rather than staffing that window. Source

Limits of that loop. The Flex’s CEO said that if the information was not there, the AI would not reply—and that misunderstanding delayed turning it on. Haven’s jump from ~40% to 90% automation required knowledge standardization, Slack “AI Avengers” review, and months of teaching, not a switch-flip. Workflows that notify cleaners or inject follow-ups are a related but separate product; see Workflows. Source

Docs map a crawl: Level 0 copilot drafts, Level 1 the team teaches simple end-to-end conversations, Level 2 the agent takes actions. “Road to Autopilot” is Connect → Teach → Test → Deploy, not an implied day-one autopilot. Source

Integrations and setup

Agents do not magically “have Guesty.” Setup is: workspace → connect channels → connect PMS/data → configure the V3 agent (knowledge, skills, tools, triggers) → sandbox → publish. Source

PMS route. Settings > Connections > PMS → pick provider → authenticate → import listings; PMS-backed content appears under Build > Knowledge; auto-sync is scheduled from the Knowledge source menu. Conduit says it integrates with over 15 PMS systems to populate listing information. Source

Messaging path is the critical split: some PMS connections (e.g. Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, Beds24) send guest messages into Conduit; others (e.g. Opera Cloud, Mews, Cloudbeds, Apaleo) supply property/reservation data only—OTA messaging must be connected as auxiliary channels. Connecting the same OTA both through a messaging PMS and directly can duplicate conversations. If Airbnb is the primary PMS, another PMS cannot be added in that workspace. Source

Opera Cloud example: OHIP credentials sync property, reservation, and profile data so agents can ground answers; Conduit states Opera “does not route guest messaging through this integration.” Source

Airbnb is documented as two-way send/receive in Conduit plus reservation modifications—verify write actions per account, not from the logo wall. Source

Voice: Settings > Channels > Phone → claim or route a VoiceAI number → configure agent voice, greeting, and escalation. Source

Full catalog and implementation caveats live in Integrations & implementation readiness.

Pricing and packaging

There is no published standalone Agents price. Voice AI (inbound and outbound) is listed inside the Messaging package, starting at $18 / unit / month with 40 credits / unit / month, alongside unified inbox, PMS/OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, and escalation. Starting rates are shown; pricing “scales beyond 50 listings.” Guest ($30/unit/month) adds the stay/portal layer; Guest + Devices ($36) adds devices; Full Suite ($48) lists workforce and operational features. Operations remains marked coming soon in navigation, so confirm the specific operational feature before promising availability. These are package rates, not a separate Agents license. A 0–25 unit Startup plan is $899 / month with 2,000 credits / month and “no implementation fee.” Source

The credit guide says inbox AI replies use no credits, regular voice costs 1 credit/minute and AI voice costs 8 credits/minute. The workflow action guide separately lists Voice Agent Call at 6 credits/minute. Confirm the applicable call path and how these meters relate before quoting; do not silently substitute or add the rates. Dollar overage pricing remains unestablished. Credit guide Workflow usage Map the account on Pricing & packaging.

Differentiation

Attributed product claims, not guarantees:

  • Answer plus act, not draft-only: property context, reservation data, and tool actions, with team escalation. Renjoy’s CTO, quoted on the pricing page: “We don’t want to just draft messages—we want real automation.” Source
  • Inspectable worker model (docs): reasoning and sources in-thread; users approve, edit, or teach inline; sandbox before deploy. Source
  • Hospitality channel + PMS split rather than a generic helpdesk bot, including scheduled or 24/7 voice. The Flex’s CEO contrasted Conduit with Front, Zendesk, and Trengo as “flow bots” on AI—his opinion, not a bake-off. Source

See Alternatives & differentiation before using competitor names in outbound copy.

Customer evidence

Company-published stories; not independently verified. Do not copy a portal, inbox, or whole-platform metric onto Agents unless the story is about AI answering/acting.

Account Agent-relevant report Scope / date notes Source
Haven Vacation Rentals 90% automation across ~270 properties, from ~40%; support staffing need described as 25 people to two per shift; quality scores held ~4.8–4.9 Using Conduit since February 2024; required teaching, workflows, and knowledge work—not Agents in isolation. Header “59%” Guest Favorite vs body “55%” Source
Cascadia Getaways 60% automation and 4.9 communication score across ~100 properties; AI on lockbox, parking, local recs; humans on empathy/escalation Start date unresolved: header says December 2024; body describes a March deployment Source
HomeHop 70% automation; voice AI 1 AM–7 AM; portfolio 40→108 listings without added guest-support hires (company claim) Using since June 2025 in the story header; body also says “approximately two years”—leave unresolved Source
Canbnb ~1,500 messages/week, 60% handled by AI Mix of inbox structure and AI; since March 2024 Source
The Flex CEO describes 70% automation as “very realistic”; the hero also claims 90% The hero and body differ, and 80–90% also appears as a future ambition. Do not use 90% as a verified outcome; using-since header says December 2023 Source

Lauderdale Boutique Hotel reports faster replies and lower support cost after replacing a call center with “Conduit’s AI-powered support platform and 24/7 staffed support team”—do not cite $500k asset value as an Agents-only outcome. Wynwood House’s “cannot tell the difference between an AI agent and a human agent” is a CX quote on reply quality inside a unified-inbox rollout. More proof: Customer evidence & usable proof.

Sales discovery

  1. Which channels must the agent own on week one (Airbnb/Hostaway messaging vs Opera/Mews data-only plus direct OTA/voice)?
  2. Which requests may the agent execute (booking change, payment, task) versus escalate—named policies, not “most FAQs”?
  3. Who will teach Knowledge/Skills weekly, and what is today’s after-hours phone path?
  4. What automation rate and quality floor would you accept in the first 60 days (Haven held scores while climbing; Cascadia locked 4.9)?
  5. Unit count and whether Messaging ($18/unit starting) vs Startup ($899/month) is the commercial path—credits included vs unknown overage?

Next step: book a demo that uses one live listing, one PMS connection type (messaging vs data-only), and a VoiceAI schedule, then sandbox the top three intents before any autopilot discussion.
