documents.summary: Conduit Inbox is the unified workspace for guest messages, calls, and team handoffs, with property/team views, assignment, notes, and PMS/OTA booking context beside the thread. It is sold inside published Messaging packages rather than as a standalone SKU, and proof should stay on unification, routing, and handoff stories—not agent automation rates from unrelated case studies.
documents.markdown:
## Overview

Conduit Inbox is the workspace where messages and calls sit so a hospitality team can see a guest in one thread, assign work, and take over from AI when a person is needed. Product copy describes it as bringing messages and calls into one workspace while agents automate routine work end to end and humans step in with full history. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)

Site navigation lists Inbox separately from [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), and [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows): “Messages, calls and team handoffs in one place.” Docs still treat the inbox as the daily operating surface—unified threads per contact, with conversations flowing through Todo, Follow-Up, and Done, plus inline visibility into how an AI reply was produced. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

## Who it is for

Conduit’s own FAQ names hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers as the audience. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Buyers are usually the leader accountable for guest (and often owner) communication quality and staffing: guest-services, CX, or operations. Users are the people in the queue—shift agents, specialists, and managers who tag, note, assign, and take over. Canbnb split Guest, Owner, and Vendor inboxes so the right team owned the right thread. Bocobay moved guest and owner communication after running WhatsApp, a separate support inbox, and Hostaway in parallel. Those are examples of how teams use the workspace, not a requirement that every account needs three inboxes. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)

## Capabilities and limits

Capabilities below are those the Inbox product and inbox docs actually describe. Adjacent products (agents, workflows, portals) should not be sold as Inbox features.

| Area | What sources describe | Bound / unknown |
| Channels | SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social messages, and connected OTA threads in one workspace; docs also name voice, Airbnb, live-chat, Messenger, Instagram, widget, LINE, and Slack as routable channels | Booking.com and VRBO are listed as coming soon on the integrations directory |
| Team coordination | Tag teammates, internal notes, assign without switching tools; views by team or property; round-robin or custom assignment rules | Channel routing rules apply only to new, unmapped contacts |
| Handoffs | Agents pass requests with conversation history; humans can review the guest request and the agent’s replies before responding; inline approve, edit, or teach | The product FAQ “How much guest messaging can Conduit automate?” is unanswered in the supplied page text |
| Stay context | Stay history, booking details, and availability from connected PMS and OTA accounts next to the conversation | Opera Cloud syncs property/reservation/profile data but does not route guest messaging through that integration |
| Daily queue | Sort/filter and triage views; Todo / Follow-Up / Done | Contacts with no routing rule land in Unmapped and need a manual move |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing) [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera)

## Workflows and use cases

**Before/after (Wynwood House; customer story says using Conduit since October 2025).** Before Conduit, CX agents drafted in ChatGPT, messaged in Guesty, translated in separate tools, and scored sentiment in Google Sheets. Guests waited an average of 14–15 minutes for resolution, and shift handoffs meant rereading entire threads. After go-live, drafting, translation, sentiment, tagging, internal notes, follow-ups, and guest messaging were centralized in one inbox; agents used AI summaries and worked the solution. The same story reports resolution time down to 3 minutes from 15 while the company operated across seven countries. That is Conduit’s attributed outcome for consolidating communication—not an Inbox-only controlled experiment. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house)

**Channel collapse (Bocobay).** The co-founder described dual inboxes as painful (WhatsApp, a separate support inbox, Hostaway). Migration was sequenced: email, then WhatsApp, then phone, then live chat, so notes and tagging lived on one thread. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)

Inbox routing runs before [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) triggers, so automation must target the *routed* inbox, not Unmapped. Inbox does not replace PMS inventory, payments, or portal upsells in [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals).

## Integrations and setup

Setup is a connection path, not a logo wall:

1. Create the workspace, invite members, set roles under Settings > Members. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)
2. Connect channels you actually reply on (email, WhatsApp Business, business phone/SMS, widget, Airbnb, LINE, and others documented). [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)
3. Connect PMS at Settings > Connections > PMS so listings and reservations sync and contacts can be created from bookings. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)
4. Add Inbox Routing rules (Settings > Inbox Routing) by channel—SMS/WhatsApp/voice number, email account, Facebook page, Instagram account, widget, Slack, helpdesk—or new contacts stay Unmapped. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing)
5. Optional: Slack or Microsoft Teams for notifications rather than as the system of record.

PMS messaging class is a design constraint. Messaging PMS connections (including Beds24, Guesty, Hostaway, Hostfully, Hostify, Lodgify, OwnerRez, Resly, Smily) send guest messages into Conduit; keep OTA messaging through the PMS or the same conversation can arrive twice. Non-messaging PMS connections (including Apaleo, Cloudbeds, Escapia, Mews, Opera Cloud, RMS, Streamline, Track) supply property and reservation data only; OTA messaging needs a direct channel connection. Airbnb has its own primary-PMS vs additional-messaging rules. Guesty marketing copy says messaging from Guesty properties can centralize in one inbox; Opera Cloud marketing says existing hotel channels handle outbound contact. Those routes are not interchangeable. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/guesty) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera)

## Pricing and packaging

No standalone Inbox price is published. Unified inbox is listed inside the Messaging package. Starting rates are shown; the page says pricing scales beyond 50 listings and that plans should be mapped with an expert. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

| Package | Starting rate (published) | Credits | Inbox-relevant inclusions listed |
| Messaging | $18 / unit / mo | 40 / unit / mo | Unified inbox, every channel; Voice AI inbound and outbound; PMS and OTA integrations; Operator, workflows, escalation; analytics |
| Guest | $30 / unit / mo | 60 / unit / mo | Everything in Messaging plus portals |
| Guest + Devices | $36 / unit / mo | 80 / unit / mo | Everything in Guest plus devices |
| Full Suite | $48 / unit / mo | 100 / unit / mo | Talk to Sales; operations items listed |
| Startup, 0–25 units | $899 / mo | 2,000 / mo | Full feature set, no implementation fee |

Whether Inbox can be bought without Voice AI or workflows is not stated. Bundle price is not an Inbox-only price. See [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing).

## Differentiation

Attributed, not guaranteed:

- Product page: stay/booking/availability beside the thread, plus calls and OTA threads with team handoffs. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)
- Bocobay left Intercom; Nick Curtis is quoted that they needed guest, owner, and on-the-ground ops in one place, and that Conduit was “as good as anything we’ve used before, but finally tailored to hospitality.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)
- The Flex’s CEO said that on day one Conduit already looked ahead of Front, Zendesk, and Trengo, and that those tools still felt like “flow bots” on AI. That is one operator’s comparison, not a bake-off. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex)

Footer “Conduit vs.” names (Canary, Akia, Zendesk, Intercom, and others) are not win-rate evidence.

## Customer evidence

Use stories that describe the inbox workspace. Do not move Haven’s 90% automation or Lauderdale’s asset-value math onto this product.

- **Wynwood House** (since October 2025): unified inbox replaced a multi-tool CX stack; reported resolution 14–15 minutes → 3 minutes; AI handoff summaries. The 4.8 Airbnb rating in Colombia is in the same story, not isolated to Inbox. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house)
- **Bocobay** (since June 2024): explicit “one inbox, not two”; notes/tagging for handoffs; owner comms centralized. Hero “80% resolution rate” and “100s hours saved” are page metrics without a method that ties them solely to Inbox. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)
- **Canbnb** (since March 2024): structured inbox and dedicated Guest/Owner/Vendor queues after a 630-unread-message morning; Hostaway + WhatsApp + email + SMS + widget. “~1,500 messages per week, 60% handled by AI” mixes agent automation with inbox operations. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb)
- **The Flex** (since December 2023): named a unified inbox with phone and messaging, tagging, and call summaries. 70% / 90% automation figures in that story describe guest-support automation, not Inbox packaging. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex)

More proof patterns: [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Sales discovery

1. How many inboxes do agents open today (PMS, WhatsApp, email, OTA, phone, Intercom/Zendesk), and which threads duplicate?
2. Is the PMS in the *messaging* class (messages through the PMS) or *non-messaging* class (direct OTA/channel connects required)?
3. Who takes over from AI—by property, shift, or guest vs owner vs vendor—and is assignment round-robin or named?
4. What must sit next to the thread (reservation, availability, stay history), and which PMS/OTA actually syncs it?
5. At shift change, do agents reread full threads, or do they need notes/summaries?
6. After hours, must calls land in the same workspace as SMS/WhatsApp?

**Next step:** run a demo on one live guest across SMS or OTA *with* PMS context, then sketch routing so new contacts never sit in Unmapped. Map listing count to Messaging ($18/unit/mo starting, 40 credits) versus Startup ($899/mo, 0–25 units). Pair with [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).
open_questions: Can Inbox be purchased without Voice AI, Agents, or Workflows, or is it only available inside Messaging and higher packages?
What is the GA timing and supported action set for Booking.com and VRBO messaging, both listed as coming soon?
When should a team choose a contact inbox versus a ticket inbox? The docs index names the distinction but the supplied passages do not define it.
How are credits consumed for human-only inbox replies versus AI sends outside workflow actions?

documents.markdown:
## Overview

Guest Portals are Conduit’s stay-level guest experience surface: one branded link for arrival prep, access instructions, upgrades, payments, and in-portal questions. The product page frames it as “the full stay, upsells, and guest support in one link,” with no guest app to download. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md))

Portals sit beside [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) and [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox). Messaging answers guests in channels; Portals is the page a guest opens before and during a stay. Capabilities below are only those Conduit attributes to Portals, the Guest package, or the Portals API—not generic inbox automation.

## Who it is for

Public pages position Portals for hotels and vacation rentals. Company FAQ copy also lists hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers as Conduit’s audience; that is a company-level statement, not a Portals-only ICP. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals))

**Buyers** are commercial owners of guest experience and ancillary revenue: operators who want a branded guide, damage waivers without a SKU fee (Guest package language), in-stay extras, and fewer “where is the code?” threads. **Users** split three ways: guests who complete the link; ops or CX leads who own templates, offers, verification rules, and brand kit; and implementation or engineering staff who use Portals API/MCP tools when the add-on is enabled.

Do not invent urgency scores or “typical” portfolio sizes from this page. Fit is an account that already has reservation/listing context in Conduit and a reason to replace a PDF guide, third-party guidebook, or manual waiver/payment chase. See [ICP strategy](#knowledge/ideal-customers) for segment work elsewhere.

## Capabilities and limits

| Capability | What Conduit publishes | Stated limit or condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One stay link | Property details, dates, check-in steps, access instructions | No app required ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) |
| Pre-arrival | Stay details, identity checks, questions, agreements/waivers, fees/deposits | Access after required steps are complete ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) |
| Payments | Stripe: card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Link | Guest enters a method in-portal; not the original booking card ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) |
| Upsells | Browse extras and pay at checkout | Offers show only after a template layout references them ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/portals/overview.md)) |
| AI concierge | Property-aware answers from stay + property info | 24/7 / local recommendations claimed on the product page, not independently measured ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) |
| Smart access | Instructions, door codes, or lock controls after pre-arrival steps | Compatible integrations only; lock behavior varies; confirmed in implementation ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) |
| Branding | Layout, colors, theme, hero, guides, offers | Team can migrate an existing guide and build a sample before portfolio rollout ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) |

API configuration is modular: verification rules (deposits, agreements, arrival details, questions), offers (examples: late checkout, mid-stay clean, airport pickup), templates, guides, brand kit, and read-only sessions (progress, submitted fields, orders, tickets, assets). You can use verification rules without a template. Portal API methods require the **Portals add-on**; otherwise they return `403 Forbidden`. Reads need `Access Portals`; writes need `Manage Portals`. ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/portals/overview.md))

Unknown from these sources: which PMS fields write back, conversion rates, and whether every Guest-bundle customer also has the API add-on entitlement.

## Workflows and use cases

**Before.** A guest books on an OTA. The team emails a PDF guidebook, a waiver link, a separate payment request, and later a door code. Identity checks live in another tool. After-hours questions bounce to [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) or a phone tree. Upsells are ad hoc messages. Access is sent even if the waiver is unsigned.

**After (as published).** Conduit uses reservation, guest, listing, and booking-channel context so each portal is stay-specific. The guest opens one branded link, completes questions and identity checks, signs the rental agreement or damage waiver, pays required fees or deposits, buys upgrades, and only then receives access when requirements are complete. The in-portal concierge answers from stay details and property information. Email or SMS can still run alongside the portal. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md))

**Limits of that workflow.** Payment and verification rules can be tailored by booking channel, including excluding flows where an OTA’s policies require it. Guests do not reuse the booking card. Exact fields, write-back, smart-lock support, and payment rules vary by integration and are confirmed before launch. Lock compatibility is not a logo-level guarantee. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md))

Devices (separate add-on) can automatically generate a door code per reservation and publish it to the guest portal; that is a Devices capability that *lands in* Portals, not a Portals-only lock catalog. ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/devices/overview.md))

## Integrations and setup

Do not treat a PMS logo as proof the portal can collect deposits or issue codes. The published route is: connect PMS/OTA so reservation and listing context exist → connect Stripe for in-portal pay → confirm lock provider and property setup if access is in-portal → configure verification rules, offers, templates/guides, brand kit → optionally activate a template. Implementation can include moving content from a current guest guide and a sample portal before rollout. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md))

PMS connection itself is workspace-level (Settings → Connections → PMS, then Knowledge sync). Messaging vs non-messaging PMS rules affect inbox routing, not portal page composition; see [Integrations](#knowledge/integrations). Guest + Devices packaging adds portal-integrated smart devices and access codes; commercial access (cards, mobile keys, Instant Keys) is documented under Devices, not on the Portals FAQ. ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms))

Developers: MCP portal tools need the add-on plus the same Access/Manage Portals permissions; v3 API/MCP enablement is a support request, not a self-serve claim on the pricing page. ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview))

## Pricing and packaging

Public materials describe **two overlapping commercial shapes**. Preserve both; do not collapse them into one SKU.

| Shape | What is published | Units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Guest bundle | Starting **$30 / unit / month**, **60 credits / unit / month**; everything in Messaging plus in-portal AI concierge, rich-media guidebooks, damage waivers with no SKU fee, one-click upsell payments ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)) | Per unit / month; starting rates; scales beyond 50 listings ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)) |
| Portals add-on | Paid add-on by **contracted listing count**, graduated volume pricing; bundles and **guest-transaction terms** can change the final rate; sales quotes monthly or annual ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)) | Listings; exact rate unpublished |
| Guest + Devices | Starting **$36 / unit / month**, **80 credits**; portal-integrated smart devices and access codes ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)) | Per unit / month |
| Startup | **0–25 units**, **$899 / month**, **2,000 credits / month**, full feature set, no implementation fee ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)) | Workspace month |

Messaging starts at **$18 / unit / month** and **40 credits** and does **not** list portals. Full Suite starts at **$48 / unit / month** and **100 credits**. Starting rates; talk to sales to map a package. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md))

**Credits (workspace usage, not a Portals meter).** Included credits reset each monthly billing cycle. Conduit tracks four categories: workflow paid actions, Operator sidebar turns, internal agent activity, and Voice AI. **Inbox AI agent replies do not consume credits.** Regular voice is **1 credit per minute**; AI voice is **8 credits per minute**. Operator cost varies by model and tokens (roughly 7,000–71,000 billable tokens per credit depending on model). Internal agents have a dynamic cost. Workflow *runs* are free; credits apply when a successful run finishes a paid action. Low-credit path: notification, then upgrade or continue into **overage billed on the next invoice**. View usage under Settings → Billing. ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits))

A bundle price is not a standalone Portals price. Guest-transaction fees are acknowledged but not quantified here.

The [workflow action guide](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage) separately lists Voice Agent Call at **6 credits/minute**, while the general guide lists AI voice at **8** and regular voice at **1**. Confirm which meter applies to the actual call path and whether any usage overlaps; these sources do not justify silently substituting or adding the rates.

## Differentiation

Attributed product claims, not third-party proof: stay-scoped branded link instead of a generic guidebook app; AI concierge that uses *this stay’s* details; Stripe checkout in the same page as waivers and extras; optional lock controls after verification; Conduit-led content migration and a sample portal. Guest package copy highlights “Damage waivers, no SKU fee” and “Upsells with One-click Payment.” ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md))

Competitive pages list Duve, Enso Connect, Canary, and others as “Conduit vs.” destinations; those pages are not evidence that Portals matches a named rival feature-for-feature. For broader positioning see [Alternatives](#knowledge/alternatives).

## Customer evidence

The broader [customer evidence library](#knowledge/customer-evidence), which includes Haven, Cascadia, Lauderdale, Cosmica and Bali Luxury Stays, report inbox/agent automation, staffing, and messaging upsells. **None of those stories isolate Guest Portals**—no portal conversion, waiver completion, or in-portal GMV figures. Do not reuse 90% automation, $500k asset value, or Dubai “up to 5%” upsell as Portals outcomes. ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026))

Until a Portals-scoped case exists, proof for this product is the documented guest path, packaging, and API—not portfolio ROI. Track named portal customers as an open investigation: [Customer evidence](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Sales discovery

Ask only what decides Guest vs Messaging vs add-on and whether implementation can land:

1. What is the current guest guide (PDF, app, PMS message, third-party portal), and who owns content?
2. Which pre-arrival steps are mandatory before access: ID, waiver, deposit, house rules?
3. Stripe (or equivalent) already in use? Any OTA channels that must **exclude** in-portal pay?
4. Lock/access vendor and whether codes must appear only after verification?
5. PMS/channel: which reservation fields must appear, and is write-back required?
6. Ancillary catalog: SKU-fee pain on waivers, one-click extras, channel-specific offers?
7. Buyer of guest experience vs ops user who will maintain templates and offers?
8. Listing count for contracted Portals add-on vs Guest per-unit bundle, plus expected credit use (voice/Operator/workflows—not inbox replies)?

**Next practical step:** book a stack review that confirms PMS fields, Stripe, lock compatibility, and a sample portal—then quote either Guest ($30/unit starting) or the listing-count add-on, stating which contradiction applies to this account. Do not promise a rate Conduit has not priced. Map credits and overage using [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) and the credit guide, not Portals page rhetoric.
open_questions: For a given account, is Portals sold as the Guest per-unit bundle, a listing-count add-on, or both stacked, and what guest-transaction terms apply?
Which PMS/OTA integrations support which portal fields, payment rules, and write-back, and which lock models can show codes or controls after verification?
Are there customer stories that isolate portal completion, waiver, payment, or upsell outcomes rather than inbox/agent automation?

documents.title: Workflows
documents.summary: Conduit Workflows is a visual automation layer for hospitality guest journeys: scheduled messages, follow-ups, upgrades, routing, and triage built from triggers, conditions, and actions. It is packaged inside Messaging-and-up plans rather than as a published standalone SKU, and customer proof should stay tied to workflow-building stories rather than platform-wide automation rates.
documents.markdown:
## Overview

Conduit Workflows provides visual automations for proactive messages, routing and triage. Hospitality examples follow the stay journey, but triggers can also involve a new contact, a tag or an AI tool call; an existing booking is not a universal prerequisite. Agents supply the live reply behavior. Conduit describes it as automating that journey from check-in through follow-ups and routine tasks, with builders assembling confirmations, check-in instructions, follow-ups, and upgrades around the booking, the property, and the guest’s response. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)

In platform architecture, workflows are the “arms and legs”: proactive outreach, routing into systems or teammates, and triage that escalates then can auto-close. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work) Conversational answering still sits with [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) and the [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox). Workflows schedule, branch, wait, notify, and inject an agent when a defined event fires.

A concrete before/after: a support team copy-pastes door codes and check-in notes whenever a reservation appears. After a PMS-tied workflow, a reservation or stay-date trigger sends the confirmation and check-in sequence on connected email, WhatsApp, or OTA channels, branches on channel or a custom signal, waits until a send window, and only then injects an agent or pings Slack if the guest replies with a problem. Limits are real: the sequence only sends on connected channels, stay-date logic needs PMS/booking data, paid actions consume credits, and inbox routing is evaluated before workflow triggers. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing)

## Who it is for

Conduit positions the company for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Workflows is aimed at operators who already have a repeating guest calendar (confirm, instruct, upsell, follow up) and want those sequences designed once instead of typed per stay.

Buyer-role hypotheses include founders, revenue/guest-services leads and operations owners, informed by named stories rather than a required title map who care whether journey automation is included in a package and whether credits will cover outbound volume. Users are guest-services managers and the people Haven calls conversational engineers—staff who build and iterate workflows rather than answering every check-in question. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) Day-to-day agents still work exceptions in the inbox; they are consumers of routing and triage, not the primary authors.

## Capabilities and limits

Published Workflows capabilities on the product page:

| Capability | What Conduit states | Depends on | Not the same as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visual builder | Hospitality triggers and actions without writing each sequence from scratch | Workspace access to workflows | Custom code in the [developer platform](#knowledge/product-developers) |
| Connected send | Email, WhatsApp, and OTA channels already connected | Channel setup | Unconnected OTAs |
| Conditional steps | Branch by booking channel, loyalty status, or custom signals; webhooks or MCP for supported tools | Those signals existing in the workspace | Guaranteed write-back to every PMS |
| Scheduled guest messages | Confirmations, check-in instructions, checkout reminders from PMS events and booking dates | Connected PMS / booking dates | Housekeeping dispatch (Operations is listed as coming soon; it is separate from the Operator assistant) |
| Post-stay campaigns | Stay dates, properties, guest responses; return offers | Identity of past guests | A measured win-back rate |
| Rule-based upgrades | Early check-in, gap nights, private chefs, room upgrades from booking details and rules you set | Rules and booking fields you configure | [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) checkout UI |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)

Docs add the building blocks: triggers such as a new contact, a conversation tag, or an AI tool call; actions (templated reply, reassign, notify, wait, inject AI); conditions/paths; and variables such as `{{contact.first_name}}`. Action groups are Message, AI, Workspace, and Controls. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/getting-started)

Limits to keep explicit: workflow **runs** are free; credits apply only when a successful run finishes a priced action. Triggers, conditions, waits, contact updates, and labels cost nothing. Failed or cancelled runs use 0 credits even if earlier steps finished. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage) Routing rules run **before** workflow triggers, so triggers should target the routed inbox, not Unmapped. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing) REST and MCP workflow APIs are documented as v3-plan features, enabled via support—not as a default on every commercial package. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

## Workflows and use cases

Docs classify three types you can build from scratch or from a template:

| Type | Role | Doc examples | Hospitality reading (interpretation) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proactive | Scheduled or triggered outbound | Survey 24 hours after a ticket resolves; renewal reminder | Confirmations, check-in/out reminders, return offers |
| Routing | Alert team or guest when conditions match | SMS when an order ships; Slack on negative survey | Slack/email when an agent books something or a tag fires |
| Triage | Ask humans when the AI lacks an answer, then reply | Billing/engineering/inventory ping then guest update | Escalate a lockout or billing exception, then close |

[Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/types-of-workflows)

Product-page hospitality sequences to scope in a demo: booking confirmation → check-in instructions on stay dates → checkout reminder → post-stay return offer; and if/then upgrade offers (early check-in, gap nights, add-ons) using booking details. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) FAQ wording is the bound of what Conduit claims workflows automate: guest messages, follow-up campaigns, and add-ons such as early check-in, gap nights, and room upgrades, with the operator choosing trigger, conditions, and actions. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)

Haven’s reported dog-at-property example is a routing/ops adjacent flow: when a guest brings a dog to a defined set of properties, notify the cleaning company and push the information back—built in about an hour by the guest-services manager. That is a customer-built workflow, not a packaged template catalog. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

## Integrations and setup

Setup is not “pick a vendor logo.” Practical route:

1. Confirm that the workspace industry setting exposes the selected PMS; follow that provider’s setup instructions; connect PMS under Settings > Connections > PMS so listings and reservations sync and contacts can be created from bookings. Messaging vs non-messaging PMS paths differ: some PMS connections deliver guest messages; others supply property/reservation data only, with OTA messaging connected separately. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)
2. Connect the send channels the builder will use (email, WhatsApp, OTAs such as Airbnb). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)
3. Set inbox routing so new contacts land in the inbox your workflow trigger targets. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing)
4. Build in the visual editor (triggers, conditions, waits, sends, AI injection) or install workflow templates from the Marketplace. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)
5. Optional: webhooks or MCP for supported tools; programmatic list/create/update of workflows and execution logs on the v3 API/MCP. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

The public integrations directory is a catalog of 43 apps (PMS, messaging, CRM, task managers). A logo is not proof that a named action exists as a first-class workflow step. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations) HomeHop’s SuiteOP workflow comment is a customer stack, not a listed Conduit integration. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop)

## Pricing and packaging

There is **no published standalone Workflows price**. On the pricing page, workflows appear inside Messaging (“Operator, workflows, escalation”), which starts at **$18 / unit / month** with **40 credits / unit / month**. Starting rates are shown; pricing scales beyond 50 listings. Guest starts at $30/unit/month and adds portals, waivers and upsells. Guest + Devices starts at $36 and adds device management workflows. Full Suite starts at $48 and lists agentic operations workflows, tasks/workforce, scheduling/dispatch and inventory. Confirm exact availability because navigation still labels Operations as coming soon. None is a Workflows-only fee. A 0–25 unit Startup package is listed at **$899 / month** with 2,000 credits / month and no implementation fee. Talk-to-sales language applies as portfolio size grows. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Credit units that matter for this product (successful finished steps only):

| Action | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| Slack or Teams message | 1 |
| HTTP webhook | 0 |
| HubSpot / Salesforce / Airtable record step | 1 |
| Run AI Prompt / Web Search | 2 / 5 |
| Email send (non-AI / AI-generated) | 1 / 4 |
| SMS or WhatsApp (non-AI / AI-generated) | 2 / 5 |
| Other-channel outbound message (non-AI / AI-generated) | 0 / 3 |
| Voice Agent Call (workflow action) | 6 per minute |

[Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage)

Inbound messages use no credits. The general credit guide separately lists regular voice at 1/minute and AI voice at 8/minute, versus the workflow action table’s 6/minute; confirm the applicable meter for the actual call path. [Credit guide](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits) How far 40 credits per unit goes for a typical stay sequence is not published; model it from the table, not from package rhetoric. See [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing).

## Differentiation

Attributed to Conduit, not independently verified: a hospitality visual builder with booking/property/guest-response context, PMS-event scheduling, and branches on booking channel or loyalty—not a generic ticket macro tool. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) Platform docs further separate workflows from agents (execution vs conversation) and from dashboards. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

Customer-attributed, not a Conduit SLA: Haven’s CEO on staff being given operational problems and building the workflow themselves. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) Do not convert that into “all customers become engineers in an hour.”

Competitive pages on conduit.ai list other vendors; those lists are not Workflows feature matrices. Keep comparisons in [Alternatives & differentiation](#knowledge/alternatives).

## Customer evidence

Use only stories that mention workflows. Do not assign Haven’s 90% automation, staffing cuts, or other accounts’ message-automation rates to this SKU unless the narrative isolates Workflows.

**Haven Vacation Rentals** (STR, ~270 properties, Conduit since February 2024; company-reported 2026 update): they had listings in Conduit at about 40% automation **with no workflows** and little knowledge-base work. The later operating model includes team members building workflows and training AI; Jack Zoppa: “Give them these problems. They just went and built the workflow and figured it out.” The dog-notification workflow was built in about an hour. Haven was rebuilding Slack triage workflows and expanding use of Conduit’s workflow engine. Portfolio automation and headcount figures in that article describe the broader Conduit program, not a Workflows-only KPI. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

**HomeHop** (customer quote): Dan Mitchen said using AI in workflows with SuiteOP “is going to be an absolute game changer”—a forward-looking expectation, not a measured workflow result. Treat as their integration pattern, not a Conduit product metric. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop)

## Sales discovery

Ask what is still typed by hand on a clock (confirmation, access instructions, checkout, win-back). Which PMS is source of truth, and does it pass messages or only reservations? Which send paths must the sequence use (email, WhatsApp, Airbnb/other OTA)? Who will own the builder after go-live—guest services, a single “Jonathan,” or a vendor? Which branches are policy (channel, pet, loyalty, gap night) versus hope? Where should a no-answer path go (Slack, reassign, inject agent)? Estimate monthly sends × credit table against the package’s credits per unit.

**Next practical step:** in a demo, rebuild one live stay sequence with their PMS event and one real channel—not a slide of 43 logos—then map Messaging-and-up packaging and credit burn. Book that working session rather than pitching Operations (still “coming soon”) or transferring an Agents case study into Workflows.

Overview

Conduit Workflows provides visual automations for proactive messages, routing and triage. Agents supply the live reply behavior. Conduit describes it as automating that journey from check-in through follow-ups and routine tasks, with builders assembling confirmations, check-in instructions, follow-ups, and upgrades around the booking, the property, and the guest’s response. Source

In platform architecture, workflows are the “arms and legs”: proactive outreach, routing into systems or teammates, and triage that escalates then can auto-close. Source Conversational answering still sits with AI Agents and the Inbox. Workflows schedule, branch, wait, notify, and inject an agent when a defined event fires.

A concrete before/after: a support team copy-pastes door codes and check-in notes whenever a reservation appears. After a PMS-tied workflow, a reservation or stay-date trigger sends the confirmation and check-in sequence on connected email, WhatsApp, or OTA channels, branches on channel or a custom signal, waits until a send window, and only then injects an agent or pings Slack if the guest replies with a problem. Limits are real: the sequence only sends on connected channels, stay-date logic needs PMS/booking data, paid actions consume credits, and inbox routing is evaluated before workflow triggers. Source

Who it is for

Conduit positions the company for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers. Source Workflows is aimed at operators who already have a repeating guest calendar (confirm, instruct, upsell, follow up) and want those sequences designed once instead of typed per stay.

Buyer-role hypotheses include founders, revenue/guest-services leads and operations owners, informed by named stories rather than a required title map who care whether journey automation is included in a package and whether credits will cover outbound volume. Users are guest-services managers and the people Haven calls conversational engineers—staff who build and iterate workflows rather than answering every check-in question. Source Day-to-day agents still work exceptions in the inbox; they are consumers of routing and triage, not the primary authors.

Visual builder Hospitality triggers and actions without writing each sequence from scratch Workspace access to workflows Custom code in the developer platform

documents.summary: Operator is Conduit’s in-workspace assistant for inspecting and editing configuration, not a fifth commercial product next to Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows. Public sources place it on the Messaging package feature list and in V3 docs; they do not support selling it as an autonomous guest or operations agent.
documents.markdown:
# Operator & internal AI availability

Operator is a named **workspace assistant** in Conduit documentation. It is not listed as a standalone product on marketing navigation, which names [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows), and **Operations** as coming soon. Treat Operator as an internal configuration surface unless a later source changes that packaging.

## What is established

Docs define Operator as Conduit’s workspace assistant: it helps create agents, write Skills, inspect data, understand escalations, and manage configuration in the current workspace. Open it from the main sidebar or as a sidebar on V3 build pages. The start guide puts it in test-and-deploy: inspect, edit, and reason about agent configuration. The agents overview lists it under Build Surfaces with Knowledge, Skills, Tools, and Sandbox. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/agent-hub/operator.md)

Public product pages do **not** sell Operator as its own SKU. Footer and product menus list Conduit Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows. Operations is labeled “Coming soon” for AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance, and inspections—a different name and job from Operator. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Pricing copy includes “Operator, workflows, escalation” on the Messaging package (starting **$18 / unit / mo**, **40 credits / unit / mo**). That is a bundle feature line, not an Operator-only price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)

Two other “operator” uses must stay separate. V3 can create **internal agents** that run on workspace data and do not own a customer inbox; Conduit publishes a gallery of those patterns. The REST API also uses “operator replies” for human/staff messages (`is_sent_by_autopilot` is true only when the AI agent sent the message). Neither is the Operator assistant. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/agent-hub/internal-agent-use-cases.md)

## Role in the product system

Operator sits in the V3 Agent Hub loop: help the team configure the workspace; do not replace a published guest agent. Docs contrast four surfaces:

| Surface | Who it serves | Guest inbox? | Documented job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operator | Workspace team | No | Inspect, edit, reason about configuration |
| Customer agent | Contacts | Yes | Reply through an inbox |
| Internal agent | Team or systems | No | Internal work; may trigger customer actions only via configured workflows, tools, or channels |
| Voice agent | Callers | Voice config | Phone handling |

[Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/agent-hub/operator.md)

A published agent’s behavior still comes from that agent’s Persona, Skills, Tools, Behavior, and Settings. Operator tool access is configured separately from agent tools. Operator Settings cover model behavior and reasoning level when supported, Operator-specific Skills, and which connection, custom, MCP, and built-in tools Operator may use. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/agent-hub/operator.md)

MCP can manage Operator Skills (`operatorSettings.skills`) with `list_operator_skills`, `create_operator_skill`, `patch_operator_skill`, and `delete_operator_skill`. Those tools are MCP-only (no matching REST route), require `workspace_id`, and writes need a read/write token plus Manage Agents. That is configuration of the assistant, not a second product. See [Developer platform](#knowledge/product-developers). [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

Devices docs state device tools are available to chat agents, voice agents, workflows, **and Operator**; once the Devices add-on is enabled, Operator can use those tools. Changelog **3.12** (28 Aug 2026) says tasks, including custom fields, can be updated “straight from the AI operator,” Operator timestamps use the workspace timezone, and a workflow-canvas fix unblocked the AI operator. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/devices/overview.md)

## Use cases and users

Documented users are workspace teammates, not guests. Concrete tasks in Operator docs:

- Create a chat agent from a plain-language description
- Draft or revise Skills (including turning a rough policy into a Skill on the Skills page)
- Inspect Knowledge gaps or conflicts; draft a Knowledge article while reviewing a source
- Reason about escalations; review an agent’s escalation Skills before changing them
- Generate reports or exports **when the workspace has the required access**
- Point the user to the right configuration page; ask what an agent needs before publish; draft a custom-tool description

[Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/agent-hub/operator.md)

With Devices enabled, Operator can use the same device tool catalog as agents and MCP (list devices, telemetry, access codes, lock/thermostat writes subject to policy). Changelog additionally records task field updates from the AI operator. Docs tell teams to review staged changes before publishing agents, enabling tools, deleting sources, or changing automation. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/devices/overview.md)

The internal-agent gallery (cleaning-status messages, trash reminders, lockout codes, and similar) is **not** a list of Operator features. Those are examples of internal agents teams have built or scoped; most need property rules, PMS fields, and escalation contacts. Do not infer Operator performs those jobs unattended.

## Availability and dependencies

| Item | What sources show | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commercial listing | Messaging package feature: Operator, workflows, escalation | No Operator-only SKU or fee |
| UI | Main sidebar; sidebar on V3 build pages; full-page threads | No public screenshot of defaults |
| MCP Operator Skills | v3 plan MCP; Manage Agents for writes | No REST equivalent |
| Devices | Operator can use device tools after Devices add-on | Writes follow device policy; remote unlock off by default |
| Operations product | Marketing: coming soon (housekeeping, maintenance, inspections) | Not Operator |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)

Messaging starting rates and credits are package-level; see [Pricing](#knowledge/pricing). The credit guide says Operator turns are metered by model and billable tokens, while internal-agent runs have a dynamic work-based cost. It gives roughly 7,000–71,000 billable tokens per credit depending on model, with possible context discounts; this is not one universal per-turn price. It does not establish that Operator autonomously sends guest messages without configured tools and permissions. [Credit guide](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits)

## What sales can say

Say Operator is the in-product workspace assistant for configuring and inspecting Conduit—drafting agents and Skills, checking Knowledge, reasoning about escalations—not a guest-facing agent and not a billed add-on with its own rate card. You may say Messaging’s published feature list includes Operator alongside workflows and escalation, that Operator Skills can be managed over MCP on eligible v3 workspaces, and that Operator can use device tools after Devices is enabled.

Do not pitch Operator as the coming Operations product, as autopilot housekeeping, or as the internal-agent gallery. Do not promise unattended guest actions, resolution rates, or that “operator” in API message flags means this assistant. Keep copy aligned with [Product catalog](#knowledge/products-capabilities) and [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents).

## Questions to resolve

Operator credit metering is documented above; there is no single flat per-turn price. Remaining questions concern default enabled tools, guest-conversation write permissions, and how Messaging’s Operator inclusion maps to each workspace version. Confirm with product before using Operator as a primary campaign object.
open_questions: Does Operator consume credits, and on which rate card, when used as the workspace assistant?
Is Operator included on every Messaging-or-above workspace, or only after a v3/API entitlement?
Can Operator send or change guest-facing messages, or only configuration artifacts unless a tool/agent is explicitly enabled?
What is the default Operator tool set before an admin grants connection, custom, MCP, or device tools?
How should sales treat the internal-agent gallery versus Operator when a prospect asks for ‘internal AI’?

documents.html:
Operator is a named workspace assistant in Conduit documentation. It is not listed as a standalone product on marketing navigation, which names AI Agents, Inbox, Guest Portals, Workflows, and Operations as coming soon. Treat Operator as an internal configuration surface unless a later source changes that packaging.

What is established

Docs define Operator as Conduit’s workspace assistant: it helps create agents, write Skills, inspect data, understand escalations, and manage configuration in the current workspace. Open it from the main sidebar or as a sidebar on V3 build pages. The start guide puts it in test-and-deploy: inspect, edit, and reason about agent configuration. The agents overview lists it under Build Surfaces with Knowledge, Skills, Tools, and Sandbox. Source

Public product pages do not sell Operator as its own SKU. Footer and product menus list Conduit Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows. Operations is labeled “Coming soon” for AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance, and inspections—a different name and job from Operator. Source

Pricing copy includes “Operator, workflows, escalation” on the Messaging package (starting $18 / unit / mo, 40 credits / unit / mo). That is a bundle feature line, not an Operator-only price. Source

Two other “operator” uses must stay separate. V3 can create internal agents that run on workspace data and do not own a customer inbox; Conduit publishes a gallery of those patterns. The REST API also uses “operator replies” for human/staff messages (is_sent_by_autopilot is true only when the AI agent sent the message). Neither is the Operator assistant. Source

Role in the product system

Operator sits in the V3 Agent Hub loop: help the team configure the workspace; do not replace a published guest agent. Docs contrast four surfaces:

Surface Who it serves Guest inbox? Documented job
Operator Workspace team No Inspect, edit, reason about configuration
Customer agent Contacts Yes Reply through an inbox
Internal agent Team or systems No Internal work; may trigger customer actions only via configured workflows, tools, or channels
Voice agent Callers Voice config Phone handling

Source

A published agent’s behavior still comes from that agent’s Persona, Skills, Tools, Behavior, and Settings. Operator tool access is configured separately from agent tools. Operator Settings cover model behavior and reasoning level when supported, Operator-specific Skills, and which connection, custom, MCP, and built-in tools Operator may use. Source

MCP can manage Operator Skills (operatorSettings.skills) with list_operator_skills, create_operator_skill, patch_operator_skill, and delete_operator_skill. Those tools are MCP-only (no matching REST route), require workspace_id, and writes need a read/write token plus Manage Agents. That is configuration of the assistant, not a second product. See Developer platform. Source

Devices docs state device tools are available to chat agents, voice agents, workflows, and Operator; once the Devices add-on is enabled, Operator can use those tools. Changelog 3.12 (28 Aug 2026) says tasks, including custom fields, can be updated “straight from the AI operator,” Operator timestamps use the workspace timezone, and a workflow-canvas fix unblocked the AI operator. Source

Use cases and users

Documented users are workspace teammates, not guests. Concrete tasks in Operator docs:

  • Create a chat agent from a plain-language description
  • Draft or revise Skills (including turning a rough policy into a Skill on the Skills page)
  • Inspect Knowledge gaps or conflicts; draft a Knowledge article while reviewing a source
  • Reason about escalations; review an agent’s escalation Skills before changing them
  • Generate reports or exports when the workspace has the required access
  • Point the user to the right configuration page; ask what an agent needs before publish; draft a custom-tool description

Source

With Devices enabled, Operator can use the same device tool catalog as agents and MCP (list devices, telemetry, access codes, lock/thermostat writes subject to policy). Changelog additionally records task field updates from the AI operator. Docs tell teams to review staged changes before publishing agents, enabling tools, deleting sources, or changing automation. Source

The internal-agent gallery (cleaning-status messages, trash reminders, lockout codes, and similar) is not a list of Operator features. Those are examples of internal agents teams have built or scoped; most need property rules, PMS fields, and escalation contacts. Do not infer Operator performs those jobs unattended.

Availability and dependencies

Item What sources show Gap
Commercial listing Messaging package feature: Operator, workflows, escalation No Operator-only SKU or fee
UI Main sidebar; sidebar on V3 build pages; full-page threads No public screenshot of defaults
MCP Operator Skills v3 plan MCP; Manage Agents for writes No REST equivalent
Devices Operator can use device tools after Devices add-on Writes follow device policy; remote unlock off by default
Operations product Marketing: coming soon (housekeeping, maintenance, inspections) Not Operator

Source

Messaging starting rates and credits are package-level; see Pricing. The credit guide says Operator turns are metered by model and billable tokens, while internal-agent runs have a dynamic work-based cost. It gives roughly 7,000–71,000 billable tokens per credit depending on model, with possible context discounts; this is not one universal per-turn price. It does not establish that Operator autonomously sends guest messages without configured tools and permissions. Credit guide

What sales can say

Say Operator is the in-product workspace assistant for configuring and inspecting Conduit—drafting agents and Skills, checking Knowledge, reasoning about escalations—not a guest-facing agent and not a billed add-on with its own rate card. You may say Messaging’s published feature list includes Operator alongside workflows and escalation, that Operator Skills can be managed over MCP on eligible v3 workspaces, and that Operator can use device tools after Devices is enabled.

Do not pitch Operator as the coming Operations product, as autopilot housekeeping, or as the internal-agent gallery. Do not promise unattended guest actions, resolution rates, or that “operator” in API message flags means this assistant. Keep copy aligned with Product catalog and AI Agents.

Questions to resolve

Operator credit metering is documented above; there is no single flat per-turn price. Remaining questions concern default enabled tools, guest-conversation write permissions, and how Messaging’s Operator inclusion maps to each workspace version. Confirm with product before using Operator as a primary campaign object.

documents.title: Developer platform & custom workflows
documents.summary: Conduit’s documented developer surfaces are a v3-plan REST API and MCP server plus in-product custom Python/JavaScript tools; visual workflows, agents, knowledge, and marketplace templates remain managed product features. An endpoint or MCP tool existing is not the same as a token, workspace permission, add-on, or per-agent tool grant authorizing an agent to execute it.
documents.markdown:
## Purpose and users

Conduit’s public developer story is to [build with Conduit](https://www.conduit.ai/developers) either by calling the REST API or by giving an AI client native access through MCP. That is a workspace-data and configuration interface, not a replacement for the hospitality product. The same workspace still holds members, inboxes, channels, Knowledge, agents, tools, workflows, and settings; operators configure those surfaces in the app. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)

A developer is needed when the account must sync Conduit records into another system, drive Cursor/Claude/Codex/VS Code against a live workspace, author custom code tools, or create agents/workflows/knowledge programmatically. Guest messaging, the unified inbox, [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [visual Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows), PMS listing sync, and marketplace templates stay product features that hospitality teams can run without writing integrations. Docs also say most teams can customize voice, policies, enable or disable workflows, and write custom API functions after going live—the last of those is the developer path, not the default path. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/overview/how-conduit-agents-work)

Unknown from these pages: how many customers use API/MCP versus the visual builder, and whether a dedicated engineering hire is required versus a technical operator.

## Interfaces and capabilities

| Surface | What sources describe | Auth model | Distinct from product UI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| REST API | Typed endpoints for workspaces, contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, knowledge, agents, skills, workflows, connected devices | Bearer token; workspace-scoped | Programmatic CRUD/send vs inbox and Build screens | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/developers)
| OpenAPI | Unique operation IDs, typed parameters, response schemas, operation descriptions for SDK generation and LLM function calling | Same API tokens | Schema for clients, not a separate product | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/developers)
| MCP server | Streamable HTTP at `https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp`; MCP revision 2025-06-18 | OAuth 2.1 for interactive clients; `capi_` tokens for server-to-server | Same authenticated capabilities as tools, with read/write/idempotent/destructive annotations | [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)
| Custom code tools | Python or JavaScript tools, plus connection tools, MCP tools, and per-agent overrides | Enabled in Tools; also creatable via API/MCP | Code the agent may call only if that agent is granted the tool | [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)
| Visual workflows | Trigger → actions/conditions in the builder; API can list/get/create/update workflows and read executions | Product UI plus workflow API | Managed automation; not an event-subscription webhook catalog | [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/getting-started)

REST overview lists contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, escalations, custom attributes, knowledge, workspace metadata, agents, skills, custom tools, workflows, reservations, appointments, helpdesk tickets, and insights such as automation rate. Base URL is `https://api.conduit.ai/v1`. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

MCP can look up contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, reservations, and appointments; search knowledge; send messages on a conversation, ticket, or contact channel; manage agents, skills, custom code tools, and contact custom attributes; list accessible workspaces; and manage Operator skills (`operatorSettings.skills`). Device inspect/control tools exist only when the Devices add-on is enabled. Portal session, verification, offer, and template tools need the Portals add-on. `operator_*` tools are MCP-only with no matching REST route. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

The ChatGPT/Codex plugin is a narrower, read-only subset (five tools). Sending messages or using the full catalog requires a direct MCP connection. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

Documented “webhooks” are not a general Conduit outbound event bus. Workflows include a **Send webhook (HTTP)** action. Some PMS setups (for example Beds24) paste a Conduit **Webhook URL** so the PMS can push into Conduit. Neither is documented as a public subscribe-to-inbox-events API. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage)

## Implementation patterns

**Keep the system of record in Conduit, poll for deltas.** List Conversations with `updated_after`, then List Conversation Messages with `created_after`. Cursors page a snapshot; timestamps find what changed. Deduplicate on message `id`. Filter on `created_at`, not `sent_at`, or backdated channel imports can be skipped. Distinguish AI sends with `is_sent_by_autopilot`—do not infer automation from `sender.user_id`. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

**MCP in an IDE or assistant.** Pin one `workspace_id` at session start (`list_workspaces`). Pre-approve read tools if the client allows it; never allow-list `send_*`, `patch_*`, `create_*`, `update_*`, or `delete_*`. Pass a stable `idempotency_key` on every send so retries do not double-message guests. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

**Custom agent actions.** Author Python/JavaScript tools in Tools (or via `create_custom_tool`). MCP guidance is to call `list_custom_tool_runtimes` first so the model matches the entrypoint and return shape. Then grant that tool on the specific agent (`set_agent_tool_access` / Toggle Agent Tool). The REST route existing is not that grant. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

**Managed custom workflows.** Ops teams still build proactive, routing, and triage flows in the visual builder (tags, delays, Slack/email, inject AI). Developers use workflow APIs when they need to version or inspect those graphs outside the UI. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/types-of-workflows)

## Dependencies and controls

Tokens are generated under **Settings > API & MCP**. The setting is personal; tokens can cover one or more workspaces where the user is an admin. Start read-only; write tools such as `send_conversation_message` need a read/write token (or OAuth `mcp:write`). Scope every request to a workspace the token can access. Rotate/revoke in the same settings screen; revocation is described as immediate. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

MCP OAuth 2.1 uses Dynamic Client Registration and workspace consent. A valid token with an empty `list_workspaces` result is not workspace-scoped. HTTP 403 means missing workspace access or missing write privilege—not that the tool is absent from the catalog. Device writes also follow workspace policy and contact scope. Portal writes need **Manage Portals**; Operator skill writes need **Manage Agents**. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)

Per-agent tool access is the control that decides whether a guest-facing agent may execute a custom function or connection tool. Publishing an agent, enabling a workflow, and handing an MCP client a write token are three different authorizations. Keep human approval on MCP writes that send guest messages.

## Packaging and limits

Both the REST API and MCP server are documented as available on the **v3 plan**, enabled by contacting `support@conduit.ai`. Public [Pricing](#knowledge/pricing) lists Messaging / Guest / Devices / Full Suite unit rates and a Startup package; it does not publish a standalone API or MCP SKU. Do not treat those package starting rates as developer-platform prices. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

Default rate limit is **120 requests per minute per workspace**, shared by REST and MCP. 429 includes `Retry-After`. Some workspaces may have higher limits by plan or entitlement. List endpoints paginate with `limit` 1–100 (default 20) and `cursor`. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/api-reference/introduction)

Workflow **runs** are free; credits apply only when a successful run finishes a paid action. **Send webhook (HTTP)** is listed at **0 credits**. That is usage for an outbound HTTP step, not evidence of unlimited webhook subscriptions. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage)

Gaps: no public quota for custom tools, no SLA, no documented webhook signature/event catalog, and no mapping of “v3 plan” to a named row on the marketing pricing table.

## Sales and technical discovery

Ask whether the buying team needs (1) visual guest-journey automation, (2) a custom tool an [agent](#knowledge/product-agents) should call, (3) an external system of record that must poll Conduit, or (4) MCP inside ChatGPT/Claude/Cursor. Custom code needs someone able to implement and maintain it, but in-app custom tools are separate from external REST/MCP enablement. REST/MCP access is described as requiring support-enabled v3 access; that wording does not establish a separately priced package. Connecting an existing MCP client may be an administrator task, while building a custom integration needs engineering. Do not require API access merely to use a visual workflow or in-app tool. Confirm add-ons before promising device or portal APIs. Confirm write-token and per-agent tool policy before promising that “the agent can hit our API.”

Treat vendor rhetoric about going live in a week as a company claim, not a measured implementation SLA. Pair this page with [Integrations](#knowledge/integrations) for PMS/channel connections and [Operator](#knowledge/product-operator) for non-code configuration work.
open_questions: How does the documented “v3 plan” required for API/MCP map to named packages on conduit.ai/pricing?
Is there a documented public event-subscription webhook API (payloads, signatures, event types), or only workflow Send webhook and inbound PMS webhook URLs?
What entitlements, quotas, or review process exist for custom Python/JavaScript tools beyond v3 enablement?

documents.title: Integrations & implementation readiness
documents.summary: Conduit publishes a 43-item integrations catalog plus setup docs that split PMS connectors into messaging and non-messaging paths, with separate channel, CRM, task, Devices, API, and MCP surfaces. Listings and marketing cards are not a per-vendor action matrix; implementation hinges on workspace type, duplicate-thread rules, and which writes are actually enabled.
documents.markdown:
Conduit’s site lists 43 integrations across CRM, channel managers, collaboration, messaging, PMS, and task managers ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)). Docs treat connections as workspace work: channels first, then PMS and other sources that feed Knowledge and tools for [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)). A logo is not proof that every account needs, or receives, every connector or write action.

## Integration map

Qualify four evidence types separately: marketplace cards, official setup docs, product claims about agent actions, and [developer](#knowledge/product-developers) API/MCP surfaces.

**PMS and related systems**

| System | Public list | Messaging via this connector (docs) | Other claim |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guesty, Beds24/Bed24, Hostaway, Hostfully, Hostify, Lodgify, OwnerRez, Resly, Smily | Marketplace + PMS docs | Messaging PMS: keep OTA messaging on the PMS or threads can duplicate | Guesty card: sync reservations and centralize Guesty messaging ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/guesty)) |
| Hospitable, PassTheKeys | PMS docs only | Messaging PMS | Absent from the 43-card scrape ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)) |
| Apaleo, Cloudbeds, Escapia, HomHero/Homhero, Mews, Opera Cloud, RMS/RMS Cloud, Streamline, Track | Mix | Non-messaging: property/reservation data; message via auxiliary OTAs | Track’s card mentions Airbnb/Booking.com routing, but setup docs classify Track as non-messaging PMS sync. Confirm the actual separate OTA messaging path; neither the card nor a coming-soon directory label settles current availability ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)) |
| CiiRUS, Kross Booking | PMS docs only | Non-messaging | Not on the marketplace scrape ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)) |
| StayNTouch | Marketplace only | Not in the docs table | Card claims two-way write-back ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)) |
| Airbnb as PMS | Docs + Airbnb card | Separate Airbnb rules | Card: messages, support, reservation modifications ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/airbnb)) |

Docs say Conduit integrates with over 15 PMS systems to populate listing information, create contacts from reservations, and show listings in Knowledge after sync ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)). Opera Cloud’s page matches the non-messaging class: property, room type, reservation, and profile sync; messaging stays on existing hotel channels ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera)). Wheelhouse is listed as dynamic pricing, not a PMS path ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)).

**Messaging channels**

| Channel | Evidence | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email, WhatsApp, phone/SMS, widget | Start guide + connect docs | [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) unifies email, calls, WhatsApp, social, and connected OTA threads ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)) |
| Airbnb | Marketplace (Messaging + Channel Manager) + connect docs | Two-way send/receive claimed on the Airbnb card ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/airbnb)) |
| Twilio | Marketplace | Unified calls and SMS ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)) |
| LINE, iMessage, VoiceAI numbers | Docs index / VoiceAI guide | Not on the 43-card list ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/llms.txt)) |
| Booking.com, VRBO | Marketplace | Both “Coming soon” ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)) |
| Expedia | Marketplace + PMS docs | Card: push availability, rates, reservations. Docs: support-managed Expedia *messaging* for non-messaging PMS such as Cloudbeds; inventory can stay on the PMS ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)) |

[Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) send through connected email, WhatsApp, and OTA channels ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)).

**Ops, knowledge, API**

Marketplace names Slack, Asana, ClickUp, Airtable, HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Drive/Docs/Sheets/Calendar, Notion, Firecrawl, Cal.com, Calendly, GitHub, and Apollo.io ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)). Docs add Microsoft Teams notifications, a V3 Marketplace for apps/templates, and Devices (locks, thermostats, sensors, cameras) as an add-on for agents, workflows, [Operator](#knowledge/product-operator), or MCP ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/llms.txt)). [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) mention compatible smart locks without naming vendors ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals)). REST (`https://api.conduit.ai/v1`) and MCP (`https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp`) are v3-plan surfaces enabled via support; default limit 120 requests/minute/workspace, shared across REST and MCP ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)).

## Direct versus relayed connections

Docs classify PMS connectors by whether *this* integration delivers guest messages—not by every feature the vendor sells. Messaging PMS (Beds24, Guesty, Hospitable, Hostaway, Hostfully, Hostify, Lodgify, OwnerRez, PassTheKeys, Resly, Smily): keep OTA messaging on the PMS. Non-messaging (Apaleo, CiiRUS, Cloudbeds, Escapia, Homhero, Kross Booking, Mews, Opera Cloud, RMS, Streamline, Track): connect each OTA messaging channel directly ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)).

Workspace rules: multiple PMS accounts only when they share the same messaging setup; messaging and non-messaging PMS cannot share a workspace; Airbnb as primary PMS blocks another PMS; Airbnb can sit beside a PMS, with messages either remaining on the PMS or matching to reservations when the PMS is non-messaging ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)). Cloudbeds + Expedia is the worked example: Cloudbeds can keep inventory, rates, availability, and reservation sync while Conduit support connects Expedia messaging; do not leave messaging on both paths ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)).

Marketing can disagree. The Mews card says teams can centralize guest messaging from Mews properties, while the PMS guide lists Mews as non-messaging ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/mews)). The Expedia marketplace line about pushing availability is not the support-managed messaging path in docs. Treat cards as listings until setup docs confirm the path.

## Data and action boundaries

Product copy says agents handle voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA messages, and can “check bookings, make reservation changes, and create tasks through supported integrations,” with live PMS, knowledge, payments, and tasks as clusters—not a per-vendor matrix ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)). Inbox copy places stay history, booking details, and availability from connected PMS/OTA accounts beside the thread and names Mews, Opera, Booking, and Airbnb as examples ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)).

Tighter documentation:

- PMS connect: listing/Knowledge sync, contacts from reservations, scheduled Knowledge refresh (daily–monthly), and “Check for new listings.” Auth differs (Lodgify API key; Beds24 invite code plus per-property webhooks; Opera Cloud via OHIP) ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)).
- Opera’s public page documents property/reservation/profile sync and no messaging through that connector. Other write actions are unestablished, not proven impossible ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera)). StayNTouch marketplace copy is the supplied source that states two-way write-back for that PMS ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations)).
- Workflows may use webhooks or MCP ([Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)). Workflow credit docs price Slack, Teams, HubSpot, Salesforce, Airtable, webhooks, and channel sends—evidence those builder actions exist, not prices for this page ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage)).
- MCP: pin `workspace_id`; keep approvals on write tools (`send_`, `patch_`, `create_`, `update_`, `delete_`); pass idempotency keys; use least-privilege tokens. The ChatGPT/Codex plugin is five read-only tools, not the full catalog ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/mcp/overview)).
- Bring-your-own Twilio VoiceAI needs webhook `https://api.conduit.ai/twilio/messaging`, A2P 10DLC, and SMS enabled, or inbound SMS fails ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-voiceai-ai-number)).

Do not infer that every logo supports reservation edits, payments, tasks, or lock control.

## Implementation checklist

Public start-guide order ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/)):

1. Create the workspace (PMS UI may require Short Term Rental, Long Term Rental, or Hotel settings) ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)).
2. Invite members; decide who can manage agent settings.
3. Connect channels that apply; then PMS/data sources.
4. Import listings; enable PMS Knowledge auto-sync; use Sync history and Check for new listings.
5. Configure V3 agents, Knowledge, Skills, and Tools (connection tools, custom code, MCP, per-agent overrides).
6. Set inbox routing so new channel contacts do not sit in Unmapped; routing runs before workflow triggers ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/inbox-routing)).
7. Sandbox-test with listing and reservation context; expand writes via Connect → Teach → Test → Deploy.
8. Confirm support-enabled REST/MCP access; the documentation’s “v3 plan” wording is not mapped to public package names. Do not equate a V3 interface or Full Suite with automatic API access. Confirm Devices or Portals entitlements before those tool groups.

Ownership issues the sources actually raise: duplicate OTA threads if messaging is dual-routed; mixed PMS types blocked in one workspace; Expedia messaging provisioned with Conduit support rather than workspace credentials; MCP send misfires if clients allow-list write tools; Twilio SMS dropped without A2P; Lodgify API access may be gated on Lodgify’s plan ([Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/connect-pms)). Sources do not document SLAs, RACI, or security-review checklists.

## Unknowns and discovery questions

There is no published matrix of per-PMS writes (modify reservation, take payment, create a task). StayNTouch, Hospitable, PassTheKeys, CiiRUS, Kross Booking, LINE, and iMessage appear on different lists. Booking.com and VRBO were “Coming soon” on the scraped catalog. The Portals FAQ “How does Portals work with my PMS and booking channels?” is unanswered in the supplied HTML. Marketplace Email/WhatsApp blurbs still say HostAI. Confirm live connector status, message path, and allowed writes against the operator’s actual PMS and OTAs.

How Guest Portals bind to PMS/OTA data and which smart-lock vendors are compatible.
