documents.title: Pricing & packaging
documents.summary: Conduit publishes USD starting rates per unit per month for Messaging, Guest, Guest + Devices, and Full Suite, plus a flat Startup price for 0–25 units; each package lists included monthly credits. Credit docs define four usage categories, voice minute rates, Operator/internal-agent variability, workflow paid actions, inbox replies that do not consume credits, and overage on the next invoice, while Portals is both bundled in Guest-and-above packages and described as a listing-count add-on without a public standalone fee.
documents.markdown:
Conduit’s public commercial story is package starting rates plus a credit pool, not a menu of separately priced Inbox, Agents, or Workflows SKUs. Figures below are what Conduit publishes on its pricing page and docs as of the captured pages—not a signed quote, not independently audited, and not a guarantee of what every customer pays.

## Published plans

The pricing page addresses “independent teams to enterprise,” shows starting rates, and says pricing scales beyond 50 listings. It also tells operators to talk to an AI expert to map a package. HTML and Markdown extracts agree on the dollar and credit numbers; nothing in the supplied pages is a conflicting toggle. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

| Package | Starting price | Included credits | Page CTA | What the package list adds |
| Messaging | $18 / unit / mo | 40 credits / unit / mo | Get Started | Unified inbox, Voice AI inbound and outbound, PMS and OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, escalation, analytics |
| Guest | $30 / unit / mo | 60 credits / unit / mo | Get Started | Everything in Messaging, plus in-portal AI concierge, rich-media guidebooks, damage waivers with no SKU fee, one-click payment upsells |
| Guest + Devices | $36 / unit / mo | 80 credits / unit / mo | Get Started | Everything in Guest, plus smart home, portal-integrated devices, guest/team access codes, device management workflows |
| Full Suite | $48 / unit / mo | 100 credits / unit / mo | Talk to Sales | Everything in Guest + Devices, plus tasks and workforce, agentic operations workflows, scheduling and dispatch, inventory management |
| Startup (0–25 units) | $899 / mo | 2,000 credits / mo | Get Started | Described as the full feature set with no implementation fee |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)

Do not treat $18–$48 as standalone licenses for [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), or [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). Those capabilities appear inside packages.

## Usage and billing units

Stacked packages are billed **per unit per month**; Startup is a **flat month**. The same pricing page talks about **listings** (rates scale beyond 50). The Portals FAQ prices an add-on by **contracted listing count**. These pages never equate unit, listing, and room—confirm the inventory object on the quote. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

A credit is Conduit’s usage unit. Included credits reset at the start of each monthly billing cycle. Usage is tracked in four categories: Workflows, Operator Sidebar, Internal Agents, and Voice AI. Replies sent by AI agents in the inbox do not consume credits. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits)

| Activity | Published credit rule | Caveat on the same page |
| Regular voice minute | 1 credit per minute | Voice AI category |
| AI voice minute | 8 credits per minute | Same category; much heavier than regular voice |
| Operator sidebar | Variable per turn | ~7,000–71,000 billable tokens per 1 credit depending on model; prior context may be discounted |
| Internal agents | Dynamic | No single flat rate |
| Workflows | Paid actions on successful runs | Starting or running a workflow is free; most steps free; charges when a successful run sends a message, calls an integration, runs an AI prompt, searches the web, or makes an agent call |

[Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/credits)

Voice AI can sit in the Messaging feature list and still draw credits when minutes run. Inbox AI replies do not. Illustration only: ten AI voice minutes would use 80 credits at 8 per minute—that is arithmetic on the published rate, not a customer invoice.

Settings > Billing shows cycle usage by category and workflow. When credits run low, Conduit says you can upgrade or continue into overage charged on the next invoice. Invoice PDFs are downloaded there; billing questions go to support@conduit.ai. [Source](https://docs.conduit.ai/setting-up-conduit/billing.md) No dollar overage rate is published.

## What is included

[Messaging](#knowledge/product-inbox) is the communications stack: every-channel inbox, inbound/outbound Voice AI, PMS/OTA integrations, [Operator](#knowledge/product-operator), workflows, escalation, analytics. [Guest](#knowledge/product-portals) adds stay-link merchandising on top of that stack (concierge, guidebooks, waivers without a SKU fee, one-click payment upsells). That is bundle copy, not a public à-la-carte Portals price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing.md)

Guest + Devices adds locks, thermostats, sensors, portal-integrated devices, access codes, and device workflows. Full Suite adds workforce/operations bullets. Product navigation still labels Operations “Coming soon,” so do not treat those Full Suite lines as independently confirmed generally available modules. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Startup is the full feature set for 0–25 units with no implementation fee. [Developer platform](#knowledge/product-developers) API and MCP access is for eligible authenticated workspaces; no developer line item appears on pricing.

The Portals FAQ (which fills gaps the HTML pricing FAQ does not answer) describes one branded stay link with no app: stay details, pre-arrival and identity checks, agreements or damage waivers, fees or deposits, upgrades, access when requirements are complete, and a stay-aware AI concierge. Portal card payments are described via a connected Stripe account (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Link), not reuse of the original booking card. Smart-lock behavior varies by provider and is confirmed in implementation. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)

The [workflow action guide](https://docs.conduit.ai/workflows/workflow-usage) separately lists Voice Agent Call at **6 credits/minute**, while the general guide lists AI voice at **8** and regular voice at **1**. Confirm which meter applies to the actual call path and whether any usage overlaps; these sources do not justify silently substituting or adding the rates.

Operator in Messaging is the workspace assistant, not the Operations product. Operations is separately marked coming soon in navigation; confirm individual Full Suite operational features before promising them. [Operator guide](#knowledge/product-operator)

## Choosing a package

Match published bullets, not assumed ROI. Messaging if the job is omnichannel inbox, voice, Operator, and workflows without portal merchandising. Guest if waivers, guidebooks, in-portal concierge, and payments matter. Guest + Devices if locks/thermostats/sensors and access codes must live in the portal. Full Suite if the buyer also wants workforce/operations language—and they should talk to sales (the only package with that CTA). Startup if the account is in the 0–25 unit band and wants the full feature set with the published no-implementation-fee claim.

Do not assume Messaging can add Portals at a listed rate. The FAQ says add-on pricing exists; the package table does not print it. Capability detail lives in the [product catalog](#knowledge/products-capabilities), not in a hidden SKU price.

## Unpublished terms

Not in these sources: overage $ per credit; volume steps above 50 listings; whether a unit is a listing; taxes; contract length; seat fees; guest-transaction fee schedule; API/MCP surcharges; currencies other than $. The HTML pricing FAQ lists “Is Conduit free?” without an answer in the extract—do not invent one. Portals FAQ says sales can quote monthly or annual; the main table is monthly starting rates only.

Portals is bundled inside Guest and higher packages **and** described as a paid add-on priced by contracted listing count with graduated volume pricing; bundles and guest-transaction terms can change the final rate. Both statements are Conduit’s; they are not one public number. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)

## Questions before a quote

1. Inventory: unit vs listing vs room, 0–25 (Startup) vs above 50 listings.
2. Portals path: Guest bundle vs listing add-on, and whether Messaging-only is even eligible.
3. Devices and access codes (Guest + Devices).
4. Full Suite operations/workforce scope versus Operations “Coming soon.”
5. Credit mix: AI voice (8/min) vs regular voice (1/min), Operator tokens, internal agents, paid workflow actions—not inbox AI replies.
6. Low-credit path: upgrade vs overage on the next invoice (rate unpublished).
7. Implementation fee (Startup says none; others unpublished) and monthly vs annual.
8. Stripe / guest-transaction terms, PMS/OTA/lock stack (lock and payment rules vary), billing entity, and Settings > Billing access (support@conduit.ai for charge disputes).

Starting rates are a map for the conversation, not the contract.
open_questions: What dollar rate is charged per credit in overage, and is it the same across packages?

Conduit’s public commercial story is package starting rates plus a credit pool, not a menu of separately priced Inbox, Agents, or Workflows SKUs. Figures below are what Conduit publishes on its pricing page and docs as of the captured pages—not a signed quote, not independently audited, and not a guarantee of what every customer pays.

Published plans

The pricing page addresses “independent teams to enterprise,” shows starting rates, and says pricing scales beyond 50 listings. It also tells operators to talk to an AI expert to map a package. HTML and Markdown extracts agree on the dollar and credit numbers; nothing in the supplied pages is a conflicting toggle. Source

| Package | Starting price | Included credits | Page CTA | What the package list adds | | Messaging | $18 / unit / mo | 40 credits / unit / mo | Get Started | Unified inbox, Voice AI inbound and outbound, PMS and OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, escalation, analytics | | Guest | $30 / unit / mo | 60 credits / unit / mo | Get Started | Everything in Messaging, plus in-portal AI concierge, rich-media guidebooks, damage waivers with no SKU fee, one-click payment upsells | | Guest + Devices | $36 / unit / mo | 80 credits / unit / mo | Get Started | Everything in Guest, plus smart home, portal-integrated devices, guest/team access codes, device management workflows | | Full Suite | $48 / unit / mo | 100 credits / unit / mo | Talk to Sales | Everything in Guest + Devices, plus tasks and workforce, agentic operations workflows, scheduling and dispatch, inventory management | | Startup (0–25 units) | $899 / mo | 2,000 credits / mo | Get Started | Described as the full feature set with no implementation fee |

Source

Do not treat $18–$48 as standalone licenses for Inbox, AI Agents, or Workflows. Those capabilities appear inside packages.

Usage and billing units

Stacked packages are billed per unit per month; Startup is a flat month. The same pricing page talks about listings (rates scale beyond 50). The Portals FAQ prices an add-on by contracted listing count. These pages never equate unit, listing, and room—confirm the inventory object on the quote. Source

A credit is Conduit’s usage unit. Included credits reset at the start of each monthly billing cycle. Usage is tracked in four categories: Workflows, Operator Sidebar, Internal Agents, and Voice AI. Replies sent by AI agents in the inbox do not consume credits. Source

| Activity | Published credit rule | Caveat on the same page | | Regular voice minute | 1 credit per minute | Voice AI category | | AI voice minute | 8 credits per minute | Same category; much heavier than regular voice | | Operator sidebar | Variable per turn | ~7,000–71,000 billable tokens per 1 credit depending on model; prior context may be discounted | | Internal agents | Dynamic | No single flat rate | | Workflows | Paid actions on successful runs | Starting or running a workflow is free; most steps free; charges when a successful run sends a message, calls an integration, runs an AI prompt, searches the web, or makes an agent call |

Source

Voice AI can sit in the Messaging feature list and still draw credits when minutes run. Inbox AI replies do not. Illustration only: ten AI voice minutes would use 80 credits at 8 per minute—that is arithmetic on the published rate, not a customer invoice.

Settings > Billing shows cycle usage by category and workflow. When credits run low, Conduit says you can upgrade or continue into overage charged on the next invoice. Invoice PDFs are downloaded there; billing questions go to support@conduit.ai. Source No dollar overage rate is published.

What is included

Messaging is the communications stack: every-channel inbox, inbound/outbound Voice AI, PMS/OTA integrations, Operator, workflows, escalation, analytics. Guest adds stay-link merchandising on top of that stack (concierge, guidebooks, waivers without a SKU fee, one-click payment upsells). That is bundle copy, not a public à-la-carte Portals price. Source

Guest + Devices adds locks, thermostats, sensors, portal-integrated devices, access codes, and device workflows. Full Suite adds workforce/operations bullets. Product navigation still labels Operations “Coming soon,” so do not treat those Full Suite lines as independently confirmed generally available modules. Source

Startup is the full feature set for 0–25 units with no implementation fee. Developer platform API and MCP access is for eligible authenticated workspaces; no developer line item appears on pricing.

The Portals FAQ (which fills gaps the HTML pricing FAQ does not answer) describes one branded stay link with no app: stay details, pre-arrival and identity checks, agreements or damage waivers, fees or deposits, upgrades, access when requirements are complete, and a stay-aware AI concierge. Portal card payments are described via a connected Stripe account (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Link), not reuse of the original booking card. Smart-lock behavior varies by provider and is confirmed in implementation. Source

The workflow action guide separately lists Voice Agent Call at 6 credits/minute, while the general guide lists AI voice at 8 and regular voice at 1. Confirm which meter applies to the actual call path and whether any usage overlaps; these sources do not justify silently substituting or adding the rates.

Operator in Messaging is the workspace assistant, not the Operations product. Operations is separately marked coming soon in navigation; confirm individual Full Suite operational features before promising them. Operator guide

Choosing a package

Match published bullets, not assumed ROI. Messaging if the job is omnichannel inbox, voice, Operator, and workflows without portal merchandising. Guest if waivers, guidebooks, in-portal concierge, and payments matter. Guest + Devices if locks/thermostats/sensors and access codes must live in the portal. Full Suite if the buyer also wants workforce/operations language—and they should talk to sales (the only package with that CTA). Startup if the account is in the 0–25 unit band and wants the full feature set with the published no-implementation-fee claim.

Do not assume Messaging can add Portals at a listed rate. The FAQ says add-on pricing exists; the package table does not print it. Capability detail lives in the product catalog, not in a hidden SKU price.

Unpublished terms

Not in these sources: overage $ per credit; volume steps above 50 listings; whether a unit is a listing; taxes; contract length; seat fees; guest-transaction fee schedule; API/MCP surcharges; currencies other than $. The HTML pricing FAQ lists “Is Conduit free?” without an answer in the extract—do not invent one. Portals FAQ says sales can quote monthly or annual; the main table is monthly starting rates only.

Portals is bundled inside Guest and higher packages and described as a paid add-on priced by contracted listing count with graduated volume pricing; bundles and guest-transaction terms can change the final rate. Both statements are Conduit’s; they are not one public number. Source

Questions before a quote

  1. Inventory: unit vs listing vs room, 0–25 (Startup) vs above 50 listings.
  2. Portals path: Guest bundle vs listing add-on, and whether Messaging-only is even eligible.
  3. Devices and access codes (Guest + Devices).
  4. Full Suite operations/workforce scope versus Operations “Coming soon.”
  5. Credit mix: AI voice (8/min) vs regular voice (1/min), Operator tokens, internal agents, paid workflow actions—not inbox AI replies.
  6. Low-credit path: upgrade vs overage on the next invoice (rate unpublished).
  7. Implementation fee (Startup says none; others unpublished) and monthly vs annual.
  8. Stripe / guest-transaction terms, PMS/OTA/lock stack (lock and payment rules vary), billing entity, and Settings > Billing access (support@conduit.ai for charge disputes).

Starting rates are a map for the conversation, not the contract.

documents.markdown:
# Customer evidence & usable proof

This library uses **named case-study pages only**. The stories index also says Conduit is trusted by hundreds of organizations and by 300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries; that is a company reach claim, not named product-adoption evidence, and logo or industry-link walls are not treated as proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers)

Pages were retrieved 19–20 September 2026. “Using Conduit since” dates are printed as-is. Results are attributed to Conduit’s write-ups, not independently verified. Stories usually name the platform as a whole ([AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows)) rather than a SKU; an integration name is not evidence of a supported action.

## Proof by customer and buying situation

### Vacation-rental and property-management operators

| Customer | Operating / buying situation | Named use | Reported result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Haven Vacation Rentals | Smokies STRs; Conduit since Feb 2024; installed earlier at ~40% automation with few workflows | Workflows, knowledge-base teaching, guest messaging | 90% automation across ~270 properties; support need from ~25 people to two per shift; 14 January listings with no extra support hires; scores held 4.8–4.9 |
| Cascadia Getaways | Oregon vacation rentals; first PM acquisition; page says using since Dec 2024 and deployed in March | Guest comms, knowledge base, routine AI answers | 60% automation and 4.9 communication score across 100 properties; 150 properties per support rep on shift |
| HomeHop | Cleveland/Akron STRs; failed prior AI vendor; Google Voice lockout; using since June 2025 (page also says ~two years) | Email, SMS, OTA and voice AI 1–7 AM; SuiteOP is the customer’s adjacent tool, not a Conduit SKU | ~40→108 listings without extra guest-support hires; 70% automation; overnight coverage in those hours |
| Canbnb | Canberra STR manager; 7→170 properties; 630-message backlog | Inbox; Hostaway/WhatsApp/email/SMS/chat; guest/owner/vendor inboxes | ~1,500 messages sent/week, 60% handled by AI; unexplained 150% headline excluded from usable results |
| Bocobay | High-end PM, Aruba and Curaçao; left Intercom (June 2024) | Unified email, WhatsApp, phone, live chat; notes/tags | Page: 80% resolution rate, “100s” hours saved; body does not show the math |
| Cosmica | Italy + Dubai; using Sep 2025 Dubai / Oct 2025 Italy | Messaging plus arrival, maintenance, cleaning workflows and Dubai upsells | No extra support team; outsourced VAs eliminated; upsells/cross-sells ~5% of Dubai revenue at peak |
| Easy BnB (published in the Bali Luxury Stays story) | Exit-oriented PM; 14 VAs; using since Dec 2024 (founded 2025 on the same page) | Guest-messaging AI; night 100% / day up to 85% | ~$22k/month labor savings; 11 VAs replaced; 75 units, 0 extra FTE; ~80–85% messaging automation |
| The Flex (Flex Living) | London/SF/Dubai; 17 SaaS tools; Conduit since Dec 2023 | Conversational AI, unified inbox, call summaries, tagging | Title 70% guest support; header also 90% of guest communication; CEO calls 70% “very realistic”; 80–90% also described as a goal |

Haven: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026). Cascadia: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways). HomeHop: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop). Canbnb: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb). Bocobay: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay). Cosmica: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cosmica). Bali/Easy BnB: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays). The Flex: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex).

Recurring STR situations: listing growth that used to require headcount, prior AI or Intercom misfit, split inboxes, overnight coverage, and acquisition or exit math. Canbnb’s body also calls the onboarding product “HostAI,” which is not resolved on the page. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb)

### Boutique hotel and separate multi-market CX proof

| Customer | Situation | Named use | Reported result |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel | Owner-operator; Jurny then other call services ($4k→$1.2k/mo, slow replies); Conduit since Dec 2024 | “AI-powered support platform and 24/7 staffed support team” replacing a call center; neither software-only savings nor a public $600 software price | Support $4,000→$600/mo; response 57 min→2 min avg; NOI +≥$3,400/mo; >$500k modeled asset value at 8% cap |
| Wynwood House | Hospitality + real estate in 7 countries; using since Oct 2025; Guesty + ChatGPT + translation + Sheets | Unified inbox, AI replies/translation, sentiment, shift-handoff summaries | Resolution 14–15 min → 3 min; 4.8 Airbnb rating in Colombia (not claimed as a lift) |

Lauderdale: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel). Wynwood: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house). Lauderdale is the only named **hotel** P&L story here. Wynwood is multi-market CX, not hotel-group operations. Index titles for BlueGems, Moxxi, Renjoy/Joy, and an unnamed 35-property 96% automation story have no bodies in this pack, so those figures are unused. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers)

Easy BnB is the business behind the eleven-VA replacement, approximately $22k/month savings and 75 additional units. Bali Luxury Stays is the founder’s subsequent venture, although the page is branded with that name. HomeHop’s portfolio growth period and its customer-since header disagree, so do not claim all 40-to-108 growth occurred during a verified Conduit deployment window. Lauderdale’s cost narrative includes an intermediate $1,200/month provider before $600 and a staffed-support component; keep those boundaries beside any campaign claim.

## What the results do and do not establish

They establish, as **company-attributed** stories: high STR automation after knowledge-base and workflow work (Haven was already installed at ~40%); some operators reporting stable communication scores while automating (Haven 4.8–4.9, Cascadia locked at 4.9); a boutique hotel owner reporting lower support cost, faster replies, fewer refunds, and a cap-rate translation of NOI; multi-market tool consolidation (Wynwood, Cosmica); a named Intercom move (Bocobay); recovery from a failed AI vendor (HomeHop); and an exit/labor story that replaced eleven VAs (Easy BnB, in the Bali Luxury Stays story)—unlike Haven, which says nobody was laid off because of AI. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays)

They do **not** establish a typical rate, a price, or that [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) or Operations (nav: coming soon) produced these outcomes. Lauderdale’s $500k is the owner’s 8% cap-rate model, not an appraisal or closed sale. The Flex header “17 tools replaced by Conduit” and “90% of guest communication automated” sit beside a 70% title, a 70% CEO quote, and 80–90% as a future build. Haven’s Guest Favorite share is 59% in the header and 55% in the TL;DR; About says 230+ properties vs ~270 in the body. Bocobay’s 80% / hundreds of hours are not derived in the article. Site widget “4.7 / 5” on G2 is not a named-customer result. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

## Matching proof to a campaign

Use **one named story per motion**. Keep customer, time window, and caveat in the same sentence as the number. Do not average rates across accounts.

| Prospect situation | Best-fit named proof | Do not stretch to |
|---|---|---|
| STR scale without linear guest-support hiring | Haven and HomeHop; Canbnb is separate message-volume evidence, not proof of flat headcount | Hotel groups or a guaranteed 90% |
| Absorb an acquisition without a new call center | Cascadia first PM company | “All integrations complete in a week” |
| NOI, OM, or exit multiple | Lauderdale $3.4k/mo NOI and 8% cap math; Easy BnB ~$22k/mo and 75 units | Treat cap-rate as appraised or sold value |
| Leave Intercom / unify WhatsApp + OTA + phone | Bocobay | The 80% header stat without methodology |
| Multi-country, multilingual CX | Wynwood 7 countries, 15→3 min; Cosmica Italy/Dubai | Causing Wynwood’s 4.8 Colombia rating |
| After-hours voice | HomeHop 1–7 AM; Haven snowstorm (three human issues) | 24/7 autopilot as current state |
| Stop building messaging AI in-house | Bali halted internal tool; Flex left comms out of a homegrown PMS | Conduit replacing the customer’s PMS |

See [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals), [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels), [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities), and [Qualification & account research playbook](#knowledge/buying-triggers).

## Evidence gaps

Hotel-group and independent-hotel proof beyond Lauderdale is missing from this pack. No story isolates Portals, a standalone price, or a contract start vs. result window. Index-only stories (BlueGems, 96% at 35 properties, Moxxi, Renjoy) are unusable until bodies exist. Staffing outcomes conflict in kind (Haven: no AI layoffs; Easy BnB: eleven VAs replaced). Automation denominators (messages vs support vs guest communication) are not defined consistently. Cascadia’s March vs December, HomeHop’s June 2025 vs “two years,” and Bali’s founded-2025 vs using-since-December-2024 need reconciliation before legal or investor use.
open_questions: What methodology sits behind Bocobay’s 80% resolution rate and “100s” of hours saved?
Which surfaces (Agents, Inbox, Workflows, voice, 24/7 staffed support) were in production for each named metric?
How should Cascadia’s March deploy vs December 2024 “using since,” HomeHop’s June 2025 vs “approximately two years,” and Bali founded-2025 vs using-since-December-2024 be reconciled?
Do index-only stories (BlueGems, 35-property 96% automation, Moxxi, Renjoy/Joy) have measurable bodies?
Is Lauderdale’s $500k an OM illustration, a completed sale, or only an 8% cap-rate model?

documents.markdown:
Buyers rarely start from a named vendor. They start from night-shift volume, a PMS inbox, a guest-journey suite, a corporate helpdesk, or a prototype on ChatGPT. This note compares those paths using only the supplied public pages. Conduit-authored competitor copy is Conduit’s argument, not a third-party bake-off. Related product detail: [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows), [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).

## Alternatives buyers consider

**Do nothing, spreadsheets, or a VA desk.** Conduit groups a VA team or spreadsheets as manual and one-off: they scale by headcount, context leaks when a thread hops apps, and the pager never sleeps. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/build-vs-buy) Ersona describes the same operating picture on Hostaway and Guesty: hundreds of weekly conversations across Airbnb, Booking.com, WhatsApp and email, VAs answering from templates without the booking in front of them, and field teams learning about requests late. [Source](https://ersona.co/solutions/vacation-rentals)

**PMS-native or PMS-inbox overlays.** Many STR operators already live in Hostaway, Guesty, or Airbnb threads. Ersona sits on Hostaway or Guesty, replies into the same conversation (including relayed OTA threads), can offer extras on a hosted checkout, create tasks for cleaners and maintenance, and open booking enquiries on the operator’s engine. It states it does not change reservations, rates, or calendars. [Source](https://ersona.co/solutions/vacation-rentals) ProhostAI connects to Airbnb, Hostaway, Hospitable, or Guesty inboxes and offers suggestion review or Autopilot. [Source](https://www.prohost.ai/messaging) Conduit Inbox says it brings SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social messages, and connected OTA threads into one workspace, with stay history and booking details from connected PMS and OTA accounts. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) What Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, or other PMS-native messaging can do *without* a third party is not in these sources.

**Hospitality point solutions / guest-journey suites.** Conduit’s product footers list Canary, Akia, Revinate, Duve, Volara, Enso Connect, Besty AI, HiJiffy, and Quicktext. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) Only Canary has a supplied Conduit alternative page. That page calls Canary a strong, broad guest-management suite (contactless check-in, upsells, digital tipping, messaging, AI Voice, Agent Studio) and positions Conduit as agentic infrastructure that writes back across systems. It also says Canary is a mature fit when a packaged enterprise guest-management suite is the primary need. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/alternatives/canary-technologies) Do not treat that page as independent evidence of Canary’s product.

**General helpdesks.** The same footers list Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, and Intercom. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) No capability comparison of those products appears in the supplied passages.

**Custom build or ChatGPT/Claude + Zapier.** Conduit’s landscape calls ChatGPT or Claude + Zapier broad but shallow: it drafts a reply, forgets SOPs, and cannot book a room, push a refund, or dispatch a contractor. In-house build is framed as deep but rigid, with every workflow its own engineering project. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/build-vs-buy)

**AI-native all-in-one STR PMS.** Jurny markets jOS powered by NIA as an all-in-one AI property management system: unified inbox across Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking and other channels, channel manager, reservations, housekeeping, branded guest web app (no download required), and specialized agents. That is a platform replacement, not an overlay. [Source](https://www.jurny.com/solutions/short-term-rentals)

| Class | Buyer intent in sources | Example | Tradeoff visible in public copy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Manual / VA | Cover volume with people | VA/spreadsheets; Ersona’s VA baseline | Scales with headcount; night coverage stays human |
| Overlay on current PMS | Keep PMS, add AI | Conduit; Ersona; ProhostAI | Write-back depth is vendor-specific |
| Guest-journey suite | Packaged check-in/upsell | Canary (Conduit’s description) | Suite modules vs claimed cross-system agent |
| All-in-one STR PMS | Collapse the stack | Jurny | Migration cost vs unified PMS |
| Helpdesk or DIY LLM | Reuse IT or engineers | Footer helpdesks; ChatGPT + Zapier | Hospitality actions not evidenced here |

## Decision criteria

Use these as discovery questions. Missing evidence means investigate, not reject. An integration name is not a supported action. A bundle is not a line-item price—see [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing).

| Criterion | Why it shows up in deals | Ask every vendor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Channels + history | Guests hop WhatsApp, SMS, email, voice, OTA | Which channels are live? Same conversation history? |
| Draft vs action | A good paragraph still needs a human to execute | Update booking, charge, create task—in which PMS? |
| Write-back limits | Overlay that cannot change a reservation still needs staff | Explicit read vs write list per connector |
| Escalation / review | Wrong auto-send is a brand incident | Holds, trainable review, who owns exceptions |
| Guest self-serve | FAQs and extras should not require a new app | One stay link: access, pay, upgrades, Q&A? |
| Ops after the message | Early check-in and broken heaters create work | Agent dispatch vs route-to-staff |
| Time-to-live and API drift | DIY hits WhatsApp/OTA/PMS change calendars | Who monitors connectors? |
| Proof definition | “Resolved” and “automation” are marketing words | Named properties, period, numerator/denominator |

Conduit Agents describe answering messages and calls with property information and reservation data, taking action through supported integrations (check bookings, reservation changes, payments, tasks), applying rules the operator sets, and escalating when needed. Channels listed: voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA messages with conversation history. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) Workflows add a visual builder for PMS-event messages, follow-ups, and conditional offers such as early check-in, gap nights, and room upgrades. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) Portals give guests one branded stay link (no app) for stay details, identity checks, agreements, fees, upgrades, access, and an AI concierge. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals)

## Conduit differentiators and evidence

**Observed Conduit product claims.** Purpose-built pages for short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups; agents that retrieve context and act in connected tools; unified inbox with human handoff; portals and workflows as separate products. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Build-vs-buy claims (Conduit-reported, not independently verified).** Time to live of days versus 6+ months and 3–5 engineers; hospitality context from 50M+ guest conversations; channels including WhatsApp, SMS, email, phone, Airbnb, Booking; named PMS connectors (Guesty, Hostaway, Mews, Cloudbeds, Opera…); action described as books, refunds, dispatches, upsells; 24/7, 140 languages, under a minute to first reply; SOC 2 Type II; 87% of guest messages resolved autonomously; 95% guest CSAT; 300+ hospitality brands; $3B+ reservation value influenced. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/build-vs-buy) The Canary comparison adds security language beyond the homepage’s SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA-workflow assertions. Confirm current attestations before repeating its HIPAA/GDPR/ISO certification language. It also claims 95% automation for Haven, while Haven’s own customer story says 90%; keep the conflicting 95% out of campaign proof. [Comparison](https://www.conduit.ai/alternatives/canary-technologies) [Haven story](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Homepage](https://www.conduit.ai/) Do not convert those figures into guarantees or all-customer outcomes. Usable proof lives in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

**Preserve a Conduit contradiction on operations.** Product navigation still lists Operations as coming soon: AI-coordinated housekeeping, maintenance and inspections. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) The Canary alternative page describes Conduit Ops as an internal layer the agent operates (housekeeping, maintenance, tasks, supplies, door locks). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/alternatives/canary-technologies) Do not tell a buyer Ops is generally available without current product confirmation. See [Operator & internal AI availability](#knowledge/product-operator).

**Versus suites (Conduit’s framing).** Conduit says the useful axis is an agent that reasons and acts across the stack versus templated flows inside one guest-experience surface, and that Canary remains appropriate for a packaged suite. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/alternatives/canary-technologies)

**Versus STR overlays (competitor pages).** Ersona’s own limit—no reservation, rate, or calendar changes—is a concrete contrast *if* Conduit’s “update bookings” claim is live for that PMS. [Source](https://ersona.co/solutions/vacation-rentals) ProhostAI’s messaging page emphasizes contextual drafts, Autopilot, confidence thresholds, and learning from history, not PMS write-back. [Source](https://www.prohost.ai/messaging) Versus Jurny, the decision is overlay on the current PMS versus adopting an AI-native PMS. [Source](https://www.jurny.com/solutions/short-term-rentals)

## Objections and honest responses

**“We’ll connect the PMS to ChatGPT.”** Conduit’s published answer is three walls: context (history, listings, SOPs, maintenance logs will not fit a prompt), action (a chatbot drafts; it cannot book or refund), and maintenance (APIs drift). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/build-vs-buy) Ask whether their prototype already updates a reservation and who owns WhatsApp/OTA breakage.

**“We have engineers.”** Conduit argues DIY rebuilds when the operation changes and competes with the real roadmap. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/build-vs-buy) Unique edge workflows may still need [Developer platform & custom workflows](#knowledge/product-developers). Engineering hours for *this* account are unknown.

**“Canary already has AI Voice and Agent Studio.”** Conduit’s page concedes the suite and differentiates on multi-step resolution across systems. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/alternatives/canary-technologies) Do not recite that as fact about Canary. Demo the same early check-in, refund, and 2am maintenance path on both products.

**“PMS Autopilot / our inbox is enough.”** If most volume is FAQ replies, an overlay that drafts or auto-sends may be enough. If the job includes booking changes, payments, and ops dispatch, demand a write-back matrix. Ersona is explicit that reservations stay in the PMS. [Source](https://ersona.co/solutions/vacation-rentals)

**“We’ll move to an all-in-one PMS.”** That is Jurny’s offer. [Source](https://www.jurny.com/solutions/short-term-rentals) Switching cost, hotel vs STR fit, and channel-manager lock-in are not quantified here.

**“We already own Zendesk / Service Cloud.”** Listed as alternatives only. These sources do not show live PMS context or hospitality actions in those helpdesks.

## Proof to request

Ask Conduit and any shortlisted alternative for the same artifacts: live channel list by property; read/write matrix per PMS and OTA; a recorded multi-step resolution (not a drafted reply); definition, period, and sample size for automation or CSAT; named references in the same segment; current security attestations; whether housekeeping/ops is GA or coming soon; and whether agents, inbox, portals, and workflows are one commercial bundle.

Draft evaluation script (not a claim of fit): run identical threads—policy FAQ, paid early check-in, refund, after-hours maintenance—on the current stack, Conduit, and one overlay or suite. Record who executed the PMS change and who spoke to the guest.

documents.title: Positioning & brand promise
documents.summary: Conduit’s observed public position is hospitality AI agents that answer guests, act in connected tools, and coordinate the work that follows—not a generic chatbot. This guide separates that language from a recommended buyer-facing promise, attaches named proof without treating it as a typical result, and lists claims that should stay out of guarantees.
documents.markdown:
## Core positioning

**Observed company language.** The shortest public line is “AI agents for hospitality.” The homepage expands it: answer guest messages and calls, handle requests end to end, and coordinate work across teams. The company page calls Conduit “the AI agent platform for hospitality”: a fleet of on-brand agents across every channel that convert inquiries into bookings, drive upsell revenue, run internal operations, and surface insights, connected to systems operators already use. The manifesto uses a sharper frame—“the coordination layer for hospitality”—an agent that works the same channels an operator does and acts on the business’s behalf instead of only shuttling messages. Industry nav is short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups. The product system behind that claim is [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), and [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows), with Operations labeled coming soon. Identity, founding-year, and brand-count conflicts belong in [Company overview](#knowledge/company-overview); capability packaging belongs in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/company) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto)

**Recommended articulation (draft, not a published slogan).** For a guest-operations buyer: Conduit is the hospitality-specific agent layer that answers guests on the channels they already use, takes the next step in connected tools, and hands exceptions to your team with the thread intact. Keep manifesto “coordination layer” language for thought leadership. Keep “AI agents for hospitality” for awareness. Do not invent a new category name.

## Promise and supporting pillars

**Observed promise.** Agents answer with property information and reservation data, act through connected tools (for example updating a booking, collecting payment, or creating a task), and escalate when a person is needed. Inbox brings messages and calls into one workspace with history. Portals give guests one branded stay link for arrival details, extras, payment, and an AI concierge. Workflows schedule confirmations, check-in, follow-ups, and rule-based upgrades. Homepage supporting claims include multilingual replies, inspectable agent activity, scheduled workflows, and reporting on automation rate, response time, resolution, and guest satisfaction. ## Why this work matters

The manifesto’s commercial argument is that hospitality already solved message speed; the bottleneck is how fast a person can absorb volume and act, especially after hours and across inboxes that do not talk to each other. documents.markdown:
# Brand voice & language

This is an inferred voice from public Conduit pages, product copy, the manifesto, customer stories, and LinkedIn ads—not a signed style guide. Pair it with [Positioning & brand promise](#knowledge/brand-messaging), [Company overview](#knowledge/company-overview), and [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence). Proposed lines below are **drafts**. Do not present them as published Conduit copy or as a relationship with a named prospect.

## Voice principles

**Write for the operator, not for “AI.”** Homepage and product pages open on guest messages, calls, bookings, handoffs, and procedures, then name the product. Industries on the same pages are short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/)

**Agents act, then people take the edges.** Product language is a relay, not a replacement slogan: agents answer and take action in connected tools; they escalate when needed; the inbox lets the team take over with history. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)

**The agent mirrors the operation.** The manifesto is the longest official voice: coordination layer, full context across channels, specialists stay, the middle shuttle role goes away—and a sloppy operation yields a sloppy agent. That is founder essay, denser than product UI copy; do not flatten it into a homepage guarantee. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto)

**Hospitality-specific, not generic desk software.** LinkedIn paid units contrast “AI agents built for hospitality” with generic chatbots and “human touch.” Use that contrast only as category language, not as a claim that every reply is indistinguishable from a host. [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1538690886) [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1538623406)

**Precision over borrowed superlatives.** Product blocks use numbered jobs and parallel verbs (answer, act, review). Scale lines conflict in public: homepage “300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries” versus a LinkedIn ad’s “1,000+ … in 120+ countries.” Attribute company reach; do not pick a number to sound bigger. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1538690886)

**Proof stays named.** Customer pages and ads retell Haven, Wynwood House, Cosmica, Lauderdale, and others with operator quotes and local numbers. Voice may be warmer there than on product FAQs; still keep the customer, metric, and caveat in one breath. See [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Vocabulary and sentence patterns

Observed pattern (public copy) → writing rule → **draft** example → avoid.

| Pattern in sources | Rule | Draft (not published copy) | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Two-beat imperatives: “Answer the question. Handle the request.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) | Lead with the guest job, then the system action. | Draft: Answer the WhatsApp. Update the reservation. | “Revolutionize hospitality with next-gen AI.” |
| Operator nouns: messages, calls, PMS, OTA threads, handoffs, procedures, knowledge base. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) | Prefer stay/ops vocabulary over SaaS abstractions. | Draft: One inbox for OTA threads and the night phone. | “Omnichannel synergy across the stack.” |
| Agent + team split: escalate when needed; team takes over when appropriate. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) | Name what the agent does *and* when a person steps in. | Draft: The agent handles the door-code thread; your night manager still owns the lockout. | “Fully autonomous hotel. No staff required.” |
| Channel list, then action: voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, connected OTAs. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) | List real channels; do not invent a channel the page does not name. | Draft: Same history on email, WhatsApp, and the call. | “We cover every app your guest might use.” |
| Manifesto scene: 1am leak → plumber on WhatsApp → owner digest. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto) | One concrete night, one sequence, no extra adjectives. | Draft: Guest reports a leak at 1am; the agent pages the on-call plumber and leaves a six-line note. | “Our AI magically orchestrates your entire estate.” |
| Founder ads: short data, then the operational ask (staff for peaks; agents in the plan). [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1538381626) | If you use volume, say it is Conduit-observed and dated in the ad, not a universal law. | Draft: Message load is not the same in every market; size coverage to the property, not the average. | “Guests everywhere send 2x the messages.” |

Keep sentences short on product and ads. The manifesto may run long, historical, and first-person (“-Punn and Cole”); that register is for essays, not pricing pages. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto)

Words that show up because they are on the site: agent, inbox, portal, workflow, guest, booking, property, procedure, escalation, handoff, coordinate, purpose-built. Words that rarely carry the homepage: chatbot (used mainly as a foil in ads), disrupt, magic, fire your team.

## Tone by situation

| Situation | Tone to match public examples | Draft (label as draft) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage / product | Calm, numbered, production. Book a demo, not a manifesto. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/) | Draft: Agents answer guests and take action in the tools you already run. |
| Manifesto / category essay | Historical, argumentative, still operational. Coordination tax, not “AI hype.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto) | Draft: The bottleneck is no longer how fast a message arrives. It is how fast someone can act on it. |
| Feature / integration announcement | Specific verbs and objects (read reservation, open a task). LinkedIn Mews/OPERA ads list actions; an integration logo is not a license to invent others. [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1502619576) | Draft: With the PMS connected, the agent can pull the live stay and open a maintenance task—confirm which writes your stack allows. |
| Customer proof | Named operator, local number, one story. Ads retell Wynwood’s guest resolution time (14–15 minutes → 3), which is different from first-response time without turning a 4.8 Colombia rating into a caused lift. [Source](https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/detail/1513892706) | Draft: Wynwood House’s published story is faster answers across seven countries—not a promise for every portfolio. |
| Human/automation | Cascadia’s quoted mission keeps boots-on-property and guest interaction human; AI is the rest. Haven’s story is teach-the-agent, not silent layoff copy. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) | Draft: If it needs someone on the property or in the room with the guest, it stays with your people. |

Product FAQs stay dry (“You provide policies… Agents combine that information with reservation data”). Match that dryness in implementation copy. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md)

## What to avoid

- **Guarantees from rhetoric.** “Build the perfect guest experience” is homepage marketing, not a SLA. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/)
- **Universal automation rates.** Manifesto 87% autonomous resolution and 95% CSAT are company-reported there; customer pages print different rates (Haven 90%, Cascadia 60%, HomeHop 70%). Do not average them. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/manifesto) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)
- **Staff-replacement punchlines** when the product page says escalate and take over. Easy BnB’s VA-replacement story, published on the Bali Luxury Stays page, is a named exit narrative; Bali Luxury Stays is the founder’s subsequent venture; Haven says nobody was laid off because of the AI. Keep those apart. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)
- **Generic chatbot / helpdesk voice** (ticket, CSAT widget, “your query is important”). Bocobay left Intercom for hospitality-shaped copy; do not sound like the tool they left. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)
- **Invented brand-count or channel coverage.** 300+ vs 1,000+ is unresolved. Do not add channels beyond those listed on product pages.
- **Unlabeled draft lines as if they ran on conduit.ai.** Campaign rules live in [Campaign writing examples & rules](#knowledge/writing-examples).

## Editing checklist

1. Is the first sentence a guest or ops job (message, call, booking, handoff), not “AI platform”? 
2. Did you name the human handoff if you named the agent? 
3. Are numbers attached to a named customer or clearly company-reported, with the source URL in the same block? 
4. Did you avoid blending manifesto metrics with homepage brand counts? 
5. Would a GM or STR ops lead recognize the nouns (property, PMS, OTA, procedure)? 
6. Is every original line marked **draft** until approved? 
7. For ads, did you keep hospitality-not-generic without claiming undetectable AI in every market? Wynwood’s “cannot tell the difference” is that operator’s quote, not a global proof point. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house)
open_questions: Is there an internal approved style guide, word list, or legal disclaimer set that should override these inferred patterns?
Which brand-count line (homepage 300+ vs LinkedIn ad 1,000+) is current for new copy?
When may manifesto metrics (87% resolution, 95% CSAT, 50M conversations) appear outside the manifesto?
How should voice differ for hotel-group vs STR campaigns given most named stories are STR/PM?

Manifesto scene: 1am leak → plumber on WhatsApp → owner digest. Source One concrete night, one sequence, no extra adjectives. Draft: Guest reports a leak at 1am; the agent pages the on-call plumber and leaves a six-line note. “Our AI magically orchestrates your entire estate.”
Founder ads: short data, then the operational ask (staff for peaks; agents in the plan). Source If you use volume, say it is Conduit-observed and dated in the ad, not a universal law. Draft: Message load is not the same in every market; size coverage to the property, not the average. “Guests everywhere send 2x the messages.”

Keep sentences short on product and ads. The manifesto may run long, historical, and first-person (“-Punn and Cole”); that register is for essays, not pricing pages. Source

Words that show up because they are on the site: agent, inbox, portal, workflow, guest, booking, property, procedure, escalation, handoff, coordinate, purpose-built. Words that rarely carry the homepage: chatbot (used mainly as a foil in ads), disrupt, magic, fire your team.

Tone by situation

Situation Tone to match public examples Draft (label as draft)
Homepage / product Calm, numbered, production. Book a demo, not a manifesto. Source Draft: Agents answer guests and take action in the tools you already run.
Manifesto / category essay Historical, argumentative, still operational. Coordination tax, not “AI hype.” Source Draft: The bottleneck is no longer how fast a message arrives. It is how fast someone can act on it.
Feature / integration announcement Specific verbs and objects (read reservation, open a task). LinkedIn Mews/OPERA ads list actions; an integration logo is not a license to invent others. Source Draft: With the PMS connected, the agent can pull the live stay and open a maintenance task—confirm which writes your stack allows.
Customer proof Named operator, local number, one story. Ads retell Wynwood’s guest resolution time (14–15 minutes → 3), which is different from first-response time without turning a 4.8 Colombia rating into a caused lift. Source Draft: Wynwood House’s published story is faster answers across seven countries—not a promise for every portfolio.
Human/automation Cascadia’s quoted mission keeps boots-on-property and guest interaction human; AI is the rest. Haven’s story is teach-the-agent, not silent layoff copy. Source Draft: If it needs someone on the property or in the room with the guest, it stays with your people.

Product FAQs stay dry (“You provide policies… Agents combine that information with reservation data”). Match that dryness in implementation copy. Source

What to avoid

  • Guarantees from rhetoric. “Build the perfect guest experience” is homepage marketing, not a SLA. Source
  • Universal automation rates. Manifesto 87% autonomous resolution and 95% CSAT are company-reported there; customer pages print different rates (Haven 90%, Cascadia 60%, HomeHop 70%). Do not average them. Source Source
  • Staff-replacement punchlines when the product page says escalate and take over. Easy BnB’s VA-replacement story, published on the Bali Luxury Stays page, is a named exit narrative; Bali Luxury Stays is the founder’s subsequent venture; Haven says nobody was laid off because of the AI. Keep those apart. Source Source
  • Generic chatbot / helpdesk voice (ticket, CSAT widget, “your query is important”). Bocobay left Intercom for hospitality-shaped copy; do not sound like the tool they left. Source
  • Invented brand-count or channel coverage. 300+ vs 1,000+ is unresolved. Do not add channels beyond those listed on product pages.
  • Unlabeled draft lines as if they ran on conduit.ai. Campaign rules live in Campaign writing examples & rules.

Editing checklist

  1. Is the first sentence a guest or ops job (message, call, booking, handoff), not “AI platform”?
  2. Did you name the human handoff if you named the agent?
  3. Are numbers attached to a named customer or clearly company-reported, with the source URL in the same block?
  4. Did you avoid blending manifesto metrics with homepage brand counts?
  5. Would a GM or STR ops lead recognize the nouns (property, PMS, OTA, procedure)?
  6. Is every original line marked draft until approved?
  7. For ads, did you keep hospitality-not-generic without claiming undetectable AI in every market? Wynwood’s “cannot tell the difference” is that operator’s quote, not a global proof point. Source

documents.title: Audience-to-message map
documents.summary: This map turns Conduit’s public Agents, Inbox, Portals, and Workflows claims into situation → capability → named-proof → next-action rows for independent hotels, hotel groups, and short-term rental operators. Figures stay attached to a single attributed story; industry-page copy is not treated as a tested campaign winner, and personalization is limited to evidence on the target account.
documents.markdown:
This map is for humans and ABM agents choosing what to say, not a guarantee of conversion. Capabilities come from [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities). Numbers come only from named pages in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence) and are Conduit-attributed, not independently verified. Industry landing pages are positioning, not performance-tested ads.

## Message hierarchy

**What the product pages say they do:** [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) answer guest messages and calls using property information and reservation data, take actions in connected tools (for example creating a task or updating a booking), and pass requests to the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**How the work is split:** [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) is the workspace for messages, calls, and handoffs with booking context beside the thread. [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) send confirmations, check-in and checkout messages, follow-ups, and rule-based add-ons. [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) give guests one branded stay link for details, extras, payments, and in-portal questions. Operations (housekeeping, maintenance, inspections) is labeled coming soon in the product nav. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Published audience:** short-term rentals, independent hotels and hotel groups are the main landing-page groups. Serviced apartments are also explicitly named, and resorts/villas/aparthotels may fit the guest-stay operating model. Navigation labels are not a closed qualification list. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Copy ladder:** the operator’s current situation → the named product that matches the job → what happens with *their* connected tools (only if research supports the connection) → **one** matching customer result with date and caveat → book a demo. Do not lead with G2 4.7/5 widget copy, “perfect guest experience,” or a blended automation rate.

Voice and tone belong in [Brand voice & language](#knowledge/brand-voice); the promise frame belongs in [Positioning & brand promise](#knowledge/brand-messaging).

## Messages by buying situation

Keep the customer name, printed window, and caveat in the same sentence as any figure. Do not average rows.

| Situation | Problem | Capability → claimed value | Specific proof (attributed) | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Independent hotel covering nights while staff work the desk | After-hours calls, late check-in, in-stay requests | Agents use hotel policies and booking details including after hours; Inbox for takeover; workflows/offers for extras such as room upgrades, spa, dining | The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel (using Conduit since Dec 2024): support $4,000→$600/mo; avg reply 57 min→2 min; the story also describes an intermediate $1,200 provider and a 24/7 staffed support team. The owner models ≥$3,400/mo NOI and >$500k at an 8% cap—not an appraisal, closed sale or Agents-only result | Demo after-hours voice + which PMS they actually run (page examples: Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds—not proof of identical write-back) |
| Hotel group | Shared brand, different policies and reservations per property | One workspace; shared brand standards and knowledge; agents use brand voice plus each property’s information; loyalty, upgrades, spa/dining explanations | No named hotel-group case body in this pack—do not borrow STR percentages | Demo parent/child listings, shared KB, and per-property PMS |
| STR operator adding listings | Volume scales with units; split OTA inboxes; overnight lockouts | Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, email, SMS, and calls in one workspace; per-listing knowledge + live PMS; scheduled stay messages; gap-night and add-on workflows | Haven (since Feb 2024): 90% automation across ~270 properties, up from ~40% with few workflows; support need ~25 people → two per shift; scores held 4.8–4.9. HomeHop: ~40→108 listings and 70% automation in its story; the stated growth period and customer-since date disagree, so the full growth cannot be attributed to a verified deployment window; voice 1–7 AM | Demo OTA+PMS inbox, listing KB, overnight voice |

Independent hotels: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels). Hotel groups: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups). STR: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals). Lauderdale: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel). Haven: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026). HomeHop: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop).

Use a second STR story only when the account’s situation matches: Cascadia’s first PM acquisition (60% automation and 4.9 communication score across 100 properties); Bocobay leaving Intercom for one inbox; Cosmica Italy/Dubai without expanding support; Canbnb ~1,500 messages sent/week with 60% handled by AI; that send-volume denominator is not interchangeable with another customer’s resolution metric. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cosmica) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb)

Segment research stays in [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels) and [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals).

## Role-specific emphasis

Do not invent buying attitudes. Emphasize jobs that appear in product pages or named stories. Committee shape is in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles).

| Role in sources | Lead with | Proof that can sit next to it | Do not stretch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Owner / founder (Lauderdale, Cosmica, Bali, Flex) | Coverage without living in Slack; labor vs growth; NOI or exit math | Lauderdale cap-rate model; Easy BnB ~$22k/mo labor, 75 units, 0 extra FTE, reported on the Bali Luxury Stays page | Combining Easy BnB (11 VAs replaced) with Haven (nobody laid off because of AI) |
| Guest services / CX (Haven’s Jonathan; Cascadia’s Ryan; Wynwood’s Mayra) | One inbox, history on handoff, quality while automating | Wynwood resolution 14–15 min → 3 min; Cascadia communication score locked at 4.9 | Treating “you cannot tell the difference” as a universal guest outcome |
| Ops / process owner (Canbnb’s Jo-Anne) | Property/team views, guest/owner/vendor inboxes, workflows | Canbnb’s structured inboxes and ~60% of ~1,500 weekly messages | Selling Operations (coming soon) as live housekeeping-at-scale |

Hotel-group cluster and revenue titles on the group page (multi-property operations, room upgrades, direct booking) are demo topics, not proven role outcomes. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

## Offer and call to action

Public product and industry pages use **Book a demo**, not a self-serve checkout. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Draft CTA (not a live campaign, not a claimed relationship): “See how agents would answer after-hours calls for this property and pass exceptions into one inbox.” Name the product that matches the job—Inbox+Agents for omnichannel takeover, Agents for voice, Portals for pre-arrival/waivers/upsells, Workflows for dated sequences. Confirm package coverage in [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing); a bundle rate is not a standalone Agents or Portals price.

Do not offer Operations as generally available. Do not invent a Portals standalone price in outbound copy.

## Proof and personalization boundaries

**Allowed:** the prospect’s industry label as Conduit names it; PMS or channels confirmed in account research *and* listed as supported; **one** matching story with printed dates. An integration logo is not evidence of a supported action—see [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).

**Not allowed:** invented partnerships or pains; averaging Haven 90%, Cascadia 60%, HomeHop 70%, Canbnb 60%, and Flex 70%/90%; presenting Lauderdale’s $500k as appraised or sold value; using Guest Favorite share or G2 stars as Conduit KPIs; implying [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) or Operations produced these results (stories name the platform, not those SKUs).

**Keep contradictions visible:** Haven About 230+ vs ~270 properties and 59% vs 55% Guest Favorite; Flex title 70% vs header 90%; HomeHop June 2025 vs “approximately two years”; Bali founded 2025 vs using Conduit since Dec 2024. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays)

Campaign sentences: [Campaign writing examples & rules](#knowledge/writing-examples).
open_questions: Which named hotel-group story, if any, can sit in group-targeted copy given this pack has no group case body?
Which automation denominator (messages, support volume, guest communication) should outbound use when stories disagree?
When, if ever, should Portals or Operations appear in a proof-led CTA before a story isolates them?
How should staffing claims be phrased when Haven reports no AI layoffs and Bali reports replacing eleven VAs?

documents.title: Campaign writing examples & rules
documents.summary: Proposed, labeled drafts for a hotel motion, a vacation-rental motion, and a technical-evaluator follow-up, each limited to published product actions and optional single-account proof. Copy rules forbid invented prospect pain, averaged automation rates, fabricated trials, and stretching named results beyond the story that printed them.
documents.markdown:
These blocks are **proposed drafts** for humans and ABM agents. They are not live campaigns, not customer-approved quotes, and not evidence that a named prospect has a problem. Pair every claim with [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence) and the product that actually performs the job in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities). Do not invent an offer, trial, SLA, or typical automation rate. Site CTAs are to book a demo. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

## How to use these examples

Run one buying situation per motion. Keep headline, support, opener, and invitation inside the same product family ([AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows)). Name a customer only when the published story matches the motion, and keep the account, time window, and caveat in the same sentence as any number. Voice and promise: [Brand voice & language](#knowledge/brand-voice), [Positioning & brand promise](#knowledge/brand-messaging). Segment notes: [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels), [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals).

| Piece | Job | Allowed sources | Stop if missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headline | Name the product action | Product or industry page | Invented pain (“your night desk is drowning”) |
| Support | One capability + optional named proof | Product FAQ + one case page | Averaged % across accounts |
| Email opener | Why this account, from research | Public stack, channels, segment | Assumed refunds, hiring freeze, or scores |
| Discovery invitation | Ask for a demo conversation | “Book a demo” on product pages | Fabricated trial, credits, or discount |

Target evidence before send: property type (independent hotel, group, or short-term rental), channels in use, PMS/OTA names if public, and whether voice or stay-link portals are in scope. If those are unknown, investigate—do not invent persona fiction.

## Hotel campaign

Situation: independent or boutique hotel evaluating guest calls and messages, not a hotel-group operations RFP. Published language: agents answer guest calls and messages using the hotel’s policies and booking details, including after hours, and pass requests when a person is needed. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

**Proposed headline (draft):** After-hours guest calls and messages, answered with your hotel’s policies.

**Proposed support (draft):** Conduit agents handle voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA threads, use reservation data to act in connected tools, and escalate with history in Inbox. Independent-hotel pages also describe extras such as room upgrades, spa, and dining. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

**Proposed email opener (draft):** Writing because you operate an independent hotel with guest contact on phone and messaging. Conduit is built for hotel teams to answer those channels with property information and booking details, then hand off when the desk should take over.

**Proposed discovery invitation (draft):** If useful, we can demo agents plus inbox against your channels and PMS. This note does not attach a trial. The public next step is to book a demo. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

Why it works: it restates published capabilities instead of diagnosing the prospect. The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel write-up may be cited only as a named, Conduit-attributed story (the cost path includes $4,000, an intermediate $1,200 provider, and $600/month with the described AI platform and 24/7 staffed support team; not an Agents-only result; average reply 57 minutes to 2 minutes; owner-modeled ≥$3,400 monthly NOI and more than $500,000 asset value at an 8% cap rate)—not as this hotel’s outcome. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

Target evidence: hotel vs rental, whether Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, or another PMS is actually in use, whether voice is in scope, and whether extras offers matter. Do not attribute Lauderdale’s figures to Portals; that page describes an AI support platform and 24/7 staffed support team.

## Vacation-rental campaign

Situation: short-term rental or property manager on OTAs plus direct channels. Published language: answer guest messages, send check-in instructions, and handle booking-change requests using details for each property; the team takes over when needed. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals)

**Proposed headline (draft):** Guest messages, check-in instructions, and booking changes—per listing.

**Proposed support (draft):** Bring Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, email, SMS, and calls into one workspace; combine PMS reservation data with a property knowledge base. Workflows can schedule confirmations, check-in instructions, and follow-ups from PMS events and stay dates. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)

**Proposed email opener (draft):** Reaching operators who already run listings across OTAs and direct messages. Conduit puts those threads in one inbox and lets agents use the listing the guest booked.

**Proposed discovery invitation (draft):** Happy to demo agents, inbox, and stay-dated workflows on your connected accounts. No packaged offer in this note.

Why it works: STR copy stays on channels and per-property knowledge, which the industry page claims. Named proof is optional and single-account: Haven Vacation Rentals (using Conduit since February 2024) is written as reaching 90 percent automation across roughly 270 properties, up from about 40 percent, with support need described as falling from around 25 people to two per shift—company-attributed, not a benchmark. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) HomeHop’s reported 40-to-108 listing growth and 70 percent automation are a separate story; its June 2025 customer-since header and “approximately two years” narrative conflict, so do not attribute the entire growth window to Conduit; do not blend rates. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop)

Target evidence: public PMS/OTA names, whether overnight voice is in scope, and the motion (scale, acquisition, or inbox unification). Bocobay is usable only for leaving Intercom / unifying channels—not as a typical resolution rate. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)

## Technical evaluator follow-up

Audience: someone asking how it works, not a new demand-gen hook.

**Proposed subject (draft):** Channels, PMS context, actions, and the rules you set

**Proposed body (draft):** An AI agent answers guest messages and calls using property information and reservation data, can take actions through connected tools (for example creating a task or updating a booking), and passes requests to the team. How to use these examples
