documents.title: ICP strategy & segment priorities
documents.summary: Conduit’s published ICP is hospitality stay operators—hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers—not a job-title list. Named proof is strongest for vacation-rental managers, thinner for independent hotels, and still a marketing claim for hotel groups; unit, employee, and revenue cutoffs are not fit gates.
documents.markdown:
Conduit’s public ICP is a hospitality **account**, not a jobs list. The pricing FAQ says Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, with AI agents that answer guest messages and calls, handle routine requests, and coordinate work with the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Global navigation names three industries in this order: short-term rentals, independent hotels, hotel groups. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Fit** means the company operates guest stays, can supply property-specific policies and reservation context, and runs conversations on channels Conduit unifies, with humans for handoffs. A motivated buyer outside that operating model does not create fit. Investigation priority follows evidence strength in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence), not invented market size: named stories cluster in vacation-rental / property-management companies; independent hotels have one boutique P&L write-up plus an industry page; hotel groups have product copy without a named group case body in this pack; serviced apartments are named in the FAQ only.

## Who is a good-fit account

A good-fit account is an operator of stays whose guest work is communication-heavy and **property-specific**. Agents use the operator’s property information and policies, act through supported connected tools, and follow rules for what the team should handle. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) Inbox assumes conversations can be organized by property or team, with stay and booking context from connected PMS and OTA accounts beside the thread. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)

Hotels and vacation-rental operators are both in-category and **not the same test**. Independent-hotel pages stress after-hours calls, front-desk load, Opera / Mews / Cloudbeds, and extras such as room upgrades, spa, and dining. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels) Short-term rental pages stress per-listing knowledge, Airbnb / Vrbo / Booking.com / Expedia threads, check-in instructions, and booking-change requests. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals) Hotel-group pages add shared brand standards with per-property policies and reservation details. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups) Run [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels) and [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals) as separate account tests. Serviced-apartment operators belong in the same FAQ sentence; investigate them as in-category until disproven—do not reject for a missing named story.

Company reach copy (“300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries”) is a Conduit claim, not named-account proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

## Priority buying situations

These are situations that appear in named stories or industry pages. They are research prompts, not needs every customer has.

| Situation observed | Where it shows up | Why it is investigable | Evidence strength |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guest volume growing faster than support headcount | STR / PM companies | Haven and HomeHop describe scale without proportional guest-support hiring; Canbnb separately describes message volume and AI handling, not a proven flat-headcount result | Strong named STR stories |
| Overnight / after-hours coverage | Hotels and STR | Independent-hotel after-hours receptionist; HomeHop voice coverage 1–7 AM | Industry page + named STR story |
| Split inboxes or generic helpdesk misfit | Luxury PM | Bocobay left Intercom to unify WhatsApp, email, phone, and live chat | One named migration |
| Acquisition or multi-market expansion without a new comms team | STR / multi-country | Cascadia’s first PM acquisition; Cosmica Italy/Dubai; Wynwood seven countries | Strong STR / CX stories |
| Owner wants leaner or more passive operations | Boutique hotel | Lauderdale replaced a call-center model and reports support-cost and NOI changes | One hotel story |

Do not treat 90% automation, modeled asset value, or any single automation rate as a qualification bar. Those figures stay attributed in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Company characteristics

No public source sets employee, revenue, or unit-count **fit gates**. Pricing publishes commercial bands only: Startup for 0–25 units, per-unit packages “from independent teams to enterprise,” and starting rates that scale beyond 50 listings. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) A small portfolio can be commercially eligible; a ~270-property manager can be a named customer. Neither is a necessary ICP cutoff.

| Characteristic | What sources show | Fit implication | Still unknown |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Industry | Hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, STR managers | Primary in-category test | Resorts, villas, aparthotels appear as marketing links, not a defined ICP |
| Ownership vs management | Owner-operator hotel (Lauderdale); PM brands managing listings (Haven, Cascadia, HomeHop, Canbnb, Bocobay) | Contracting party may be owner or manager | Franchise vs brand vs asset manager not specified |
| Geography / language | Company claim of 120+ countries; named stories in the US, Australia, Italy, Dubai, Caribbean, Latin America/Europe, Bali, London/SF | Geography is not a published exclusion | Multilingual replies are marketed, but required-language quality and channel coverage must be confirmed for the actual workflow |
| Portfolio complexity | Inbox views by property or team; hotel-group shared KB; STR per-listing KB | Multi-property / multi-listing is how the product is demonstrated | No required property count |
| Systems | Hotel examples Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds; STR examples Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, Airbnb | Check live connectors in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations) | A logo is not proof of a supported agent action |

## Buyer roles versus company fit

Company fit is the lodging model and guest-operations stack. Buyer roles are how that account buys and runs the product. Founders, CEOs, guest-services leads, and CX heads appear in stories; those titles are not the ICP. Map influence in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles). If the company does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental stays, a strong champion does not create fit. If the company is in-category, a missing named persona is a research gap, not a reject.

## Readiness and urgency

Readiness the sources actually describe: connected channels and PMS/OTA context; a knowledge base of property policies; escalation rules; people who review handoffs. Haven’s story says Conduit was already installed at about 40% automation with listings uploaded, no workflows, and minimal knowledge-base work until the team standardized answers. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) Docs-style product FAQ copy says how much agents resolve depends on guest requests, knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md)

Urgency is not a published score. Named stories involve growth, staffing, acquisitions, overnight coverage, and owner valuation. Test whether those situations exist with [Qualification & account research playbook](#knowledge/buying-triggers). Do not invent a buying attitude or timeline. Package choice (Messaging vs Guest vs devices vs Full Suite) is commercial mapping in [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) after the account is in-category. Capabilities live in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities).

## Exclusions and unknowns

Sources do not publish a negative ICP. Do not reject for unknown unit count, missing hotel-group proof, or an integration that is only a logo—investigate.

The practical out-of-category signal is an account that does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays. That follows the FAQ; it is not a legal exclusion list. Hybrid real-estate-plus-hospitality operators that still run guest stays (Wynwood) remain in-category.

Material gaps: named proof for hotel groups and serviced apartments; whether “unit” equals listing, room, or key; franchise buying units; language product limits; whether Operations (nav: coming soon) is required for group ops use cases. Preserve the contradiction that Full Suite already lists workforce/operations lines while the product nav still says Operations is coming soon. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

## What the company must confirm

Before treating segments as equally proven, confirm: hotel-group and serviced-apartment referenceability; billable unit vs listing vs room; which PMS/OTA paths actually write bookings, tasks, or payments for this stack; which required guest languages and channels are supported at the needed quality; and whether the contracting party is owner, management company, or brand. Until then, prioritize STR/PM investigation, keep independent hotels in-category with thinner proof, and treat hotel groups as marketed but under-evidenced.
open_questions: Is there named, body-complete proof for hotel groups comparable to STR stories?
Which serviced-apartment operators are referenceable, and how do they differ from hotels and STRs in buying unit?
Does Conduit bill a unit as a listing, room, key, or something else—and is that ever a fit rule or only packaging?
Who contracts—owner, management company, franchisee, or brand—and does that change qualification?
Which languages and locales are product-supported versus outcomes reported only in the Wynwood story?

icp_criteria.criterion: Account operates hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays
icp_criteria.rationale: The pricing FAQ names these three operator types as who Conduit is for.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm lodging model from the company site, OTA/PMS presence, and match to independent-hotel, hotel-group, or short-term rental industry pages.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If the noun is adjacent (resort, villa, aparthotel, hybrid real-estate hospitality), investigate against industry pages; do not reject solely because the FAQ used a different label.

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest conversations can use a confirmed Conduit channel path
icp_criteria.rationale: A supported channel path enables the intended workflow; property/team views are product capabilities, not a minimum portfolio-size rule.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Identify actual guest channels and confirm their connection path. Single-property and multi-property operators can both qualify.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Research unknown channels. Do not reject a single-property operator or an account whose current inbox is not segmented.

icp_criteria.criterion: Vacation-rental or short-term rental management company
icp_criteria.rationale: Named customer stories with operating detail cluster in STR/PM companies; industry page exists for this segment.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm STR listings, channel mix, and management vs owner-operator model; use the vacation-rental ICP doc for the deeper test.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If hybrid hotel-plus-rental, score both hotel and rental tests separately.

icp_criteria.criterion: Independent or boutique hotel operator
icp_criteria.rationale: Independent hotels are a named industry; Lauderdale is the named hotel P&L story in this pack.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm hotel (not only STR) operations, front-desk/after-hours load, and hotel-oriented PMS names such as Opera, Mews, or Cloudbeds.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Thin named proof is a proof gap, not a reason to mark the account out-of-category.

icp_criteria.criterion: Hotel group with shared brand standards and per-property policies
icp_criteria.rationale: Hotel-group pages market multi-property brand standards, but this source pack has no named hotel-group case body.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm multiple hotels, shared vs local procedures, and group vs property buying unit.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Treat as marketed in-category; do not assume conversion or outcomes equal STR stories until references exist.

icp_criteria.criterion: Connected PMS or OTA that can supply reservation/listing context
icp_criteria.rationale: Agents and inbox claims depend on property information, reservation data, and connected tools; connector depth varies.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Name the PMS/OTA and check it against the integrations guide; confirm messaging vs reservation-data-only path.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Unknown stack is investigate, not reject. A logo is not evidence of write-back.

icp_criteria.criterion: Capacity to document property policies and set escalation rules
icp_criteria.rationale: Haven was installed at ~40% automation until knowledge-base and workflow work; agent resolution is described as depending on knowledge, integrations, and rules.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask whether listings/policies are documented, who owns the knowledge base, and what must stay human.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Low current documentation is a readiness gap, not automatic unfit.

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest-support volume, after-hours coverage, or call-center cost creating a live operating pressure
icp_criteria.rationale: Named stories involve headcount, overnight coverage, acquisitions, and call-center replacement; none of these is stated as a required trigger.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask how nights, peaks, and current support vendors are staffed; record dates and vendors.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Missing urgency does not fail fit; log it for sequencing only.

icp_criteria.criterion: Business that does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays
icp_criteria.rationale: Published industries and the who-is-for FAQ are hospitality stay operators; no source targets other verticals.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: If the company has no guest-stay inventory or guest-communication operation, mark out-of-category.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Hybrids that still run guest stays remain in-category pending investigation.

Serviced-apartment operators belong in the same FAQ sentence; investigate them as in-category until disproven—do not reject for a missing named story.

Company reach copy (“300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries”) is a Conduit claim, not named-account proof. Source

Priority buying situations

These are situations that appear in named stories or industry pages. They are research prompts, not needs every customer has.

Situation observed Where it shows up Why it is investigable Evidence strength
Guest volume growing faster than support headcount STR / PM companies Haven and HomeHop describe scale without proportional guest-support hiring; Canbnb separately describes message volume and AI handling, not a proven flat-headcount result Strong named STR stories
Overnight / after-hours coverage Hotels and STR Independent-hotel after-hours receptionist; HomeHop voice coverage 1–7 AM Industry page + named STR story
Split inboxes or generic helpdesk misfit Luxury PM Bocobay left Intercom to unify WhatsApp, email, phone, and live chat One named migration
Acquisition or multi-market expansion without a new comms team STR / multi-country Cascadia’s first PM acquisition; Cosmica Italy/Dubai; Wynwood seven countries Strong STR / CX stories
Owner wants leaner or more passive operations Boutique hotel Lauderdale replaced a call-center model and reports support-cost and NOI changes One hotel story

Do not treat 90% automation, modeled asset value, or any single automation rate as a qualification bar. Those figures stay attributed in Customer evidence & usable proof.

Company characteristics

No public source sets employee, revenue, or unit-count fit gates. Pricing publishes commercial bands only: Startup for 0–25 units, per-unit packages “from independent teams to enterprise,” and starting rates that scale beyond 50 listings. Source A small portfolio can be commercially eligible; a ~270-property manager can be a named customer. Neither is a necessary ICP cutoff.

Characteristic What sources show Fit implication Still unknown
Industry Hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, STR managers Primary in-category test Resorts, villas, aparthotels appear as marketing links, not a defined ICP
Ownership vs management Owner-operator hotel (Lauderdale); PM brands managing listings (Haven, Cascadia, HomeHop, Canbnb, Bocobay) Contracting party may be owner or manager Franchise vs brand vs asset manager not specified
Geography / language Company claim of 120+ countries; named stories in the US, Australia, Italy, Dubai, Caribbean, Latin America/Europe, Bali, London/SF Geography is not a published exclusion Multilingual replies are marketed, but required-language quality and channel coverage must be confirmed for the actual workflow
Portfolio complexity Inbox views by property or team; hotel-group shared KB; STR per-listing KB Multi-property / multi-listing is how the product is demonstrated No required property count
Systems Hotel examples Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds; STR examples Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, Airbnb Check live connectors in Integrations & implementation readiness A logo is not proof of a supported agent action

Buyer roles versus company fit

Company fit is the lodging model and guest-operations stack. Buyer roles are how that account buys and runs the product. Founders, CEOs, guest-services leads, and CX heads appear in stories; those titles are not the ICP. Map influence in Buying committee & professional personas. If the company does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental stays, a strong champion does not create fit. If the company is in-category, a missing named persona is a research gap, not a reject.

Readiness and urgency

Readiness the sources actually describe: connected channels and PMS/OTA context; a knowledge base of property policies; escalation rules; people who review handoffs. Haven’s story says Conduit was already installed at about 40% automation with listings uploaded, no workflows, and minimal knowledge-base work until the team standardized answers. Source Docs-style product FAQ copy says how much agents resolve depends on guest requests, knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules. Source

Urgency is not a published score. Named stories involve growth, staffing, acquisitions, overnight coverage, and owner valuation. Test whether those situations exist with Qualification & account research playbook. Do not invent a buying attitude or timeline. Package choice (Messaging vs Guest vs devices vs Full Suite) is commercial mapping in Pricing & packaging after the account is in-category. Capabilities live in Product catalog & capability map.

Exclusions and unknowns

Sources do not publish a negative ICP. Do not reject for unknown unit count, missing hotel-group proof, or an integration that is only a logo—investigate.

The practical out-of-category signal is an account that does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays. That follows the FAQ; it is not a legal exclusion list. Hybrid real-estate-plus-hospitality operators that still run guest stays (Wynwood) remain in-category.

Material gaps: named proof for hotel groups and serviced apartments; whether “unit” equals listing, room, or key; franchise buying units; language product limits; whether Operations (nav: coming soon) is required for group ops use cases. Preserve the contradiction that Full Suite already lists workforce/operations lines while the product nav still says Operations is coming soon. Source

What the company must confirm

Before treating segments as equally proven, confirm: hotel-group and serviced-apartment referenceability; billable unit vs listing vs room; which PMS/OTA paths actually write bookings, tasks, or payments for this stack; which required guest languages and channels are supported at the needed quality; and whether the contracting party is owner, management company, or brand. Until then, prioritize STR/PM investigation, keep independent hotels in-category with thinner proof, and treat hotel groups as marketed but under-evidenced.

documents.title: ICP · hotel operators
documents.summary: Hotel operators are two marketed subsegments—independent hotels and hotel groups—defined by guest communication, property or group knowledge, and PMS context, not a generic hospitality label. Public proof in this pack is one boutique owner-operator story; group-scale outcomes and operations-led purchases remain investigate-not-reject gaps.
documents.markdown:
Treat hotel operators as two site industries—**Independent Hotels** and **Hotel Groups**—not one vague hospitality ICP. Short-term rentals are a separate segment; use [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals) and do not import STR automation rates as hotel proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

FAQs state Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, with agents answering guest messages and calls, handling routine requests, and coordinating with the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

## Account definition

**Independent hotels** are marketed as property-level guest operations: agents answer calls and messages while the team looks after people at the desk, using that hotel’s policies and booking details, including after hours. The buying locus in the copy is the desk—front office, reservations, overnight cover—not a corporate shared-services org. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

**Hotel groups** are marketed as a portfolio workspace: handle messages and calls across the group, share brand standards, and still give agents each property’s policies and reservation details (parent + child listings, shared knowledge base, org structure). Calls are described as landing in a shared inbox. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

A site claim of being trusted by 300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries is company reach language, not named hotel-group adoption. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

The only named **hotel** customer body in this pack is The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel (using Conduit since December 2024; founder Noel Poler). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

## Best-fit operating situations

Fit is a communication-and-action job around the stay, not “unattended hotel.” Product pages describe answering across voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA threads; acting through supported tools; escalating with history. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

| Operating load | Independent Hotels page | Hotel Groups page | Surface |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Night / late arrival / in-stay | After-hours receptionist; overnight cover; late check-in | Voice + omnichannel; calls in shared inbox | [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) |
| Desk volume and handoffs | Always-on front desk | Omnichannel inbox; multi-property conversations | [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) |
| Extras during the stay | Room upgrades, spa, dining | Loyalty/perks, upgrades, spa and dining | [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows); [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) is a package/workflow option to investigate, not a proven hotel case outcome |
| Consistency | One hotel’s brand voice | Shared brand voice plus property knowledge | Inbox views by property or team |

Lauderdale’s attributed pattern is an owner replacing inconsistent call-center models (costs cited from $4,000 down to $1,200, then Conduit at $600/month) with an “AI-powered support platform and 24/7 staffed support team,” faster replies, fewer refunds, and NOI/cap-rate math. That is one boutique, hands-off-investment story—not a typical hotel outcome. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

**Scenario A — good-fit (hypothetical, unlabeled property):** A single independent hotel whose night team still takes late-arrival calls and WhatsApp, and a GM willing to maintain property policies. Opera or Mews would be readiness examples to investigate, not mandatory fit criteria. The job is coverage plus reservation context, not removing the desk.

**Scenario B — uncertain (hypothetical):** A group whose RFP requires labor/payroll or portfolio housekeeping as the must-have needs feature-level availability confirmation. An enterprise guest-CRM, loyalty or shared-inbox requirement is a different discovery path and must not be treated as the same coming-soon Operations question. Investigate whether live need is guest communication. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Scenario C — poor-fit (hypothetical):** A buyer who needs a physical self-check-in kiosk. Group copy: Conduit supports guest communication; it is not a physical check-in kiosk. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

## Company and technology profile

No public room-count, flag, or chain-scale cutoff. Commercial packaging is per unit per month with starting rates, scaling beyond 50 listings; 0–25 units has a Startup full-feature monthly price. Map packages in a sales conversation rather than treating a bundle rate as an Agents-only price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Hotel industry pages name Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, Apaleo, RMS Cloud, StayNTouch, Booking.com, Expedia, WhatsApp, and email; the hotel-groups stack card also lists Salesforce. Inbox examples include Mews + Opera beside the thread. A logo is not evidence of reservation write-back—confirm path in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

Agents combine a configurable knowledge base with reservation data; they can check bookings, change reservations, and create tasks only through supported integrations, then pass work the team should handle. How much they resolve “on their own” is explicitly dependent on requests, knowledge, integrations, and rules—not a hotel SLA. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md)

## Buying committee

Sources do not publish a hotel RACI. What is observable:

- **Independent / boutique:** founder or owner plus lean on-property oversight (Lauderdale: founder; part-time property manager after go-live). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)
- **Groups:** marketing implies a central brand/knowledge owner and property teams; maintenance use-case copy mentions cluster managers seeing open work—page language, not a named org chart. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

Day-to-day users of [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) are front desk, reservations, and guest services (property or team views, round-robin or custom assignment, human takeover). PMS/IT owners matter for Opera-class connections. Role detail lives in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles).

## Qualification decisions

Qualify **subsegment → communication job → stack → package → proof**, in that order.

1. Independent hotel vs hotel group vs mis-tagged STR or serviced apartment.
2. Buying locus: one desk and one policy set vs shared standards plus per-property exceptions.
3. Channels: voice and messaging in one workspace; confirm each OTA’s actual messaging versus reservation-context path. The integration directory has coming-soon labels, while other public pages describe OTA messaging; resolve that conflict for this account. [Integration directory](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)
4. Package vs job: Messaging vs Guest (portals, waivers, upsells) vs devices vs Full Suite—see [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) and [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities).
5. Proof match: cite Lauderdale only for boutique owner-operator support cost, response time, and modeled asset value, with Conduit attribution and cap-rate caveats. No hotel-group case body is in this pack. Missing group proof means investigate, not reject. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

## Signals and next questions

Useful public signals: hotel (not listing) inventory; night phone plus OTA/WhatsApp; PMS names that appear on hotel pages; one GM vs brand standards team. None of these are numeric thresholds.

Ask: Which system is source of truth for reservations, and should guest messaging stay on the PMS? Who owns brand voice versus property exceptions? Which requests must still hit a person at the desk? Is the purchase guest communication, or housekeeping/labor still marked coming soon?

## Disqualifiers and unresolved assumptions

A physical check-in kiosk as the required deliverable is a product mismatch. Operational requirements such as housekeeping or workforce management require feature-level confirmation: navigation says Operations is coming soon while Full Suite lists operational capabilities. That conflict is a readiness question, not an automatic rejection of the hotel account. Separately, transferring STR percentages to hotels or assuming all PMS connectors support the same writes are sales errors, not negative ICP criteria. [Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Unresolved in sources: no named hotel-group outcomes; Lauderdale’s $600/month and 2-minute average mix AI with a staffed support team, so the human share is not isolated; Guest includes portals at a published starting package rate, while the Portals FAQ also describes a listing-based add-on; confirm the applicable commercial path. No Portals outcome is isolated in the hotel story; implementation effort for hotels is not published here. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)
open_questions: Is there a named hotel-group customer with documented outcomes, or only industry-page use cases?
For Lauderdale, what mix of AI agents versus 24/7 staffed support produced the $600/month and 2-minute response figures?
Which Opera, Mews, and Cloudbeds actions are live for hotels (read context vs reservation changes, payments, tasks)?
Do independent hotels in practice buy Messaging only or Guest/Portals, given no hotel portal proof in this pack?
Who signs (owner, GM, brand, procurement) when a group wants shared standards plus property exceptions?

icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask who owns brand standards versus property exceptions and whether conversations should be grouped by property or central team.

icp_criteria.criterion: Owner-operator support-cost or hands-off valuation problem similar to Lauderdale
icp_criteria.rationale: The only named hotel story is a boutique owner replacing call-center spend; that pain is not shown as all hotels’ urgency.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Current third-party support cost, response times, and whether the owner still handles exceptions personally.

documents.markdown:
This page is an **account-fit model** for professional short-term / vacation-rental operators. It is not a claim that every listing owner shares the same pain. Public FAQs say Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and **short-term rental managers**. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Industry entry: [AI for Short-Term Rentals](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals). Hotel-shaped accounts belong in [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels). Capabilities sit in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities); named proof in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

## Account definition

The operator Conduit describes answers **guests per listing**: messages and calls using property information and reservation data, actions in connected tools, escalation to a team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) Inbox copy says hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers use it for guest communication across properties. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)

**Owner versus management company** (do not collapse):

| Pattern | What sources show | Unknown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Property management company | Bocobay: high-end PM firm in Aruba and Curaçao. Canbnb: Canberra PMC for Airbnb and short-term accommodation. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) | Whether the economic buyer is founder, ops, or owner-clients |
| Local operator acquiring other PMs | Cascadia Getaways: locally owned Oregon vacation rentals; leadership expected to absorb its first PM acquisition without extra guest-service staff; a completed staffing outcome is not established. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) | Acquisition size |
| Multi-market hospitality + real estate | Wynwood House across seven countries in Latin America and Europe. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house) | Unit count behind “thousands of guest interactions” |
| Individual listing owner | No named owner-host story in this pack. **Startup** is 0–25 units at $899/mo with 2,000 credits. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) | Whether hosts without a support team are a priority |

A vacation-rental homepage is not evidence of professional ops, distributed guest communications, or field staff. Identify who answers OTA threads, who holds the PMS, and who employs cleaners.

## Best-fit operating situations

These are **published situations**, not a ranked need list. Do not read pain into a prospect from marketing copy.

| Situation as published | Named example | Confirm in product |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Portfolio growth without extra guest-support hires | HomeHop: roughly 40→108 Cleveland/Akron listings; case TL;DR 70% automation. Canbnb’s 7→170 properties describes the scaling challenge, not proven hire avoidance; its reported outcome is ~1,500 messages sent/week, 60% AI-handled. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) | [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) Product nav still labels Operations “Coming soon.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

## Company and technology profile

Packages are **per unit per month** (Messaging from $18 / 40 credits; Guest $30 / 60; Guest + Devices $36 / 80; Full Suite $48 / 100). “Starting rates shown. Pricing scales beyond 50 listings.” Startup is a full-feature $899/mo bundle for 0–25 units. A bundle price is not a standalone Agents or Portals price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) See [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing).

The STR page lists Guesty, Hostaway, Track, Wheelhouse, Streamline, Lodgify, Hostfully, OwnerRez, Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia, and VRBO, and describes bringing Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, email, SMS, and calls into one workspace through connected accounts. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals) A logo is not proof of reservation writes, payments, or lock control—confirm in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations).

[Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) describe one branded stay link (no app) for stay details, identity checks, rental agreements or damage waivers, fees/deposits, upgrades, access when requirements are complete, and an AI concierge. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals) [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) can send check-in instructions and offer add-ons such as early check-in and gap nights. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows)

## Buying committee

Named STR voices: co-founders (Bocobay’s Nick Curtis; HomeHop’s Dan Mitchen), Canbnb’s Process and Communication Manager Jo-Anne Quiros plus leadership Dan, Cascadia’s Ryan (Revenue & Guest Services), Wynwood’s Mayra (Global Head of Customer Experience). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house)

Do not invent a mandatory economic-buyer title or a segment-wide attitude toward AI. Jo-Anne was skeptical; Dan Mitchen was leery after a failed vendor—those are **those people**. Map roles in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles).

## Qualification decisions

1. **Operator class.** STR/vacation-rental manager versus hotel-led operation. For serviced apartments and mixed portfolios, establish staffed front-desk versus distributed listing operations before selecting the hotel or rental motion; do not transfer STR case metrics automatically. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)
2. **Who runs communications.** If listing owners never touch guest threads, the manager is the account.
3. **Channels and reservation context.** Inbox lists SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social messages, and connected OTA threads, with PMS/OTA details beside the conversation. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)
4. **Scale.** No published minimum units, revenue, or headcount. 100 / 108 / 170+ are **examples**, not cutoffs. Startup exists for 0–25 units. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)
5. **Proof.** One named story, dates and caveats in the same breath. Do not average 60% / 70% / 80%. See [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

Research without projecting pain: management brand vs owner name on OTAs; PMS mentioned in careers or help center; advertised 24/7 guest line; Intercom/Zendesk vs Hostaway/Guesty messaging; multi-market sites. Then ask—playbook: [Qualification & account research playbook](#knowledge/buying-triggers).

## Signals and next questions

**Public signals to investigate (not auto-qualify):** multiple listings under one management brand; Hostaway/Guesty/Lodgify in public stack clues; WhatsApp as the guest line; overnight phone coverage; a recent PM acquisition; owner-communication copy.

**Next questions:** Which system owns Airbnb/Vrbo threads today? Separate owner vs guest vs vendor queues? Who approves AI vs autopilot? Are smart locks, waivers, or deposits on the critical path? Is housekeeping coordination a now-need while Operations is still “coming soon” on the nav?

## Disqualifiers and unresolved assumptions

No hard listing-count exclusion is published—do not reject “too small” from the site alone. Preferential misfits to **investigate**: no guest messaging (pure back-office admin); the only job is AI-coordinated housekeeping as a generally available catalog product; treating Conduit as a PMS replacement (STR page positions it on top of Guesty, Hostaway, and Lodgify). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals)

**Unresolved:** live messaging path for every OTA named on the industry page; Cascadia “using Conduit since December 2024” vs deployed in March; HomeHop “June 2025” vs “approximately two years”; automation denominators (messages vs resolution rate); whether owner-hosts on Startup are a priority versus PMCs. Segment ranking: [ICP strategy & segment priorities](#knowledge/ideal-customers).

documents.summary: Named Conduit stories show founders and CEOs as economic buyers and guest-experience or communications managers as champions, while public pages address hotel, serviced-apartment, and short-term rental teams rather than a published RACI. Trust, control, and job-change attitudes are taken from those write-ups; ages, income, security evaluators, and unstated hotel-group titles are not inferred.
documents.markdown:
Conduit’s site names the audience as hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, not a published buying committee. Named stories mostly put founders or CEOs on the commercial decision and guest-experience or communications leads on daily configuration. Titles below are observed in those pages or in industry copy; they are not a confirmed org chart. Pair this with [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence), [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels), and [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals).

## Buying roles and title map

Committee labels are a working overlay. Only titles in the observed column appear in the supplied sources.

| Function | Observed titles | Remit / scope in sources | Product surface they actually used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Economic buyer | CEO (Haven, The Flex); Founder (Lauderdale, Cosmica, Bali Luxury Stays); Co-Founder (Bocobay, HomeHop) | Headcount, NOI or exit math, whether listing growth needs more support staff | Platform as a whole vs call center, VAs, or Intercom |
| Champion / process owner | Process and Communication Manager (Canbnb); Revenue & Guest Services (Cascadia); Global Head of Customer Experience (Wynwood); guest services manager (Haven) | Inbox design, knowledge, automation rate without dropping scores | [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows) |
| Operational user (can block) | Guest-services reps, VA teams, night shift, front-desk staff; remaining “conversational engineers” | Takeovers, teaching replies, owner/vendor threads | Handoffs, notes/tags, after-hours voice |
| Technical / build evaluator | The Flex: homegrown PMS, with communications AI bought separately; HomeHop: SuiteOP as an adjacent system; Easy BnB founder: abandoned in-house messaging AI (story on Bali Luxury Stays page) | Stack fit, knowledge quality, when writes are allowed | [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations), [Developer platform & custom workflows](#knowledge/product-developers) |

Independent-hotel copy is a desk team covering calls after hours while people remain at the desk. Hotel-group copy is shared brand standards plus per-property policies. STR copy is per-listing knowledge and OTA inboxes. None of those pages maps to GM, cluster manager, or CISO as buyers. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals)

A security evaluator is not named here. API/MCP is a workspace capability, not proof that engineering always sits on the committee. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/developers)

### Roles to test during discovery

The following title hypotheses make the committee map actionable; they are suggested search roles, not confirmed Conduit buyers or required titles.

| Buying role | Titles to test | Decision and practical question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Independent-hotel sponsor | Owner, general manager, operations director | Owns staffing and guest-service economics. Who can approve a change to night coverage and its budget? |
| Group-level sponsor | COO, VP/Director of Operations, guest-experience leader | Owns shared service standards and rollout. Is purchasing centralized, property-led, or franchise-controlled? |
| Operational champion | Front Office Manager, reservations lead, guest-services/CX manager | Owns queues, knowledge and escalation. Who can maintain policies and measure response quality after launch? |
| Technical evaluator | IT director, business-systems/PMS administrator, integration owner | Confirms reservation data, channel routing and permitted actions. Which connection path and write permissions are actually available? |
| Risk and commercial reviewers | Security/privacy reviewer, procurement or finance owner when required | Confirms guest-data handling, contract and usage economics. Who approves access, billing assumptions and vendor onboarding? |

Role seniority and property-versus-group remit are relevant professional demographics. Age, gender and personal income are not needed for these buying decisions. Validate the role map with the account instead of assuming that every company has every department.

## Priorities and desired results

| Observed role | Job in the stories | Result they cited | Proof they pointed at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Founder / CEO / owner | Stop linear hiring; raise NOI or EBITDA; absorb an acquisition | Automation %, support cost, listings per rep, modeled asset value | Lauderdale support $4,000→$600/mo and ≥$3,400/mo NOI; Haven’s support staffing need ~25 people → two per shift, alongside its no-AI-layoff pledge and staff retraining; HomeHop 40→108 listings without extra guest-support hires |
| CX / guest services lead | One inbox, faster resolution, multilingual quality, shift handoffs | Resolution time, communication score, AI/human indistinguishability | Wynwood 14–15 min → 3 min; Cascadia 4.9 communication score; Canbnb ~1,500 messages/week, 60% AI |
| Revenue + guest services | Free people for upsells and proactive calls | Upsell share, pre-arrival programs | Cosmica ~5% of Dubai revenue from upsells/cross-sells at peak; Cascadia concierge and pre-arrival calls |
| Ops / process manager | Virtual vs on-site coordination; brand-consistent replies | Queue control, fewer tool switches | Canbnb guest/owner/vendor inboxes; Bocobay leaving Intercom |

Agents are evaluated as answering with property information and reservation data, acting in connected tools, and escalating on procedures the operator sets—not as a guaranteed resolution rate. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

## Buying attitudes and objections

**Trust.** Wynwood’s CX lead said guests cannot tell an AI agent from a human. Cascadia’s Ryan said guests think they are talking to someone local. Haven’s CEO had the agent say it needs a moment and will follow up in two or three minutes rather than guess. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

**Control.** Site copy stresses rules you set and requests the team should handle. HomeHop wanted to approve messages or run autopilot after a failed vendor. The Flex’s CEO delayed turning AI on until he understood it would not answer without knowledge. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex)

**Change.** Haven’s CEO held three meetings, pledged no AI layoffs, and moved people into workflow building. Cascadia told the team AI would not take their jobs and expanded people into SEO, revenue, and concierge. Easy BnB, in the Bali Luxury Stays story, is the contrary case: eleven VAs replaced for an exit. Do not treat one staffing model as the category. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays)

**Fit skepticism.** Canbnb’s process manager was unconvinced AI would fit operations. HomeHop’s co-founder was leery after a chatbot that did not work. Bocobay’s objection was Intercom versus guest, owner, and ground operations in one place. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)

## Decision process

These pages describe implementations, not a standard RFP.

1. **The trigger is operational scale:** Canbnb’s 630-message backlog, Lauderdale’s call-center cost and ~57-minute replies, Bocobay’s dual inboxes, The Flex’s 17 SaaS tools, Haven/HomeHop growth without proportional support, Cascadia’s first PM acquisition.
2. **Economic buyer plus an operator** show up together (Jack and Jonathan; Jo-Anne and Dan; Dan Mitchen and Nate; Mayra as global CX). The Flex later said knowledge setup should have been founder-led.
3. **Proof is control, then measured automation.** Haven tied incentives to automation *and* scores. Bocobay moved email, then WhatsApp, then phone, then live chat. A security questionnaire is not documented.

Hotel-group buying (loyalty, cluster reporting, shared KB) appears on the industry page, not in a named hotel-group case in this pack. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

**CX / process champion.** Which channels must share one workspace? What must never be automated, and who trains exceptions? How will you count resolved versus handed-off conversations without dropping communication scores?

**Operational users.** How do property views, routing, and notes work on shift handoff? What is handled at 2am (access codes, voice) versus what still pages a person?

**Technical evaluator (when present).** Messaging versus reservation-only PMS path, and duplicate-thread risk? Which writes (booking change, payment, task) are enabled for this stack? Is API/MCP in scope, or only the four marketed products in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities)?

If a title is missing, ask. Do not invent ages, gender, income, or a fixed hotel-group committee. Related jobs live in [Buyer problems & desired results](#knowledge/customer-jobs).

Conduit’s site names the audience as hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, not a published buying committee. Named stories mostly put founders or CEOs on the commercial decision and guest-experience or communications leads on daily configuration. Titles below are observed in those pages or in industry copy; they are not a confirmed org chart. Pair this with Customer evidence & usable proof, ICP · hotel operators, and ICP · vacation-rental operators.

Buying roles and title map

Committee labels are a working overlay. Only titles in the observed column appear in the supplied sources.

Function Observed titles Remit / scope in sources Product surface they actually used
Economic buyer CEO (Haven, The Flex); Founder (Lauderdale, Cosmica, Bali Luxury Stays); Co-Founder (Bocobay, HomeHop) Headcount, NOI or exit math, whether listing growth needs more support staff Platform as a whole vs call center, VAs, or Intercom
Champion / process owner Process and Communication Manager (Canbnb); Revenue & Guest Services (Cascadia); Global Head of Customer Experience (Wynwood); guest services manager (Haven) Inbox design, knowledge, automation rate without dropping scores Inbox, AI Agents, Workflows
Operational user (can block) Guest-services reps, VA teams, night shift, front-desk staff; remaining “conversational engineers” Takeovers, teaching replies, owner/vendor threads Handoffs, notes/tags, after-hours voice
Technical / build evaluator The Flex: homegrown PMS, with communications AI bought separately; HomeHop: SuiteOP as an adjacent system; Easy BnB founder: abandoned in-house messaging AI (story on Bali Luxury Stays page) Stack fit, knowledge quality, when writes are allowed Integrations & implementation readiness, Developer platform & custom workflows

Independent-hotel copy is a desk team covering calls after hours while people remain at the desk. Hotel-group copy is shared brand standards plus per-property policies. STR copy is per-listing knowledge and OTA inboxes. None of those pages maps to GM, cluster manager, or CISO as buyers. Source Source Source

A security evaluator is not named here. API/MCP is a workspace capability, not proof that engineering always sits on the committee. Source

Roles to test during discovery

The following title hypotheses make the committee map actionable; they are suggested search roles, not confirmed Conduit buyers or required titles.

Buying role Titles to test Decision and practical question
Independent-hotel sponsor Owner, general manager, operations director Owns staffing and guest-service economics. Who can approve a change to night coverage and its budget?
Group-level sponsor COO, VP/Director of Operations, guest-experience leader Owns shared service standards and rollout. Is purchasing centralized, property-led, or franchise-controlled?
Operational champion Front Office Manager, reservations lead, guest-services/CX manager Owns queues, knowledge and escalation. Who can maintain policies and measure response quality after launch?
Technical evaluator IT director, business-systems/PMS administrator, integration owner Confirms reservation data, channel routing and permitted actions. Which connection path and write permissions are actually available?
Risk and commercial reviewers Security/privacy reviewer, procurement or finance owner when required Confirms guest-data handling, contract and usage economics. Who approves access, billing assumptions and vendor onboarding?

Role seniority and property-versus-group remit are relevant professional demographics. Age, gender and personal income are not needed for these buying decisions. Validate the role map with the account instead of assuming that every company has every department.

Priorities and desired results

Observed role Job in the stories Result they cited Proof they pointed at
Founder / CEO / owner Stop linear hiring; raise NOI or EBITDA; absorb an acquisition Automation %, support cost, listings per rep, modeled asset value Lauderdale support $4,000→$600/mo and ≥$3,400/mo NOI; Haven’s support staffing need ~25 people → two per shift, alongside its no-AI-layoff pledge and staff retraining; HomeHop 40→108 listings without extra guest-support hires
CX / guest services lead One inbox, faster resolution, multilingual quality, shift handoffs Resolution time, communication score, AI/human indistinguishability Wynwood 14–15 min → 3 min; Cascadia 4.9 communication score; Canbnb ~1,500 messages/week, 60% AI
Revenue + guest services Free people for upsells and proactive calls Upsell share, pre-arrival programs Cosmica ~5% of Dubai revenue from upsells/cross-sells at peak; Cascadia concierge and pre-arrival calls
Ops / process manager Virtual vs on-site coordination; brand-consistent replies Queue control, fewer tool switches Canbnb guest/owner/vendor inboxes; Bocobay leaving Intercom

Agents are evaluated as answering with property information and reservation data, acting in connected tools, and escalating on procedures the operator sets—not as a guaranteed resolution rate. Source

Buying attitudes and objections

Trust. Wynwood’s CX lead said guests cannot tell an AI agent from a human. Cascadia’s Ryan said guests think they are talking to someone local. Haven’s CEO had the agent say it needs a moment and will follow up in two or three minutes rather than guess. Source Source Source

Control. Site copy stresses rules you set and requests the team should handle. HomeHop wanted to approve messages or run autopilot after a failed vendor. The Flex’s CEO delayed turning AI on until he understood it would not answer without knowledge. Source Source Source

Change. Haven’s CEO held three meetings, pledged no AI layoffs, and moved people into workflow building. Cascadia told the team AI would not take their jobs and expanded people into SEO, revenue, and concierge. Easy BnB, in the Bali Luxury Stays story, is the contrary case: eleven VAs replaced for an exit. Do not treat one staffing model as the category. Source Source Source

Fit skepticism. Canbnb’s process manager was unconvinced AI would fit operations. HomeHop’s co-founder was leery after a chatbot that did not work. Bocobay’s objection was Intercom versus guest, owner, and ground operations in one place. Source Source

documents.title: Qualification & account research playbook
documents.summary: Qualify Conduit accounts by lodging model, property-specific guest work, and a connectable channel/PMS path—not by job title, unit count, or automation-rate targets. Treat growth, overnight coverage, stack misfit, acquisition, and support-cost pressure as timing hypotheses to confirm in discovery, then proceed, research, or hold with explicit dependencies.
documents.markdown:
This playbook is a test sequence for humans and ABM agents, not a scored lead model. Fit is whether the company operates hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental stays. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Readiness is whether agents can use property information, reservation data, connected tools, and escalation rules. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md) Timing is a present operating situation—not later automation rates or modeled asset value, which stay attributed in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence).

Run [ICP strategy & segment priorities](#knowledge/ideal-customers) first, then [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels) or [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals). Map capabilities in [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities) and stack in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations). [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) is commercial mapping after fit, not a fit gate.

## Fit, readiness and timing

**Fit.** The pricing FAQ states Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers; agents answer guest messages and calls, handle routine requests, and coordinate work with the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) Site industries are short-term rentals, independent hotels, and hotel groups. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) Positive observation: the account sells or manages stays and already talks to guests on channels the inbox unifies. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox.md) Hotels and STR operators are both in-category and different tests (after-hours desk, Opera/Mews/Cloudbeds, spa/dining extras versus per-listing knowledge, Airbnb threads, check-in and booking-change requests). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals) Unknown: keep serviced apartments and hotel groups in-category until disproven—named stories in this pack cluster in STR/PM companies, with one boutique-hotel write-up. Disqualify only when the company does not operate those stays. A motivated champion does not create fit; titles belong in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles).

**Readiness.** Agents retrieve context and take action in connected tools, then escalate. How much they resolve “depends on your guest requests, knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules.” [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md) Haven already had Conduit installed at about 40 percent automation with listings uploaded, no workflows, and minimal knowledge-base work—so a live install is not readiness. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) Confirm whether a PMS path actually supplies live reservation context and whether messaging rides that connector. Opera Cloud is described as reservation and profile sync; it does not route guest messaging through that integration. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/opera) Booking.com and VRBO were marked coming soon on the captured directory. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations) A logo is not a supported action.

**Timing versus later outcomes.** Named situations to investigate, not needs every customer has: guest volume versus support seats (Haven, HomeHop, Canbnb); overnight voice (HomeHop 1–7 AM; independent-hotel after-hours copy); split inboxes or generic helpdesk misfit (Bocobay leaving Intercom); acquisition or multi-market expansion (Cascadia, Cosmica, Wynwood); owner support-cost / NOI (Lauderdale). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel) “We cannot cover the next peak, night shift, or acquired portfolio” is buying timing. “We want 90% automation” or cap-rate math is a later adoption or outcome claim—do not use it as a qualification bar.

## Qualification matrix

No weights. Unknown means investigate.

| Criterion | Dimension | Positive observation | Source / method | Unknown or hold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stay operator in FAQ industries | Fit | Hotel, serviced-apartment, or STR guest stays | Site, OTA, PMS, discovery | Hybrid RE+hospitality still in-category if stays are operated; exclude only non-stay businesses |
| Property-specific answers | Fit | Policies and booking context differ by property or listing | Product claims + discovery | Ask how answers differ by stay; generic ticket-only ops is a research flag |
| Channels Conduit unifies | Readiness | SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social, connected OTA threads | Inbox FAQ vs their stack | [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox.md) List required OTAs; hold if Booking.com/VRBO is mandatory until live status is confirmed |
| Reservation context path | Readiness | Connected PMS/OTA shows stay/booking beside the thread | Integration page + demo | Opera: messaging stays on existing hotel channels; confirm write-back separately |
| Knowledge + escalation owner | Readiness | Named person will standardize answers and review handoffs | Ops interview (Haven pattern) | Hold close until an owner exists; refusal to document policies is disqualifying for implementation |
| Present operating pressure | Urgency | Headcount lag, overnight gap, acquisition, call-center cost, two inboxes | Jobs, news, discovery | Hypothesis only—do not invent a timeline |

Startup (0–25 units, $899/mo, no implementation fee) and per-unit starting rates ($18–$48) that “scale beyond 50 listings” are commercial bands, not ICP cutoffs. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

## Signals and sourcing

Search for operators and stacks, not buzzwords.

| Signal | Where to source | What it tests | Do not infer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Listings + PMS names (Guesty, Hostaway, Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, Airbnb) | Website, OTA, careers, [integrations](#knowledge/integrations) | Fit and connector research | Any write action; Airbnb card claims two-way messages and reservation modifications—verify for this account [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/integrations/airbnb) |
| Multi-channel guest lines | Support pages, WhatsApp, phone | Inbox / Agents path | Full Suite operations jobs; nav still marks Operations coming soon |
| Guest-support or night hiring | Job boards | Timing hypothesis | Headcount as a fit score |
| Acquisition, new market, OM/exit language | Press | Cascadia / Lauderdale / Bali-type situations | Those customers’ dollar or automation results |
| Intercom / VoIP / prior AI failure | Stack tools, reviews | Bocobay / HomeHop / Flex-type misfit | A guaranteed migration outcome |

Company “300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries” is reach copy, not named-account proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

## Discovery conversation

Collect observations that fill the matrix. Do not quote attributed rates as typical.

Draft questions:

1. Who operates the stays, and is the contract with the owner, manager, or brand?
2. Which channels must sit in one workspace on day one?
3. Which system is source of truth for reservations, and should guest messaging stay on the PMS or move?
4. Who owns property policies, and who reviews agent handoffs?
5. What breaks if you add listings, an overnight window, or an acquired portfolio without new support seats? Haven reported adding 14 listings in January without adding support staff—ask whether that pressure exists; do not promise the result. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)
6. Is the job unified inbox and voice (Messaging starting $18/unit/mo), portals/waivers/payments (Guest starting $30), devices, or Full Suite operational features? Operator is the workspace assistant; Operations is a separate coming-soon product label. Confirm the exact operational feature before quoting a delivery commitment. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Separate current pain (unread backlog, hour-long replies, two inboxes, Slack as the night desk) from later desired state (automation share, NOI, 24/7 autopilot).

## Decision and handoff

| Decision | When observed | Dependencies | Handoff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proceed | In-category stays + connectable path + named knowledge/escalation owner. Timing evidence prioritizes the conversation; it is not a required fit gate | Package choice after fit; write actions confirmed for this PMS | Solution design with one named analog from [customer-evidence](#knowledge/customer-evidence), never an averaged rate |
| Research | Lodging-adjacent; hotel group or serviced apartment without a story analog; OTA/PMS path unclear; Booking.com/VRBO required; unit vs listing undefined | Integration owner + sales mapping | Do not reject; log unknowns |
| Hold | No guest-stay operation; no one will document policies; asked job is a physical check-in kiosk | Hotel-groups copy: communication support, not a kiosk [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups) | Polite close or recast the job |

Packet: segment, stack versus live connectors, observed timing (not inferred attitude), open unknowns, and the entry product (Inbox/Agents versus Portals versus Workflows).
open_questions: What Conduit bills as a unit versus a listing, room, or key, and whether that changes hotel versus STR quotes.
Which PMS/OTA connectors actually modify reservations, take payment, or create tasks for a given stack—not merely appear as logos.
Whether Booking.com and VRBO messaging are live after the 19 Sep 2026 directory capture that marked both coming soon.
Named, in-body proof for hotel groups and serviced-apartment operators comparable to the STR stories.
Whether Full Suite operations lines can be scoped while product nav still labels Operations coming soon.

icp_criteria.criterion: Company operates hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental guest stays
icp_criteria.rationale: Public FAQ defines Conduit’s buyers as those three operator types, not a job-title list.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm lodging model from website, OTA listings, PMS, and discovery; use hotel vs STR industry pages as separate tests.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Investigate hybrids that still run guest stays; do not reject for a missing named story.

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest work is property- or listing-specific and uses reservation context
icp_criteria.rationale: Agents are described as answering with property information and reservation data and acting in connected tools.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask how policies, access instructions, and booking changes differ by stay; look for multi-property or per-listing operations.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Research; a generic contact-center with no stay context is a flag, not an automatic reject until confirmed.

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest conversations run on channels the inbox can unify
icp_criteria.rationale: Inbox coverage is specified as SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social messages, and connected OTA threads.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Inventory live channels against the inbox FAQ and the integrations directory.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If Booking.com or VRBO is required, research live status (captured as coming soon) before promising that path.

icp_criteria.criterion: A PMS or OTA path can supply live booking context; messaging path is explicit
icp_criteria.rationale: Inbox places booking details beside the thread; Opera Cloud is documented as context sync without messaging through that connector.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Name the PMS/OTA, read the matching integration card, and confirm in discovery whether messaging stays on existing hotel channels or a two-way OTA path (e.g. Airbnb card).
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Do not infer write-back from a logo; hold solution design until the message path is stated.

icp_criteria.criterion: Named owner will maintain knowledge, procedures, and escalation rules
icp_criteria.rationale: Public agent FAQ ties autonomous resolution to knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules; Haven’s underuse at ~40% shows install without that work.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Identify who standardizes answers and reviews handoffs before close.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Proceed to research, not commercial close, until an owner is named; explicit refusal to document policies is implementation-disqualifying.

icp_criteria.criterion: A present operating pressure exists (volume vs staff, overnight coverage, acquisition, support-cost model, or split inbox)
icp_criteria.rationale: Named stories describe those situations; they are research prompts, not universal needs or a scoring model.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Jobs, press, and discovery questions that separate current breakage from later automation or valuation goals.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Leave urgency unknown; do not invent timeline or buying attitude.

icp_criteria.criterion: Account does not operate hotel, serviced-apartment, or short-term rental stays
icp_criteria.rationale: Out-of-category follows the published who-it-is-for sentence; sources do not publish a broader negative ICP.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: If the core business is not guest stays, hold even if a champion is enthusiastic.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Missing unit count, thinner hotel-group proof, or an unverified connector is not exclusion.

icp_criteria.criterion: Hotel-group or serviced-apartment motion with shared brand standards and per-property policies
icp_criteria.rationale: Hotel groups are a marketed industry; serviced apartments appear in the FAQ; named case bodies in this pack do not establish group-level proof.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm multi-property org, shared vs local knowledge, and PMS mix; keep in-category while logging proof gap.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Investigate rather than reject; do not treat STR story metrics as group evidence.
