HostAI becomes Conduit, raises $3.1M
News
/
Startups
By
Morgan Hines
|
April 11, 2025
Share
Artificial intelligence-powered short-term rental (STR), hotel and housing platform HostAI has become
Conduit
and raised $3.1 million.
Cole Rubin, co-founder and CEO of Conduit, shared the news in a lengthy
post on LinkedIn
and said the seed funding will accelerate growth and enable the company to work with more real estate operators.
Conduit, which started
out calling itself “Shopify for Travel,”
has grown from an automated guest messaging tool for STRs “into something much bigger,” Rubin said.
“The short-term rental industry pushed us in that direction,” Rubin said. “It was chaotic—operators were juggling dozens of tools, and the integration landscape was nowhere near mature enough to support a viable third-party messaging product—core integrations didn’t exist.”
The company built workarounds in response, integrating with Airbnb’s application programming interface, developing more features, developing more integrations and now working with STR managers around the globe. The efforts laid the groundwork for the company in its new iteration as Conduit, Rubin said.
“Conduit partners with enterprise property managers across all asset classes to power the future of real estate operations—with AI at the core. Real estate is a conversation-driven industry,” Rubin said. “Leasing, retention, maintenance, scheduling—it all runs on messaging and phone calls. But most operators are still stuck with fragmented systems and manual workflows. We saw a better way.”
Conduit’s AI agents can handle voice and text conversations and be integrated with companies’ businesses, from systems to documentation. They’re meant to function like “your best team member,” according to Rubin, who said the agents are responsive, consistent and know when to “escalate.”

The new funding was led by Pi Labs, according to investor Dhruv Gupta, who also shared the news

“We are thrilled to lead the $3.1 million seed round in Conduit (formerly HostAI), with participation from our friends at Y Combinator led by Pete Koomen, a16z Scout, YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim, Snapdocs founder Aaron King and others,” he said.
Gupta said Conduit's founding team, value proposition, customer perception, market opportunity and AI capabilities were among the key reasons why Pi Labs invested in the company.
“We believe AI agents are the future of property management. Conduit's AI, designed specifically for tenant/guest engagement, positions it as a leader in this technological shift,” Gupta said. “They have a strong product roadmap to maintain their competitive edge.”

# Conduit AI Review: Voice & Chat Agents for STR Guest Messaging (2026)

1 min read· Updated 2026-02-18· Reviewed by STR Specialist

## Overview

Conduit (formerly HostAI) is an AI agent platform that handles guest communication and sales for short‑term rental operators and hotels. It uses voice and chat agents trained on your policies and PMS data to answer questions, handle bookings, and run upsell workflows 24/7.

- It’s powerful for teams managing dozens of units who want to deflect calls and messages, but pricing is SaaS‑style at team level rather than per‑property, and it’s not a PMS or pricing engine.

What it does

- Focuses on AI agents for hospitality that can field guest inquiries, handle bookings, and upsell extras across voice and chat, instead of just being a chatbot widget.
- Voice AI can answer calls 24/7, look up property availability, quote prices, send quotes, and even create or modify reservations using PMS integrations.
- Workflow automation for STRs includes pre‑arrival messages, during‑stay Q&A, maintenance requests, upsells, and turnover task creation, all driven by AI agents.

- Automation-first workflows

## Pros & Cons

Highlights and considerations for Conduit AI.

Pros

- Focuses on AI agents for hospitality that can field guest inquiries, handle bookings, and upsell extras across voice and chat, instead of just being a chatbot widget.
- Voice AI can answer calls 24/7, look up property availability, quote prices, send quotes, and even create or modify reservations using PMS integrations.
- Workflow automation for STRs includes pre‑arrival messages, during‑stay Q&A, maintenance requests, upsells, and turnover task creation, all driven by AI agents.
- Integrates with PMS platforms such as Guesty, Hospitable, Hostaway and others to pull real‑time availability, guest information, and maintenance schedules into the AI agent’s context.
- Case studies highlight measurable revenue impact, such as an extra $40 per reservation from automated upsell flows and multi‑thousand‑dollar monthly savings compared with hiring more staff.

Cons

- Not a PMS, pricing tool, or channel manager; it must sit on top of existing systems and depends heavily on the quality of your PMS and processes.
- Public pricing is oriented around team‑wide AI usage (e.g., a Growth plan around $500/month) rather than simple per‑unit fees, which can be steep for very small portfolios.
- Rebrand from HostAI to Conduit and broader cross‑industry positioning can make hospitality‑specific information harder to find on the main site.
- As with any AI agent, you need careful SOPs, knowledge base curation, and guardrails to avoid wrong or off‑brand responses.
- Best value is for 20–50+ listings; solo hosts may find comparable benefit from cheaper, lighter‑weight automation built into PMS tools.

Conduit Review: AI Voice Agents for Property Management Operations | BestCRE

# Conduit Review: AI Voice Agents for Property Management Operations

Conduit deploys AI voice agents trained on property management workflows with native Yardi and AppFolio integrations. Reviewed by BestCRE using the 9AI Framework.

B

The commercial real estate industry spent an estimated $15.8 billion on property management technology in 2025, according to JLL’s PropTech report, yet tenant communication remains one of the most operationally expensive and inconsistent functions in the stack. CBRE’s 2025 Occupier Survey found that 62 percent of property managers cite after hours service requests as their single largest staffing cost driver, with average response times exceeding four hours for non emergency maintenance calls. Cushman and Wakefield estimates that a typical 500 unit multifamily property fields between 1,200 and 1,800 inbound calls per month, and that roughly 40 percent of those calls are repeat inquiries that could be resolved without human intervention. The gap between tenant expectations and operational capacity is widening as portfolios scale, creating a structural demand for AI systems that can absorb conversational volume without sacrificing service quality.

Conduit, formerly known as HostAI, is a Y Combinator backed AI agent platform that automates customer conversations for property management teams. The platform deploys voice and text AI agents trained specifically on property workflows, capable of triaging maintenance requests, distinguishing emergencies from routine issues, and routing calls to the appropriate resolution path. Conduit integrates natively with Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium, which allows it to create work orders, update tenant records, and provide real time status updates without manual handoffs. The company raised $3.1 million in seed funding led by Pi Labs with participation from Y Combinator and YouTube co founder Jawed Karim.

Conduit earns a 9AI Score of 87 out of 100, reflecting strong integration depth with major property management systems and a differentiated approach to conversational AI in a sector where automation has historically underperformed. The score is anchored by native workflow connectivity and innovation in voice AI, tempered by early stage market presence and limited published performance benchmarks.

This review is part of BestCRE’s systematic coverage of commercial real estate AI tools across 20 CRE sectors. For the full AI tools directory, see our Best CRE AI Tools hub.

## What Conduit Does and How It Works

Conduit is an AI agent platform that handles inbound and outbound conversations for property management companies through voice calls, SMS, email, and chat. The system is trained on property management workflows rather than general customer service scripts, which means it understands the difference between an emergency water leak that requires immediate escalation and a routine HVAC filter replacement that can be logged as a standard work order. When a tenant calls, the AI agent answers, identifies the nature of the request, creates or updates the appropriate record in the connected property management system, and either resolves the issue autonomously or routes it to the correct human staff member with full context attached.

The platform’s architecture is built around deep integrations with the property management software that operators already use. Native connectors to Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium mean that Conduit can pull tenant information, property details, and maintenance histories in real time during a conversation. This eliminates the double entry problem that plagues many bolt on communication tools and allows the AI to provide informed responses rather than generic scripts. For example, when a tenant calls about a maintenance issue, Conduit can confirm the unit number, check for open work orders on the same issue, and provide an estimated resolution timeline based on historical data from the property management system.

Conduit’s conversational agents also handle leasing inquiries, tour scheduling, and follow up communications, which extends its value beyond maintenance triage into revenue generating workflows. The platform supports multilingual interactions and can operate around the clock, which addresses the after hours service gap that represents one of the most persistent operational challenges in multifamily and commercial property management. The company positions itself as a replacement for answering services and call centers, with the additional capability of executing actions inside connected systems rather than simply taking messages. For property management companies running portfolios of several hundred to several thousand units, Conduit aims to reduce headcount dependency on repetitive conversational tasks while maintaining or improving tenant satisfaction scores.

### CRE Relevance: 7/10

Conduit was built from the ground up for the property management and housing sector, which gives it a meaningful edge over general purpose conversational AI platforms that require extensive customization to handle real estate workflows. The platform understands lease terminology, maintenance categorization, and the operational rhythms of multifamily and commercial property management. Its origin as HostAI, focused on short term rental management, demonstrates a lineage rooted in real estate operations rather than a pivot from an unrelated industry. The relevance is strongest for multifamily operators, student housing managers, and mixed use property teams that field high volumes of tenant communication. For pure commercial office or industrial portfolios with lower tenant interaction volumes, the value proposition is less pronounced but still applicable for tenant services and building operations. In practice: Conduit addresses a genuine operational pain point in property management that general purpose AI tools have not solved effectively.

### Data Quality and Sources: 5/10

Conduit is a conversational AI platform, not a data analytics or market intelligence tool, which means the data quality dimension is evaluated differently than it would be for a valuation or comp platform. The system does not generate proprietary market data or property level analytics. Instead, its data quality depends on the accuracy of information it pulls from connected property management systems and the reliability of its natural language understanding when processing tenant requests. The platform’s ability to correctly interpret maintenance urgency levels and route calls appropriately is a form of data quality, but it is dependent on the underlying PM system’s data integrity rather than Conduit’s own data assets. The company does not publish accuracy benchmarks for its language understanding or call routing in the way that valuation tools publish error rates. In practice: Conduit’s data handling is functional and context aware, but the platform does not contribute independent data assets to CRE decision making.

### Ease of Adoption: 7/10

The native integrations with Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium significantly reduce the adoption friction that typically accompanies new technology in property management. Rather than requiring a custom API build or middleware layer, Conduit can connect to the most widely used PM platforms through pre built connectors that sync tenant data, property records, and work order systems. This means a property management company can deploy the platform without a dedicated IT team or extensive configuration work. The setup process involves connecting the PM system, configuring workflow rules for call routing and escalation, and training the AI on property specific information such as amenities, policies, and emergency protocols. Reviews suggest that deployment can be completed within days rather than weeks, which is fast by property management technology standards. The learning curve for staff is minimal because the AI handles the conversations autonomously, with human oversight through a dashboard. In practice: most mid size property management firms can get Conduit operational quickly, though fine tuning escalation rules and exception handling may require ongoing adjustment.

### Output Accuracy: 6/10

Conduit’s output accuracy is measured by how correctly it interprets tenant requests, categorizes issues, and executes the appropriate workflow action. A published case study describes a 500 unit multifamily operator that reduced after hours call escalations by 67 percent using Conduit’s voice AI to triage maintenance requests, automatically create urgent work orders, and provide residents with estimated resolution timelines. That is a meaningful operational result, but the company has not published comprehensive accuracy rates for intent recognition, false positive escalation rates, or tenant satisfaction scores across a broad client base. For a conversational AI system, the risk of inaccuracy includes misclassifying an emergency as routine, failing to capture critical details in a maintenance request, or providing incorrect information about lease terms. The limited volume of published performance data makes it difficult to assess reliability at scale with the same confidence as tools that publish statistical benchmarks. In practice: early results are promising based on available case studies, but the absence of broad published accuracy data warrants conservative scoring.

### Integration and Workflow Fit: 8/10

Integration is Conduit’s strongest dimension. The platform offers native connectors to Yardi, AppFolio, and Buildium, which collectively represent the majority of the property management software market. These are not surface level integrations that simply pass data through an API. Conduit reads from and writes to the PM system in real time, which means it can create work orders, update tenant records, log communication histories, and trigger automated follow ups without requiring manual data entry. This bidirectional integration is critical because it allows the AI agent to function as an extension of the property management system rather than a disconnected communication layer. For property management companies that have standardized on one of these platforms, the integration depth removes a major barrier to adoption. The platform also supports communication channels including voice, SMS, email, and web chat, which consolidates tenant interactions into a single workflow layer. In practice: Conduit’s integration architecture is among the strongest in the CRE conversational AI space and is a primary driver of its value proposition.

### Pricing Transparency: 5/10

Conduit uses a credit based pricing model with tiered plans, but the company does not publish detailed pricing on its website. Third party sources reference a range of approximately $200 to $600 per month for AI powered property management communication platforms, though the exact pricing for Conduit depends on portfolio size, call volume, and the number of integrated properties. The absence of a public pricing page means that prospective customers must engage with sales to get a quote, which is common for enterprise focused property technology but creates friction for smaller operators who want to evaluate cost before committing to a demo. The credit based model adds a layer of complexity because it requires buyers to estimate their usage patterns before they can calculate total cost of ownership. For mid size property management firms budgeting for AI adoption, the lack of published pricing makes it harder to compare Conduit against alternatives without entering a sales process. In practice: pricing information is available through direct engagement but not transparent enough for self serve evaluation.

### Support and Reliability: 5/10

Punn Kam

Promoted by Conduit

Guests in LatAm send 2x more messages than in North America.

We looked at millions of guest messages on Conduit and averaged them by property. The spread was not what I expected.

Messages per property per month:

- Latin America: 23.7
- Middle East and Africa: 21.5
- Europe: 19.0
- Asia-Pacific: 15.4
- North America: 10.3

Latin America runs more than double North America. Inside the regions it gets wider still, with Argentina at 52.5 and Brazil at 43.1 against Australia at 10.4 and the United States at 9.6.

I don't think there's a single cause. North America may be more established with self-check-ins, which reduce message volume. The density of Latin America might make navigation more confusing. 

Whatever the reason, operators must staff up for the demand across both the average and on seasonal peaks. AI agents must play a major role in that staffing plan.

Full analysis in the comments.

To keep up with the volume, he was running virtual assistant teams out of the Philippines and Pakistan just to cover the messages, a workaround that kept things running but didn't let the business grow.

So he moved the whole operation onto Conduit and built custom tooling on top of it:

Your agents personalize each portal in the conversation and place the most relevant offers at the top. Guests pay in a double-tap with Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link, and more.

Cole Rubin

Promoted by Conduit

Every guidebook, welcome book and QR code on the fridge fixes the half of the problem that was never broken.

The pitch makes sense. Guests have questions, so give them a well-organized place to find the answers. Nicer layout, better categories, a link in the pre-arrival message.

We measured whether any of it lands. In threads where the operator had already sent the door code unprompted, before the guest asked anything, 27.4% of guests asked for it regardless. Check-in time ran 20.8%, wifi 18.4%.

That is information sitting on their phone, in a thread they already have open. If it gets missed there, a PDF will not rescue it.

Most guidebooks are organized fine. The timing is what fails. The information arrives days before anyone wants it, and when they finally do want it, finding it becomes the guest's job.

So we built the other half. Portals is our guest portal, and the AI chat lives in it. The guest asks the question the way they would say it out loud and gets an answer that knows which property they are standing in.

"What's a good dinner spot for us tonight around here."

Keep the guidebook. Just stop expecting it to answer anything.

Link in the comments.

> An AI agent platform for hospitality. Answer guest messages and calls, handle requests, and coordinate work through your connected PMS and tools.

Use this index to find machine-readable product, industry, company, trust, and developer resources. Follow the linked indexes for individual integrations, articles, and product updates.

Conduit serves hotel groups, independent hotels, short-term-rental operators, resorts, aparthotels, and villas. Agents built on Conduit work across email, phone, SMS, WhatsApp, online travel agencies, and connected property-management systems. Package pricing is published per unit per month, and portfolios of 0–25 units use the Startup plan at $899 per month.

Conduit Start Guide
Set up your Conduit workspace, connect channels, build V3 agents, and move from copilot to autopilot.
Looking to get started with Conduit?
Book a demo
or contact us at
support@conduit.ai
for personalized guidance.
​
Overview
Conduit gives your team one workspace for customer conversations, AI agents, workflow automation, and operational records. Start by setting up the workspace and channels, then build the V3 agent surfaces that control what the AI knows, how it behaves, and what actions it can take.
Create workspace
Invite teammates, configure roles, and set the workspace basics.
Connect channels
Bring email, WhatsApp, phone, SMS, widget, and other channels into Conduit.
Build agents
Configure external, internal, and voice agents from the V3 Agents area.
​
Set Up The Workspace
Everything in Conduit happens in your team’s workspace. A workspace contains your members, inboxes, connected channels, Knowledge Base, agents, tools, workflows, records, and settings.
Workspace setup
Configure the workspace, invite teammates, and decide who can manage agent settings.
Inbox and fields
Organize conversations by inbox, contact type, routing, and custom fields.
Admins can invite new members and manage roles from
Settings > Members
.
​
Connect Channels And Integrations
Connect your communication channels to centralize all customer interactions in one place.
Email
Link your support email to centralize all communication in Conduit.
WhatsApp Business
Manage WhatsApp inquiries directly in Conduit.
Business Phone Number
Handle calls and SMS alongside other channels.
Chat Widget
Add a custom chat widget to your company website.
Connect business systems and data sources after your channels are working.
PMS and integrations
Sync structured business data that agents can use in conversations.
Marketplace
Install apps, agent templates, skill templates, and workflow templates.
​
Build The V3 Agent System
V3 separates the agent system into focused surfaces. Use each one for the right kind of configuration.
Agents
Create customer, internal, and voice agents, then configure persona, behavior, triggers, and publish state.
Knowledge
Add pages, folders, documents, links, and synced data sources that agents can retrieve as facts.
Skills
Write reusable instructions that combine policy, process, variables, and tool-use guidance.
Tools
Enable connection tools, custom Python or JavaScript tools, MCP tools, and per-agent overrides.
​
Test And Deploy
Validate changes before you let the AI act on its own.
Operator
Use Conduit’s workspace assistant to help inspect, edit, and reason about agent configuration.
Sandbox testing
Test a specific agent with realistic customer, listing, and reservation context.
Road to Autopilot
Follow the Connect, Teach, Test, and Deploy loop to expand automation safely.
V3 migration
Review what changed for teams moving from the older interface to V3.
​
Using the Inbox
A clean inbox is still the daily operating surface. Conversations flow through Todo, Follow-Up, and Done, while agent activity, sources, and tool calls give your team visibility into how each response was produced.
The 5 Levels of AI Automation
Learn about the different levels of AI automation and how to progress through them.

Use typed endpoints for workspaces, contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, knowledge, agents, skills, workflows, and connected devices. Requests use bearer authentication and workspace-scoped authorization.

Authentication and safe automation
Generate API tokens under Settings > API & MCP. Start with read-only access, scope every request to a workspace your token can access, and keep explicit approval on actions that send messages or change records. The OpenAPI document provides unique operation IDs, typed parameters, response schemas, and operation descriptions for SDK generation and LLM function calling. MCP clients discover the same authenticated capabilities as tools, with annotations that distinguish read, write, idempotent, and potentially destructive operations.

3.15
SEPTEMBER 18, 2026
Major Features
Custom workspace roles
Build your own roles instead of choosing only Admin or Member. Create a role, pick exactly which pages and actions it can reach, and assign it to teammates or pending invites. Built-in roles stay put, and a role that is currently assigned to someone is protected from accidental deletion.
Find it under Settings → Members → Roles and permissions.
Enhanced Capabilities
Attach files to workflow messages
Workflow "Send message" steps can now carry file attachments, including files pulled from workflow variables. Send documents, guides, and forms automatically as part of an automation instead of pasting links.
Find it under Workflows → open a workflow → a Send message step.
More ways to filter your inbox
Quick filters in the inbox sidebar now include the same custom fields, listings, and assignee options as the full filter menu, and you can save them as views. Slice your conversations the way your team actually works.
Find it under Inbox → Filters.
Set your own warm-transfer wait time
Voice agents that warm-transfer a call to a person can now use a wait time you configure, so the hand-off matches how quickly your team picks up instead of a fixed default.
Find it under AI Agents → Voice → Escalations.
Target guest verification by custom attributes
Guest verification rules can now be scoped by the custom attributes on a reservation, so you can require the right checks for the right stays instead of applying one blanket rule.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
Pause and reactivate a reservation's guest portal
Turn an individual reservation's guest portal off and back on without deleting anything. Useful when a stay is on hold or a guest shouldn't have portal access for a while.
Find it under a reservation's detail panel → Portal.
One-click reconnect for PMS connections
Each PMS connection on the settings page now has its own Reconnect button that repairs that exact integration, instead of adding a new connection row. Reconnecting a property is now unambiguous.
Find it under Settings → Connections → PMS.
Configure how tasks are marked done
Choose which status counts as "done" per task category and control task completion behavior, so your operations board reflects your own workflow.
Find it under Settings → Operations → Task statuses.
Performance & Quality Improvements
Workflows
: Workflow steps now show template names and their approval status, so it's clear which message template a step will send.
Translation
: Added Polish for chat translation and AI agents.
Chat widget
: Polished interactions, layout, and scrolling in the chat widget.
Voice
: Corrected the message shown when a call is canceled before it's answered.
Designed, Built, and Written By
Will Garman
Full Stack Engineer
Cristian
Engineer
Bohdan
Engineer
Yash
Engineer
3.14
SEPTEMBER 11, 2026
Major Features
Security deposits in guest portals
Collect, hold, and release security deposits right through your guest portals. Guests see the deposit amount and its status before they check out, holds are captured or released as the stay progresses, and every deposit keeps a full history you can review and act on.
Find it under Portals → Transactions → Security deposits.
Enhanced Capabilities
Change door codes without leaving the inbox
Set, update, and retry a reservation's smart-lock door code straight from the inbox, and mark access codes and portals active or inactive as availability changes. Access codes can also be updated programmatically through the API.
Find it in the inbox reservation panel, or under Devices.
Turn any message into a task
Create a task directly from a guest message — the details are drafted for you from the conversation — through a redesigned new-task modal.
Find it in the inbox: open a message and choose Create task, or start one under Operations → Tasks.
Speaker labels in call summaries
Call summaries now identify who said what, so agent and guest turns are clear at a glance.
Find it in a call's summary in the inbox.
Video walkthroughs in listing details
Video links you add to a listing now render as rich preview cards in the guest-facing listing details, instead of a plain URL.
Find it under Portals → Listing details → open a listing.
Clearer workforce call reporting
Workforce now separates abandoned calls, where the caller hung up, from missed calls, with a dedicated abandoned-call-rate metric. Live and Overview also show real-time ticket counts with per-inbox and per-call-group breakdowns.
Find it in the org dashboard under Workforce → Misses and Overview.
Verification rules by booking date
Portal verification rules can now be scoped to a booking's dates, so ID and document checks apply only to the stays you choose.
Find it under Portals → Verification.
Performance & Quality Improvements
New widget chats start fresh instead of resurfacing a previous session.
Chat tool cards stay in place after a reply finishes, with smoother transitions in the chat widget.
Conduit no longer answers a call the caller has already hung up on.
Insights dashboards now load reliably across month-long date ranges.
Opening a workflow now takes you straight to its latest draft.
Guest PDFs now render emoji and international characters correctly.
Designed, Built, and Written By
Cristian
Engineer
Will Garman
Full Stack Engineer
Punn Kam
Co-Founder
Yash
Engineer
Bohdan
Engineer
3.13
SEPTEMBER 4, 2026
Major Features
Guest portals for every reservation
Generate a guest portal straight from a reservation. Open a reservation, and if it doesn't have a portal yet, create one in a click from the sidebar, scoped to that exact stay. A new workflow trigger fires the moment a guest finishes portal check-in, so the rest of your arrival flow can run on its own.
Find it under Reservations, open a reservation, and use the portal panel in the sidebar. The trigger is in the workflow builder as "Portal check-in completed."
Run your connected apps inside workflows
A workflow step can now run the tools from apps you've connected, like Monday.com or Asana, as a Run Tool step. Pass in parameters, including lists and structured values, and if a tool fails you get the real reason back instead of a generic error. Managers can refresh a connection's tool list so newly available tools show up without reconnecting.
Find it in the workflow builder: add a Run Tool step and pick a connected app's tool.
Enhanced Capabilities
See guest ID and selfie when you review check-in
When you review a guest's identity verification, you now see the ID front and back and the liveness selfie right in the review panel, so you can approve or reject without leaving Conduit.
Find it where you review check-in verification submissions.
Route each task category to its own Slack channel
Choose which Slack channel every task category posts to, so the right team sees the right work. You can also require specific custom fields before a task in a category can be marked complete.
Find it under Operations, then Tasks, in category settings.
Plan the day in Operations
Clearer day planning on the operations schedule, a new Trips table, and a "no assignee" filter to find unassigned tasks fast.
Find it under Operations, in Schedule and Tasks.
A contact's tasks, right in the inbox
Open a conversation and see every task tied to that contact in a new Tasks tab, without switching pages.
Find it in the Inbox conversation sidebar.
WhatsApp calls follow your call groups
Inbound WhatsApp calls now route through your call groups, ringing the right people and rolling to voicemail on the same rules as your phone lines.
Find it under Settings, then Call groups.
The chat widget remembers recent conversations
Guests returning to your website widget can pick up recent conversations again instead of starting over.
Find it in the chat widget on your website.
Search and filter workflow runs
Find a specific workflow run fast with new search and filters, and page through long histories without losing your place.
Find it under Workflows.
Keypad and access codes
Add a submit key to keypad access codes, and generate a guest's door code from the phone number on their reservation.
Find it under Devices.
Voice callbacks
When a caller asks for a callback, the voice agent can capture it as a note so your team can follow up.
Search reservations by confirmation ID
Search the inbox for a reservation by its PMS online confirmation ID.
Find it in the Inbox search bar.
Portal improvements
Group your upsell offers into categories guests browse in the portal
Embed YouTube videos in listing details
Let guests decline a damage waiver or security deposit when you allow it
Guest contact details from the portal now sync into your Conduit contacts
Show a notice in the portal when a guest's request has been escalated
Override the map link shown for a listing
Performance & Quality Improvements
Calls
: A refused call retries on a fresh device instead of dropping
Calls
: Stopped sending callers to voicemail after their agent had already joined
WhatsApp setup
: Clear guidance when your WhatsApp Business account doesn't match
Help
: Fixed broken in-app help links
Calendar
: Polished date-range calendar styling and filter controls
Designed, Built, and Written By
Cristian
Engineer
Will Garman
Full Stack Engineer
Punn Kam
Co-Founder
Yash
Engineer
3.12
AUGUST 28, 2026
Major Features
Jobber integration
Connect your Jobber account to Conduit. Jobber's jobs and work orders are now available as tools your AI agents and the public API can use, and a Jobber job change can trigger a workflow. Set up automations that fire when a job is scheduled, updated, or completed.
Find it in the workflow builder: add a trigger and pick Jobber. Jobber's work-order tools are also available to your AI agents and through the public API.
Book directly in the chat widget
The chat widget can now walk a guest through a booking without leaving the conversation: browse a listing, check availability, choose the guest count, and get a checkout link, all inline. It works across your connected property systems.
Find it in the chat widget on your website.
Enhanced Capabilities
Noise cancellation on calls
Turn on background noise cancellation so voices come through clearly on noisy lines.
Find it under the call panel's audio settings.
Search inside attachments
Inbox and ticket search now looks inside attachments, so you can find a conversation by the contents of a file someone sent, across every channel.
Find it in the Inbox search bar.
Post task activity to Slack
Task updates can now flow into a Slack thread, so the right people stay in the loop without opening Conduit. You can also update tasks, including custom fields, straight from the AI operator.
Find it under Operations → Tasks, and connect Slack under Settings → Connections.
Pause a contact's AI over the API
The public API can now pause and resume AI replies for a specific contact, so your own tools can hand a conversation to a human and take it back.
Find it in the public API reference.
Give workflow AI steps their own tools
When an AI step sends a message in a workflow, you can now grant it specific tools to use, so it can look things up or take action mid-workflow.
Find it in the workflow builder on the Send AI Message step.
Door codes in the inbox before check-in
Access codes now show in the conversation sidebar before a stay is activated, so you can share them without digging.
Find it in the Inbox conversation sidebar.
File uploads in Portal questions
Guide portals can now ask a guest to upload a file as an answer (an ID photo, a signed form), and it appears with the submission.
Find it under Portals when editing additional questions; uploads show with each submission.
Chat widget: pets and returning guests
The widget's guest count picker now includes pets, and returning visitors skip the intro setup and go straight to chatting.
Find it under Settings → Channels → Widget.
New property system: Avantio
Avantio is now available as a property management connection.
Find it under Settings → Connections when adding a property system.
Guest portal in the guest's language
Guests can now translate their guide portal into their own language with one tap, so check-in steps, house guides, and offers read clearly no matter where they are from.

JUNE 4, 2026
Conduit V3 just went live, with smarter agents, a faster inbox, improved escalations, and Operator. This is the biggest release we have shipped: the whole product is now organized around agents, your agents are split into the ones that talk to your contacts and the ones that run your operations, and every agent has its own home. And Operator, our agentic copilot, is here to do the work you ask of it.
Agents
Your agents now come in two kinds, and the difference is simple. External agents are the ones your contacts talk to. They handle the people writing in, and each one is triggered by an inbox. Internal agents run your operations. They have no inbox, and you trigger them through the channels you set up or by asking Operator.
A page for every agent
Open any agent and you land on its own page. You can see how it has been running at a glance, tune how it behaves, set its personalization and guardrails, and connect it to Slack, all in one place. No more hunting through settings to find one agent's configuration.
Triggers, front and center
The agent sidebar is built around triggers now. External agents live under an inbox trigger. Internal agents live under channel triggers, with Slack available today and Phone, Email, WhatsApp, and Teams on the way.
A marketplace to start from
The new Marketplace gives you a library of ready-made agents and skills. Pick one, install it, and you start from a working setup instead of a blank page. Each one tells you what it needs before it goes live, so there are no surprises.
Inbox
Call straight from a conversation
You can now place a call right from a conversation in the inbox. An inbound text or email can become a live call without you ever leaving the thread.
A calmer way to handle calls
Inbound calls got a real cleanup. A ringing call shows a clear Answer card instead of a pill you might tap by accident, and the call widget collapses to a safe state so nobody joins a call by mistake. If you are marked Away, calls stop ringing you, so they only reach people who can actually pick up.
Less setup, more context
Phone fields default to your workspace's country and preferred number, so you stop re-picking the same sender every time. And the conversation list now shows the booking channel, reservation dates, and status inline, so you can read the state of a booking without opening it.
Escalations
The right issue gets to the right place
When you hand an escalation to Operator, it routes the issue where it belongs and turns down anything it cannot actually act on, instead of quietly doing the wrong thing. And conversations that need a follow-up get put back in the queue, so a contact who needs a second touch is not forgotten.
Operator
Operator is the copilot you talk to, and it does the work. Ask it a question and it answers. Ask it for a report and it builds one. Hand it a pile of work and it triages it. It lives in your sidebar, and you can reach it through Slack too.
Here is some of what Operator can do for you:
Build a polished PDF report from your data, with charts included, ready to download and share.
Export your analytics to a CSV you can open in a spreadsheet.
Answer questions about your numbers and pull insights on demand.
Add contacts and fill in their custom fields.
Update your knowledge base, your agent instructions, and your guardrails.
Set up workflows.
Resolve escalations.
You describe what you need in plain language. Operator figures out the rest, shows its work, and hands you something you can use.

Get Started
MCP Server
Connect ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Cursor, VS Code, or any Model Context Protocol client to your Conduit workspace.
Conduit’s MCP server is available on the
v3 plan
. Contact
support@conduit.ai
to enable it for your workspace.
​
Overview
The
Model Context Protocol
is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to external systems. Conduit’s MCP server exposes your contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, knowledge base, and agents as tools any MCP-compatible client can call.
Once connected, your AI client can:
Look up contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, reservations, and appointments
Search the knowledge base and read knowledge nodes
Send messages on a conversation or ticket, or to a contact on a specific channel
Inspect and control connected locks, thermostats, sensors, and cameras when the Devices add-on is enabled
Create and manage agents, skills, custom code tools, and contact custom attributes
Manage the Operator’s skills (
operatorSettings.skills
), separate from regular agent skills
List workspaces your token has access to
The server implements the MCP specification revision
2025-06-18
over
streamable HTTP
.
​
MCP Endpoint
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
Every request includes an
Authorization: Bearer <token>
header. Workspace-scoped tools (most of them) also require a
workspace_id
argument.
​
Authentication
Two token types are accepted. Pick the one that matches the client.
OAuth 2.1
Interactive clients that want a user-consent flow, for example Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Claude Code, or Codex. Supports Dynamic Client Registration, so no pre-provisioning is needed.
API token
Server-to-server, CI, or CLI use. Generate a
capi_...
token under
Settings > API & MCP
and paste it into the client’s bearer-token field.
​
OAuth 2.1
Conduit’s MCP server advertises itself as an OAuth 2.1 protected resource per
RFC 9728
. When a client first POSTs to the MCP endpoint without a token, the server responds with
401
and a
WWW-Authenticate
header pointing at the resource metadata document. Any spec-compliant client will discover the rest automatically.
Metadata
URL
Protected resource metadata
https://api.conduit.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp
Authorization server
https://base.conduit.ai/oauth/mcp
Authorization server metadata
https://base.conduit.ai/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/oauth/mcp
Scopes
mcp:read
,
mcp:write
,
offline_access
Dynamic Client Registration (
RFC 7591
) is enabled, so clients register themselves on first connect. You sign in with your Conduit account in the browser window the client opens, pick which workspaces to grant access to, and the client caches the resulting access and refresh tokens.
​
API tokens
API tokens start with the
capi_
prefix and carry either
read-only
or
read/write
access. Write tools (
send_conversation_message
,
patch_contact
,
create_agent
, etc.) require a read/write token. Rotate or revoke tokens under
Settings > API & MCP
at any time.
curl
-X
POST
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
\
-H
"Authorization: Bearer capi_YOUR_TOKEN"
\
-H
"Content-Type: application/json"
\
-H
"Accept: application/json, text/event-stream"
\
-d
'{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl","version":"1.0"}}}'
​
Connect a Client
ChatGPT
Claude Desktop
Claude Code
Codex
Cursor
VS Code
Other clients
For the quickest setup in ChatGPT or Codex,
add the Conduit ChatGPT plugin
. Follow the prompts to sign in to Conduit and choose which workspaces the plugin can access.
Once added, the plugin provides five focused, read-only Conduit tools in both ChatGPT and Codex. It does not include the full MCP tool catalog or any write tools. Configure a direct MCP connection to send messages, update records, or use the other tools in the
Tool Reference
.
Connect directly from the
Conduit listing in Claude’s connector directory
, then complete the OAuth flow in your browser.
To add Conduit manually as a custom connector instead:
Open
Settings > Connectors
in Claude Desktop
Click
Add custom connector
Name:
Conduit
, URL:
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
Click
Connect
and complete the OAuth flow in your browser
Once connected, the Conduit tools show up under the plug icon in any chat.
Add the server from the CLI:
claude
mcp
add
--transport
http
conduit
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
The first tool call opens a browser for OAuth. Run
/mcp
in any session to see status, reconnect, or list available tools.
Scope.
claude mcp add
writes to your local config by default. Use
--scope user
to make Conduit available across every project, or
--scope project
to commit a
.mcp.json
your teammates share (each teammate still goes through their own OAuth):
claude
mcp
add
--transport
http
--scope
project
conduit
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
API token instead of OAuth.
For headless agents or CI, pass the token as a header:
claude
mcp
add
--transport
http
conduit
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
\
--header
"Authorization: Bearer capi_YOUR_TOKEN"
Pre-approve read-only tools.
Approval prompts on every read get noisy. Allow-list the safe ones in
~/.claude/settings.json
(or
.claude/settings.json
in the project):
{
"permissions"
: {
"allow"
: [
"mcp__conduit__list_workspaces"
,
"mcp__conduit__list_contacts"
,
"mcp__conduit__get_contact"
,
"mcp__conduit__search_contacts"
,
"mcp__conduit__list_conversations"
,
"mcp__conduit__list_conversation_messages"
,
"mcp__conduit__list_tickets"
,
"mcp__conduit__get_ticket"
,
"mcp__conduit__list_ticket_messages"
,
"mcp__conduit__search_knowledge"
,
"mcp__conduit__get_knowledge_node"
]
}
}
Never allow-list write tools (
send_*
,
patch_*
,
create_*
,
update_*
,
delete_*
). Keep approval prompts on for those.
For quick read-only access,
add the Conduit ChatGPT plugin
. Its five focused tools are also available in Codex.
To access the full tool catalog, including write tools, configure Conduit directly through MCP from the CLI:
codex
mcp
add
conduit
--url
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
codex
mcp
login
--scopes
mcp:read,mcp:write,offline_access
conduit
codex mcp login
opens a browser for OAuth and caches the tokens locally. Restart Codex after adding the server if the tools do not appear in your current session.
For API-token auth, point Codex at an environment variable that contains your token:
export
CONDUIT_API_TOKEN
=
capi_YOUR_TOKEN
codex
mcp
add
conduit
--url
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
--bearer-token-env-var
CONDUIT_API_TOKEN
Edit
~/.cursor/mcp.json
(or
.cursor/mcp.json
in a project) and add:
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"conduit"
: {
"url"
:
"https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp"
}
}
}
Restart Cursor. The first tool call opens the OAuth flow in a browser window.
For API-token auth, use the
headers
field instead of going through OAuth:
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"conduit"
: {
"url"
:
"https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp"
,
"headers"
: {
"Authorization"
:
"Bearer capi_YOUR_TOKEN"
}
}
}
}
Press
Cmd+Shift+P
(or
Ctrl+Shift+P
on Windows/Linux) and run
MCP: Add server
. Pick
HTTP
, enter
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
, and name it
conduit
. VS Code writes the entry to
mcp.json
:
{
"servers"
: {
"conduit"
: {
"type"
:
"http"
,
"url"
:
"https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp"
}
}
}
Sign in through the browser prompt on first use. Invoke tools with
#
in Copilot Chat.
Any client that supports MCP streamable HTTP works. Point it at
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
and either let it walk the OAuth discovery chain or configure an
Authorization: Bearer capi_...
header.
For stdio-only clients, use
npx -y mcp-remote https://api.conduit.ai/v1/mcp
as the command.
​
Production Setup
Four practices that keep MCP usage safe and predictable in real workflows.
​
Pin a workspace at the start of each session
Almost every tool requires a
workspace_id
. Open each session by anchoring the model to one workspace:
Use list_workspaces and operate on the "acme-hotels" workspace for the rest of this conversation.
The model holds onto that ID in context. Subsequent prompts don’t need to repeat it. Without this anchor, the model may guess at workspace IDs or call
list_workspaces
repeatedly.
​
Keep approvals on for write tools
Read tools are safe to pre-approve in clients that support it. Write tools — anything starting with
send_
,
patch_
,
create_
,
update_
, or
delete_
— should always prompt. Each Conduit tool advertises a
destructiveHint
annotation; well-behaved clients surface it on the approval dialog.
A misfired model decision against an allow-listed
send_conversation_message
ships a real message to a real customer. Don’t allow-list it.
​
Pass an idempotency key on every send
Every write tool accepts an
idempotency_key
input (or
Idempotency-Key
HTTP header). Pass a stable UUID per logical send. Clients retry on transient failures, and without a key a retry double-sends.
{
"name"
:
"send_conversation_message"
,
"arguments"
: {
"workspace_id"
:
"wp_..."
,
"conversation_id"
:
"cv_..."
,
"body"
:
"Hi! Quick update on your booking."
,
"idempotency_key"
:
"9f2c3d1a-..."
}
}
Either tell the model to generate one per send, or set it as a project rule that gets injected into every session.
​
Use least-privilege API tokens
For non-interactive use cases (CI, server-to-server, scripts), generate a
read-only
capi_
token and use it everywhere reads are sufficient. Only generate a
read_write
token for the specific session that needs writes, and rotate it after. Tokens are revoked under
Settings > API & MCP
and take effect immediately.
​
Example Prompts
Generic starting points that work in any MCP-enabled client. Swap names and IDs for your own.
Triage open tickets
For the acme-hotels workspace, list every open helpdesk ticket touched in the last 24 hours,
group them by inferred topic, and tell me the three most urgent ones with the customer name
and a one-line summary.
Uses
list_helpdesk_tickets
,
get_helpdesk_ticket
,
list_ticket_messages
. All read-only — no approval prompts if those tools are pre-approved.
Reproduce a customer report
Search the acme-hotels workspace for any conversation where the contact mentioned
"double charge" in the last week. Pull the full message thread for the most recent
one and show me the timestamps.
Useful in terminal-based clients (Claude Code, Codex) where you can immediately jump from the conversation into the relevant code path.
Draft a reply with full context
Pull conversation cv_abc on the acme-hotels workspace. Read the last twenty messages.
Draft a reply that addresses the refund question, matches the tone of our previous
responses, and cites our refund policy from the knowledge base. Don't send it — just print it.
The “don’t send” constraint is the safety belt while iterating. Drop it when you’re ready and the model will call
send_conversation_message
, which prompts for approval before anything ships.
Audit a knowledge base section
Search the knowledge base for any node that mentions our old cancellation policy
("48 hours"). For each match, show me the node title, the path, and the sentence
that contains the phrase.
Pair with a follow-up that calls
update_knowledge_node
(write tool, prompts for approval) once you’ve reviewed the list.
​
Rate Limits and Errors
By default, MCP tool calls are limited to
120 requests per minute per workspace
and share the same workspace-level budget as REST API requests. A
429
response includes a
Retry-After
header. Error responses follow the MCP spec:
content[0].text
holds the error message and
isError: true
is set on tool results.
See
Rate Limits
for details.
Status
Meaning
401
Missing, expired, or revoked token
403
Token does not have access to the requested workspace, or lacks
read_write
for a write tool
404
Resource not found in the given workspace
429
Rate limit exceeded
​
Tool Reference

initialize
and
tools/list
will receive every tool, its input schema, and its annotations (
readOnlyHint
,
destructiveHint
,
idempotentHint

openWorldHint
).

The
operator_*
tools manage the
Operator’s
skills (the knowledge cards the Operator assistant uses), which are separate from the regular agent skills managed by
*_skill

operatorSettings.skills
with the same workspace scoping and
Manage Agents
permission as the Operator settings screen in the app, and they are MCP-only (there is no matching REST route). Every
operator_*
tool takes a required
workspace_id
; writes need a read/write token and the
Manage Agents
permission.
The portal tools read guest sessions and build verification rules, offers, and page templates for the Portals add-on. They need the add-on enabled plus
Access Portals
for reads and
Manage Portals
for writes. See the
Portals API reference
for session submissions, step types, layout blocks, and worked examples.
The device tools require the Devices add-on. Read tools can inspect device state and history; write tools can manage access codes, locks, thermostats, noise thresholds, and property mappings. Device actions also follow workspace policy and contact scope. See
Devices
for supported locks, agent behavior, and the full tool guide.
See the
REST API reference
for the underlying resource shapes. MCP tools share the same schemas.
To author a custom tool over MCP, call
list_custom_tool_runtimes
first. It returns the entrypoint signature, required return shape, and available dependencies for Python and JavaScript, so the model writes
code
that passes validation on the first try. See the
Custom Tools overview
for the full contract.
​
Troubleshooting
Claude shows Request instead of Connect
On a Claude Team plan, members without permission to enable connectors see a
Request
button for Conduit instead of
Connect
. Click
Request
to send the connector to your organization’s admins for review. The button changes to
Requested
while approval is pending. An admin must approve the connector before you can connect it.
See Claude’s
guide to requesting a connector on a Team plan
for more details.
Client says Unauthorized after working for a while
The OAuth access token expired and the client does not have a refresh token. Disconnect and reconnect the server. If you’re using an API token, it may have been rotated or revoked. Check
Settings > API & MCP
.
list_workspaces returns an empty array
The token is valid but not scoped to any workspace. For OAuth, remove the Conduit connector in your client and reconnect, making sure to grant at least one workspace during consent. For API tokens, confirm the token is attached to the right workspace.
Write tool returns 403
API tokens default to read-only. Create a new token with read/write access, or use an OAuth client where you consented to the
mcp:write
scope.
Client cannot discover the OAuth server
Some clients do not support Dynamic Client Registration or do not follow the
WWW-Authenticate
resource metadata pointer. In that case, use an API token instead, or point the client directly at the authorization server URLs in the
Authentication
section.
No tools showing up after connecting
The connection succeeded but the client hasn’t refreshed its tool list. Disconnect and reconnect, or restart the client. In Claude Code, run
/mcp
to force a reconnect.
​

Getting Started
Conduit API
Programmatic access to your Conduit workspace data.
The Conduit API is only available on the
v3 plan
. Contact
support@conduit.ai
to enable API access for your workspace.
​
Overview
The Conduit API gives you programmatic access to contacts, conversations, tickets, calls, escalations, custom attributes, knowledge base, and workspace metadata. Read and write endpoints are available depending on your token’s access level. All endpoints are REST-based and return JSON.
Base URL
https://api.conduit.ai/v1
​
Authentication
All requests require a
Bearer token
in the
Authorization
header. Generate API tokens from
Settings > API & MCP
. The setting is personal, so tokens can grant access to one or more workspaces where you are an admin.
curl
https://api.conduit.ai/v1/workspaces
\
-H
"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"
Tokens are scoped to one or more workspaces. Use the
List Workspaces
endpoint to discover which workspaces your token can access.
​
Pagination
List endpoints return paginated results. Use
limit
(1-100, default 20) and
cursor
to page through results.
{
"data"
: [
...
],
"next_cursor"
:
"page-token"
,
"has_more"
:
true
}
Pass
next_cursor
as the
cursor
query parameter in your next request to fetch the next page. When
has_more
is
false
, you’ve reached the end.
​
Polling for new activity
Cursors page through a result set once. Keeping an external system in sync needs the opposite: only what has changed since you last looked. Two timestamp filters cover that.
1
Find threads that moved
Call
List Conversations
with
updated_after
set to the highest
updated_at
you have already stored.
GET /v1/conversations?workspace_id=WS&updated_after=2026-04-03T03:15:04.000Z
2
Fetch only the new messages in each thread
For each conversation returned, call
List Conversation Messages
with
created_after
set to the highest
created_at
you have stored for that thread. This replaces re-paging the whole transcript.
GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages?created_after=2026-04-03T03:15:04.000Z
Both filters are inclusive (at or after), and
created_at
is truncated to the millisecond, so the message on the boundary is normally returned again. Deduplicate on the message
id
rather than assuming every result is new.
created_after
filters on
created_at
(when Conduit recorded the message), not
sent_at
(when the channel says it was sent). Those differ for messages imported from a connected channel, and only
created_at
moves forward as Conduit observes messages, so it is the safe watermark. Using
sent_at
as your cursor will eventually skip a backdated import.
​
Telling AI replies from operator replies
Every message carries
is_sent_by_autopilot
. It is
true
only when Conduit’s AI agent generated and sent the message, and
false
for operator replies, workflow sends, and messages ingested from a connected channel’s own UI.
Use the flag directly. Do not infer automation from
sender.user_id
: AI sends usually leave it
null
, but so do host replies typed in an OTA’s own UI and messages sent by workflows, and a small number of AI sends do carry a user id.
​
Rate Limits
By default, API requests are limited to
120 requests per minute per workspace
. If you exceed the limit, the API returns
429 Too Many Requests
with a
Retry-After
header indicating when you can retry. Some workspaces may have higher limits based on plan or entitlement.
See
Rate Limits
for details.
​
Errors
All errors return a JSON object with an
error
field:
{
"error"
:
"Invalid workspace id"
}
Status
Meaning
400
Invalid request parameters
401
Missing or invalid API token
403
Token does not have access to the requested workspace
404
Resource not found
429
Rate limit exceeded

ABOUT:
Canbnb is a property management company based in Canberra, Australia, specializing in Airbnb and short-term accommodation management.
FOUNDED:
2017
USING CONDUIT SINCE:
March 2024
“Everything is right where we need it. We’re not scrambling anymore. We’re in control.”
Jo-Anne Quiros
Process and Communication Manager, Canbnb
In the early days, Jo’s morning routine was simple. Running a lean operation at Canbnb meant she handled all guest communications herself, responding to emails and messages while juggling last-minute bookings. Two freelance cleaners managed turnovers, and when things got busy, even the owner pitched in to clean properties.
It wasn’t perfect, but it worked.
Then, growth hit.
From 7 properties to 170, the pace was relentless. What had once been a manageable workflow quickly turned into a daily scramble to keep up. Guest messages overflowed, on-site teams struggled to stay aligned with the growing virtual support staff, and small inefficiencies began compounding into operational bottlenecks.
The Challenge
One morning, Jo logged in to find 630 unread messages—some from guests, some from cleaners, and a few urgent ones from owners. By the time she triaged the inbox, a check-in issue had already escalated into a full refund request. “We were moving too slow,” she recalled. “And at that scale, slow is expensive.”
Logging into multiple platforms, cross-referencing guest requests with cleaner schedules, answering urgent owner inquiries, all while making sure nothing slipped through the cracks, Jo’s morning routine was no longer no longer sustainable.
The stress of managing scale without the right infrastructure was mounting. Canbnb needed a system that could keep up with their growth—
without breaking their operations.
“We couldn’t run things the same way anymore,” Jo recalls. “The volume of messages and tasks was overwhelming, and the disconnect between virtual and on-site teams was creating inefficiencies we couldn’t ignore.”
Their operational challenges boiled down to three key problems:
Virtual vs. On-Site Coordination
– Remote support staff and on-the-ground teams needed to work in sync, but managing that balance at scale became increasingly difficult.
Response Time and Guest Experience
– With more properties came more inquiries. Slow response times meant unhappy guests, and scattered systems made it harder to track urgent issues.
Onboarding Complexity
– Property management software is notoriously difficult to implement at scale. With 170+ properties, switching systems felt like a high-risk, high-friction move.
Jo and Dan, the company’s leadership team, knew they needed a better solution—but they weren’t convinced AI was the answer.
The Skepticism
The buzz around AI in hospitality was everywhere, but Jo remained skeptical.
“I’m in operations every day. I see the gaps in these systems. AI sounded promising, but I wasn’t convinced it could really fit into our workflow.”
Dan, however, saw the bigger picture. As Canbnb pushed toward their next growth milestone, he knew they needed a platform that could do more than just streamline messaging. It had to be their central system—the foundation for everything from guest interactions to team coordination.
Their biggest hesitation? Onboarding. Property management systems are notoriously difficult to migrate, and the last thing they wanted was a drawn-out, complicated transition.
But when they set up Conduit, their doubts quickly disappeared.
The Shift
“Honestly, setting up Conduit was one of the easiest things I’ve ever done,” Jo admits. "Compared to other property management platforms, which often require weeks (or even months) to fully integrate, HostAI was up and running in a fraction of the time.”
More than just ease of use, it was that it fit into their existing operations:
A structured inbox
made it easier to monitor guest inquiries and escalate urgent issues before they became problems.
Multi-Channel Integration
– Conduit connected seamlessly with Hostaway, WhatsApp, Email, SMS, and a Chat Widget, consolidating all interactions into a single interface.
Dedicated Inboxes
– Canbnb structured their team’s workflow with separate Guest, Owner, and Vendor inboxes, ensuring the right teams handled the right conversations.
AI as the voice & tone guide
– Instead of training each new hire manually, Conduit enforced brand-aligned responses and company policies automatically.
The Transformation
Once onboarded, Jo saw a shift in her team’s mindset.
“We’re no longer just answering messages—we’re editing and guiding our AI assistant. The cognitive load has dropped, and each guest services rep is 10x more impactful.”
More importantly:
Automating at Scale
– Conduit now helps Canbnb send roughly
1,500 messages per week
, with
60% handled by AI
.
Operations became streamlined
– No more scattered attention across platforms. Remote agents could see exactly what on-site teams needed in real time.
Guest interactions improved
– AI-assisted replies ensured that every guest received timely, accurate responses, even during peak hours.
Company policies were reinforced
– AI suggestions kept human agents aligned with company standards, reducing errors and inconsistencies.
Better visibility into guest issues
– Conduit's built-in reporting helped them track
the most common guest concerns
, allowing them to address root causes proactively.
One of the biggest wins? The ability to track and act on guest feedback more effectively. Conduit's review dashboard gave them a real-time pulse on guest satisfaction, allowing them to marry guest reviews with cleaner performance and reservation data.
Conduit didn’t just improve efficiency—it
became the connective tissue
between their virtual and on-site teams.
The Outcome
Today, Canbnb isn’t just using Conduit—they’re building their future on it.
“We see Conduit as our central platform,” Dan says. "As we push past 200 properties, it’s not just about keeping up—it’s about scaling the right way, without losing control of our operations.”
With AI reducing friction, streamlining communication, and reinforcing company standards, Canbnb is moving toward its next phase of growth with clarity, not chaos.
And as for Jo? The morning routine looks a little different now.
“It’s just…easier,” she says. “Everything is right where we need it. We’re not scrambling anymore. We’re in control.”

Connect PMS
Connect PMS
Connect your property management system to Conduit to sync booking data, create contacts, and power AI responses.
​
Overview
Conduit operates fully horizontally across industries. For hospitality and property management teams, connecting your Property Management System brings property and booking data into the platform. The system automatically creates contacts from reservations and facilitates communication. Conduit integrates with over 15 different PMS systems to populate listing information.
​
Setup Steps
The initial configuration process involves four main steps:
Airbnb can be the workspace’s primary PMS or an additional messaging
connection. To use it as your PMS, select Airbnb from
Add PMS
or choose
Use Airbnb as your PMS
under
Settings > Connections > Airbnb
. See
Connect Airbnb
for both connection types.
Navigate to
Settings > Connections > PMS
If PMS isn’t visible, create a new workspace and select either
Short Term
Rental
or
Long Term Rental
under Advanced settings
Select your business’s PMS provider
Complete the provider’s authentication steps. Airbnb uses an authorization
window instead of an account ID and API key.
Your listings and PMS-backed content will appear in
Build > Knowledge
after sync completes.
​
Schedule PMS Knowledge Sync
After importing listings, turn on auto-sync to keep their PMS-backed Knowledge
current:
Open
Knowledge
from the main sidebar.
Click
Sources
at the bottom of the Knowledge sidebar.
Open your PMS source.
Open the three-dot menu, choose
Set auto-sync
, then select
Daily
,
Weekly
,
Every 2 weeks
, or
Monthly
.
The schedule applies to the whole PMS integration. It refreshes Knowledge for
listings already imported into Conduit. To find and import a property added to
your PMS later, use
Check for new listings
from the same PMS source menu.
Choosing a schedule does not run a sync immediately. Use
Sync knowledge
for
an immediate refresh, and open
Sync history
to review past and upcoming
syncs. See
Auto-sync Knowledge Sources
for screenshots,
status meanings, paused-sync recovery, and how to turn auto-sync off.
​
Connection Rules
Conduit prevents connection combinations that could create duplicate guest
conversations.
You can connect multiple PMS accounts when they use the same messaging
setup. PMS providers that deliver guest messages cannot share a workspace
with providers that only supply property and reservation data.
When you choose another PMS, incompatible providers are disabled. Use a
separate workspace if you need both types.
If Airbnb is your primary property management connection, you cannot connect
another PMS.
You can connect Airbnb directly alongside a PMS. If the PMS handles guest
messages, those messages continue through the PMS. If it does not, Conduit
can receive Airbnb messages directly and match them to PMS reservations. See
Connect Airbnb
for setup instructions.
If your workspace already has both PMS types, you can reconnect an existing
account to refresh its credentials, but you cannot add another PMS until the
conflict is resolved.
​
Messaging Support by PMS
Conduit classifies each PMS connection by whether it sends guest messages to
Conduit. This describes the Conduit integration, not every messaging feature the
PMS vendor may offer.
“Non-messaging” does not mean that guest messaging is unsupported in Conduit.
It means messaging is not supported natively through that PMS connection.
Conduit supports messaging for those PMS providers through auxiliary channel
connections, such as direct Airbnb and Expedia connections.
Connection type
PMS providers
How guest messages reach Conduit
Messaging
Beds24, Guesty, Hospitable, Hostaway, Hostfully, Hostify, Lodgify, OwnerRez, PassTheKeys, Resly, Smily
The PMS sends guest messages to Conduit. Keep OTA messaging routed through the PMS. Connecting the same OTA directly can create duplicate conversations.
Non-messaging
Apaleo, CiiRUS, Cloudbeds, Escapia, Homhero, Kross Booking, Mews, Opera Cloud, RMS, Streamline, Track
The PMS supplies property and reservation data but does not send guest messages to Conduit natively. Messaging is supported through auxiliary connections, so connect each OTA messaging channel directly to Conduit.
For example, Cloudbeds syncs Expedia reservations but does not send Expedia
messages to Conduit. To receive those messages in the Conduit inbox, contact
Conduit support to connect the Expedia properties directly. Expedia messaging
uses a shared connection managed by Conduit, so there are no workspace
credentials to enter.
Connecting Expedia messaging to Conduit does not disconnect Expedia from
Cloudbeds. Cloudbeds continues to manage inventory, rates, availability, and
reservation sync. Only Expedia guest messaging is routed directly to Conduit.
Do not keep messaging enabled through both Cloudbeds and Conduit, because the
same conversation could arrive twice.
Airbnb is handled separately from these PMS groups. Follow
Connect
Airbnb
to use Airbnb as your PMS, manage
the primary account, or add direct Airbnb messaging accounts.
​
Opera Cloud Connection Instructions
Oracle OPERA Cloud connects through the Oracle Hospitality Integration Platform
(OHIP) and needs five values from the OHIP Developer Portal rather than a single
API key. It has its own page:
Connect Opera Cloud
.
​
Lodgify Connection Instructions
Lodgify connects with a single
API key
. There’s no OAuth redirect and no
account ID, paste the key, Conduit pulls in your properties, and you pick which
listings to import.
​
Part 1: Get your Lodgify API key
Log in to
Lodgify
and open the
Menu
in the top right, then click
Settings
.
Select
Public API
in the settings menu.
Click the copy button next to your API key. That key is your access token, it has both read and write permissions. Keep it private.
If the Public API page doesn’t show a key, your plan may not include API
access yet. Request access from that page or contact Lodgify support.
​
Part 2: Connect Lodgify in Conduit
1
Open the PMS connection screen
In Conduit, go to
Settings > Connections > PMS
and click
Connect PMS
.
If PMS isn’t visible, your workspace needs to be a
Short Term Rental
or
Hotel
type. Set the industry under the workspace’s company settings, or
create a new workspace of that type.
2
Pick Lodgify from the provider list
Search for
Lodgify
and click it.
3
Paste your API key and connect
Paste the API key you copied from Lodgify into the
API Key
field and click
Connect
.
4
Import your listings
Conduit fetches your Lodgify properties and shows how many it found. Click
Import
to bring them in (or
Skip
to connect without importing yet).
The import runs in the background and can take a few minutes.
Once the sync finishes, your listings and PMS-backed content appear under
Build > Knowledge
, and new reservations start creating contacts
automatically.
​
Beds24 Connection Instructions
​
Part 1: Authentication
Open
Settings > Connections > PMS
in Conduit and click the Beds24 logo to reach the authentication screen
Select “Select all” on all three checkboxes, then click “Generate Invite Code”
Copy the invite code and paste it back on the authentication screen
Click “Connect” and wait for the success confirmation message
​
Part 2: Messaging Setup
In Conduit, open your completed Beds24 connection and copy the
Webhook URL
field
Open the Beds24 app and navigate to Settings > Properties > Access
In the Booking Webhooks section, select “2 - with personal data” as the webhook version
Paste the Conduit Webhook URL into the URL field
Leave the Custom Header empty and click “Save”
Repeat this process for each property in your Beds24 account

ABOUT:
We are reimagining the idea of 'home' from something fixed to something flexible and simplifying the rental process for both landlords and tenants as we go.
FOUNDED:

USING CONDUIT SINCE:
December 2023
“Within our niche of property management, we wanted to tackle as many goals as possible...the only thing we wouldn’t bother to do is what you guys do.”
Michael Buggy
CEO, The Flex
Two years ago, Flex Living was like many fast-growing operators, juggling a stack of tools, rising support volume, and increasingly fragmented data. Today, they’re building toward a future with just two systems: one for operations, one for AI.
Here’s how a modern rental platform became a full-stack AI company, and why Conduit is one of only two platforms they still need.
The Challenge
When Flex Living launched, it was lean, fast, and human-powered. But as the company scaled across cities like London, San Francisco, and Dubai, that model broke down.
“We were using 17 different SaaS platforms at one point,” said Michael Buggy, CEO. “The cost adds up, and it makes everything really inefficient because the platforms don’t speak to each other.”
Fragmentation is both costly and limiting. Different tools created data silos. Tasks couldn’t be automated. Support agents had to bounce between inboxes, project management tools, and CRMs just to resolve basic issues. Scaling the business meant scaling headcount.
And none of it felt sustainable.
The tipping point came when Flex Living decided to build its own property management system from scratch. They were replacing 17 disconnected SaaS tools with a unified platform tailored to their workflow. But there was one category they deliberately left out: communication.
“Within our niche of property management, we wanted to tackle as many goals as possible,” Michael explained. “The only thing we wouldn’t bother to do is what you guys do conversational AI.”
Building high-quality AI communication, from inbox to escalation logic, requires a different kind of infrastructure and a level of precision they knew would be hard to replicate in-house. Rather than dilute their focus, they chose to partner with a team already years ahead in that domain. That’s when they turned to Conduit.
The Solution
Flex Living partnered with Conduit to overhaul how they handled guest communication. This meant everything from automating frontline messaging to improving visibility across conversations. Conduit’s AI agents connected directly to their property data, resolving common issues autonomously and escalating when needed.
“70% automation of customer service is very realistic,” Michael said. “It’s achievable based on where we’re at today, not even based on where we’re going to be in a year’s time.”
At first, Michael hesitated to switch on the AI. He was worried it would get things wrong or confuse guests. But the turning point came when he understood how Conduit was designed.
If the information wasn’t there, the AI wouldn’t reply. If it was there, it would. That failure of understanding created a sense of fear to switch the AI on. Had I known that it wasn't going to do things that I had not told it to do, I would have felt much more comfortable switching it on sooner.
Flex Living’s rollout wasn’t frictionless. One early mistake was assigning the onboarding to someone without the technical context needed to structure the knowledge base. In retrospect, Michael said it should’ve been founder-led, or supported by a tool that made setup simple.
Despite the initial bumps, the team quickly aligned. Agents weren’t being replaced. They were being refocused.
“I think that hesitation sort of disappeared when they realized that what Conduit was doing was serving the customers and then enabling them to follow up where the real problems were. So it was giving them more time to solve real problems and less time spent on doing stuff that didn't need to be solved because the AI could easily do it.”
The Impact
Flex Living moved from reactive support to proactive operations. Instead of dealing with fragmented messages and manual escalation, the team gained real-time visibility into what guests needed and how the business was performing.
Favorite features include:
Call summaries that condense 30-minute conversations into 10 bullet points
Conversation tagging to quickly identify issues like cleaning or maintenance
A unified inbox with both phone and messaging support
Key Results:
70%+ automation of customer support volume
Significant reduction in manual triage and agent overhead
Streamlined escalation and task management for ops teams
And unlike legacy tools, Conduit was evolving rapidly.
“On day one, Conduit was a Lamborghini,” Michael said. “Comparing for example Front to Zendesk to Trengo and so on, it was already clear on day one that you guys were light years ahead of them Trengo and Front. And I remember the first time we spoke to you guys, we instantly understood that you had the culture of a company that was going to succeed.” That speed and clarity of vision sealed the deal.
“And when it comes to AI, I don't think any of them have even come close to building something that works well. I mean, I mean they're still basically like flow bots.”
Looking Ahead
The next chapter is even more ambitious. Flex Living is nearly done building its own PMS platform to replace tools like Hostaway and Monday.com. In four months, they expect to run on just two systems: their internal ops hub and Conduit.
The goal? A world with zero system fragmentation, where 90% of tasks are automated and AI agents orchestrate the flow of work.
We’re building the ultimate product. Something that handles 80–90% of customer communication, ties into tasks, and makes it easy to know which customers need attention.
With the communication layer solved, the team can now focus on what comes next: scaling globally, shipping faster, and pushing the limits of AI-native operations.
As Michael put it: “We’re just getting started.”
